features.name: What Frame Job needs
features.summary: Frame Job runs on an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 26 or later.

features.name: Download and install
features.summary: The newest signed and notarized build is a DMG on the project's GitHub Releases page; drag Frame Job to Applications.

features.name: What a first launch asks
features.summary: Frame Job asks for no account, key or system permission at first launch, and with nothing to open it shows the Welcome window.

features.name: Your first edit, start to finish
features.summary: Open a movie, cut a section out, add a title and export an H.264 file.

features.name: The editor window
features.summary: Each project opens in one window: title bar, toolbar, preview and inspector side by side, the timeline bar and the timeline.

features.name: Title bar
features.summary: The title bar shows the project's name; its subtitle gives the canvas size, frame rate and "edited" while changes are unsaved.

features.name: Toolbar
features.summary: A strip under the title bar holds the transport, the timecode, the preview zoom, Safe and Export….

features.name: Timeline bar
features.summary: A bar above the timeline names the selection and holds the clip tools, Snap, the level meter, zoom and track size.

features.name: Pane dividers and remembered sizes
features.summary: Drag the dividers to size the inspector and the timeline; new windows open at the sizes you chose.
features.where: The dividers left of the inspector and above the timeline

features.name: Minimize and Zoom
features.summary: The standard window commands: Minimize sends the window to the Dock and Zoom makes it larger or smaller.

features.name: Project
features.summary: A project is one .framejob package: a single file in the Finder that holds the edit and its caches.

features.name: Media and clips
features.summary: Media is a file the project knows about; a clip is one placement of something on the timeline.

features.name: Tracks and stacking
features.summary: There is one kind of track, it holds any clip, and tracks stack back to front.

features.name: The canvas
features.summary: The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is drawn into, at the project's size and frame rate.

features.name: Nests
features.summary: A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group.

features.name: The five inspector tabs
features.summary: The inspector has five tabs: Clip, Media, Document, Transcript and Assistant.
features.where: Inspector tab strip, editor window middle right

features.name: The Clip tab's pinned block
features.summary: Above its sections the Clip tab pins the selection header, the action lane and the sub-tabs.

features.name: Sub-tabs follow the selection
features.summary: Text, Shape, Graphic, Picture, Color, Sound and Clip sub-tabs split the Clip tab, showing only what the selection can use.

features.name: Selection follows to the Clip tab
features.summary: Clicking a clip moves the inspector to the Clip tab, unless you're on Transcript, which stays and scrolls to that clip's first word.
features.where: Click a clip on the timeline or the canvas

features.name: Folding sections and their summaries
features.summary: Click a section's header to fold it; a folded header keeps a one-line summary of what is inside, and the fold is remembered.

features.name: Hide or show the inspector
features.summary: View ▸ Hide Inspector collapses the inspector so the preview takes its space; the item then reads Show Inspector.

features.name: Typing a value
features.summary: A number field applies your value on Return, Tab or a click elsewhere, throws it away on Esc, and holds it to the field's range.

features.name: Quick-pick chevrons
features.summary: A field with common values has a chevron at its right that opens a menu of them.
features.where: The chevron at the right of a value field

features.name: Sliders
features.summary: A click on a slider jumps to that value and a drag follows the pointer, as one undo step.
features.where: Click or drag an inspector slider

features.name: Colour swatches and the colour panel
features.summary: Clicking a colour swatch opens the macOS colour panel, with opacity, and the value follows it live.

features.name: Edit several clips at once
features.summary: With several clips selected, a row whose values differ shows a mixed badge, and an edit gives every clip it applies to the same value.

features.name: Section Reset
features.summary: A Reset button appears on a section's header only while the section differs from its default, and puts the whole section back.

features.name: Right-click menu on a row
features.summary: Right-click an inspector row to reset it to its default, take it out of an action, or go to another action that changes it.
features.where: Right-click a row in the inspector

features.name: Single-letter editor keys
features.summary: Space, the letter keys, comma, period and the arrow keys act on the editor window whenever you are not typing and no sheet is open.

features.name: ⌘ shortcuts follow their menu item
features.summary: Every ⌘ shortcut is a menu shortcut, and does nothing while its item is greyed out.

features.name: Start and finish typing
features.summary: A field takes the keys only when you click in it or choose a command that opens one for typing, and hands them back when you finish.

features.name: Delete keys in a text field
features.summary: Delete, ⌘⌫, ⌘↓ and ⌘↑ act on the timeline, but in a text field they keep their usual text meaning.

features.name: Multi-line field keys
features.summary: In a multi-line field, Return applies the text and Return with ⇧, ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ starts a new line.
features.where: Text tab ▸ Content, the Assistant's message field

features.name: Keys in a sheet
features.summary: In a sheet, Return presses the main button and Esc presses Cancel.

features.name: What Esc leaves
features.summary: Esc backs out of whatever is under way, such as a canvas drag, crop mode, region mode, an eyedropper or a selected curve point.

features.name: Undo and Redo
features.summary: Edit ▸ Undo and Edit ▸ Redo walk back and forward one step at a time.

features.name: What one step is
features.summary: A menu command or key is one step however many clips it changes, and a gesture is one step from mouse-down to mouse-up.

features.name: Named steps
features.summary: The Edit menu names the step it will take back, for example Undo Move Clips.

features.name: What makes no step
features.summary: Anything that does not change the project makes no undo step.

features.name: The Refused line in the inspector
features.summary: When a rule won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and shows a "Refused:" line at the foot of the inspector saying why.

features.name: A beep with no message
features.summary: An edit that would change nothing beeps but shows no message, because no rule was broken.

features.name: An error alert
features.summary: A request Frame Job can't use at all, such as a value outside its allowed range, shows an error alert naming the value.

features.name: Your own keys, your own bill
features.summary: There is no Frame Job account or relay: the cloud features run on your own API keys, and the provider bills you directly.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant or Transcription

features.name: What needs a key
features.summary: Anything that sends your words or audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key; everything that runs on your Mac needs none.

features.name: Greyed commands and their tooltips
features.summary: A command that needs a key you have not set is greyed rather than hidden, and says which key and where to set it.

features.name: Saving a key takes effect at once
features.summary: Saving or removing a key updates open sheets and menu items immediately, with nothing to reopen or relaunch.

features.name: What stays on this Mac
features.summary: Editing, analysis, on-device transcription, recording and export stay on this Mac; only things you start or can see reach the network.

features.name: Which copy updates itself
features.summary: The copy downloaded from the project's GitHub Releases page updates itself with Sparkle; a copy built from source has no updater.

features.name: Check for Updates…
features.summary: Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates… checks now for a newer Frame Job and offers to install it.

features.name: Automatic checks
features.summary: The second time you open Frame Job it asks whether to check automatically; if you agree it checks about once a day while open.
features.where: The prompt the second time you open Frame Job

features.name: Turning automatic checks off
features.summary: There is no Settings control for automatic checks, but a Terminal command turns them off.

features.name: Signed updates
features.summary: Every update is signed, and Frame Job won't install one whose signature doesn't match the key built into the app.

features.name: Open a movie as a project
features.summary: Opening a movie makes an untitled project at its size and frame rate, with the movie as the first clip on Track 1.

features.name: The canvas takes the movie's display size
features.summary: A project built from a movie uses the size the movie displays at, so a portrait phone clip opens as 1080 × 1920 and not sideways.

features.name: The exact frame rate from the file
features.summary: A project opened from a movie keeps the file's exact rate, so 29.97 and 23.976 are never rounded to 30 or 24.

features.name: Open a sound file as a project
features.summary: Opening a sound file makes an untitled 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project with that sound as its first clip.

features.name: Open a picture as a project
features.summary: Opening a PNG, JPEG or HEIC makes an untitled project at the picture's pixel size with the picture as a 5-second clip.

features.name: New Project
features.summary: File ▸ New Project opens a blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project at once, with no dialog, in a window titled "Untitled Project".

features.name: A project from a file starts unsaved
features.summary: A project made from an opened file exists only in its window until you save it, so closing it asks whether to save.

features.name: The first Save goes beside the source
features.summary: The first Save of a project made from a file offers to put the package next to the source file, under the source's name.

features.name: The Welcome window
features.summary: With nothing open, a start window offers the ways in and your recent projects.
features.where: Shown when Frame Job starts with nothing to open

features.name: Open Video… on the Welcome window
features.summary: Shows the same open panel as File ▸ Open…, so it also opens sound files, pictures and saved projects.

features.name: New Project on the Welcome window
features.summary: Starts a blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project.

features.name: New Recording… on the Welcome window
features.summary: Opens the recorder panel, with no project needed.

features.name: The Recent list
features.summary: Lists up to five recently opened projects by name, most recent first; one click reopens one.

features.name: The file types line
features.summary: The foot of the window names the common types it opens: MOV · MP4 · M4V · M4A · MP3 · WAV · AIFF · PNG · JPEG · HEIC.

features.name: Drop files on the Welcome window
features.summary: A project or media file dropped anywhere on the Welcome window opens, each as its own document.
features.where: Drag files from the Finder onto the Welcome window

features.name: Open a project
features.summary: Opening a .framejob package opens that project, and a double-click on a package always opens it in Frame Job.

features.name: Open Recent
features.summary: File ▸ Open Recent lists recently opened projects, with Clear Menu to empty the list.

features.name: A project already open comes forward
features.summary: Opening a saved project that's already open brings its window forward instead of opening a second copy.

features.name: Drop files to open them
features.summary: Files dropped on a project window outside the Media tab, on the Welcome window or on the Dock icon each open as a document of their own.
features.where: Drag from the Finder onto a project window, outside the Media tab

features.name: Older projects open
features.summary: A project saved by any earlier version of Frame Job opens, and the next save writes it in the current format.

features.name: Projects from a newer Frame Job
features.summary: A project saved by a newer Frame Job won't open, and the message gives both versions and asks you to update.

features.name: Damaged projects
features.summary: A damaged or out-of-range project fails to open with a message naming the problem, and the package is not rewritten.

features.name: Missing media still opens
features.summary: A project whose files have moved or gone still opens, with slates in their place and a sheet to relink them.

features.name: New Project from Range
features.summary: Opens a new project holding exactly the timeline's In–Out range, moved to start at 0, and leaves the source project unchanged.

features.name: Clips cut at the range's edges
features.summary: A clip across the range's In or Out is cut there as Split cuts it; markers inside are kept and media no kept clip plays is left out.

features.name: The new project's name and undo
features.summary: The new project opens untitled with unsaved changes, named like "Interview (range)", with no undo step back to the whole timeline.

features.name: What's already measured comes along
features.summary: Filmstrips, waveforms, on-device transcripts, analyses and reversed renders of each kept file come along, so nothing is measured again.

features.name: Cloud transcripts in a range project
features.summary: A cloud transcript goes to the range project only once AssemblyAI has been told to delete its copy.

features.name: Graphics come along
features.summary: The graphics the kept clips draw come along, with every font and picture of the project's graphics.

features.name: When a range can't be kept
features.summary: If the range can't be kept, the command beeps and shows why at the foot of the inspector, and no project opens.

features.name: Save
features.summary: Writes the project to its package; an untitled project asks for a name and a place first.

features.name: Save As and Duplicate
features.summary: Duplicate opens a copy as a new untitled project; Save As…, shown while you hold ⌥, writes to a new package and carries on in it.

features.name: Autosave
features.summary: Once saved, a project autosaves in place as you work, the macOS way.

features.name: Crash-safe package writes
features.summary: The package is written beside the old one and swapped in, so a crash part-way through a save cannot leave half a package.

features.name: Revert To and browsing versions
features.summary: Goes back to the last saved version, or browses earlier versions of the package.

features.name: Rename
features.summary: The standard macOS command renames the project's package, from the File menu or the window's title.

features.name: Move To
features.summary: The standard macOS command moves the project's package to another folder, from the File menu or the window's title.

features.name: Share
features.summary: Opens the macOS Share menu for the project.

features.name: Close
features.summary: Closes the window: a saved project writes its changes without asking, and an untitled project with changes asks whether to save.

features.name: A project saves only as a package
features.summary: A project only ever saves as a .framejob package; a movie or still is a separate Export step.

features.name: The Document tab
features.summary: Holds what belongs to the whole project, in five sections: its size, frame rate, background and markers.

features.name: Document summary rows
features.summary: Read-only rows show Resolution, Frame rate, Duration, Tracks, Background and Colour.

features.name: Canvas Preset
features.summary: Picks a canvas size from a popup of common shapes.

features.name: Source Size
features.summary: Sets the canvas to the size of the first media file that has a picture size, as long as both sides are even.
features.where: Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Preset ▸ Source Size

features.name: Custom Width and Height
features.summary: You type the canvas size in pixels: even numbers from 16 to 16,384.
features.where: Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Width and Height

features.name: Resize clips proportionally
features.summary: When on, clips follow a canvas size change so the layout looks the same; when off, they keep their scale and distance from the centre.
features.where: Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Resize clips proportionally

features.name: Project frame rate
features.summary: Picks the project's rate: 24, 23.976, 25, 30, 29.97, 50 or 60 fps, or Match First Clip. Custom shows a rate it doesn't list.

features.name: Match First Clip
features.summary: Takes the rate of the earliest clip on the timeline whose file has video.
features.where: Document tab ▸ Frame Rate ▸ Rate ▸ Match First Clip

features.name: Rates the popup does not list
features.summary: A project can run at a rate the popup doesn't list. The popup then shows Custom, and the Frame rate row shows the real rate.

features.name: What a rate change does to the timeline
features.summary: Changing the rate moves every clip start, length, action and marker onto the new frame grid.

features.name: Duration row
features.summary: A read-only row shows the timeline's length.

features.name: Canvas background colour
features.summary: Sets the colour behind every layer.

features.name: A transparent background
features.summary: Lowering the background's opacity makes it transparent, and the section adds a note about the export formats that keep it.

features.name: Timecode
features.summary: Shows times as Frames (HH:MM:SS:FF) or Milliseconds (HH:MM:SS.mmm) everywhere in the project.

features.name: Fit new clips to canvas
features.summary: When on, a new clip bigger than the canvas starts scaled down to fit; when off, it starts at 100 % and runs past the edges.
features.where: Document tab ▸ Appearance ▸ Fit new clips to canvas

features.name: Reset Appearance
features.summary: Reset on the section header puts Background, Timecode and Fit new clips back to their defaults: opaque black, Frames and on.

features.name: Add Media
features.summary: Adds one or more files to the Media tab as one undo step, without putting them on the timeline.

features.name: Drop files on the Media tab
features.summary: Dragging files from the Finder onto the Media tab adds them to this project, including types the panels don't list.
features.where: Drag from the Finder onto the Media tab

features.name: Media is referenced, not copied
features.summary: A project remembers each file's path and a Finder bookmark and reads it from there, so the package stays small.

features.name: What the open panels list
features.summary: The Add Media… and Open panels list movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG, HEIC and, in Add Media… only, .cube.

features.name: Add a media entry from a description
features.summary: An agent can add a media entry from a description it supplies, without reading the file, to replay a project's own JSON.

features.name: Codecs this Mac can't decode
features.summary: A video in a codec this Mac can't decode is left out at import, and an alert names the codec.

features.name: When a file won't import
features.summary: A file that can't be read, holds no video or sound, or takes over 30 seconds to check shows an alert saying so.

features.name: WebM and Matroska import
features.summary: A .webm or .mkv is copied unchanged into a QuickTime movie the first time it comes in, with no re-encoding, and the original stays put.

features.name: The Copying Movie window
features.summary: A copy that takes more than a second shows a small progress window with Cancel.

features.name: The free-space check
features.summary: Before copying, Frame Job checks the disk has room; if it doesn't, nothing is copied and an alert says what's needed.

features.name: The Rewrapped folder
features.summary: Copies live in ~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/, shared by all projects. Frame Job doesn't clear it, but you can.

features.name: A copied file keeps its name
features.summary: The media keeps the original's name, and its Media tab tooltip says where the copy lives.

features.name: Streams the copy can't carry
features.summary: A file with a stream the copy can't carry isn't added, and an alert names the stream; with ffmpeg installed, Frame Job offers to help.

features.name: Stated colour is kept
features.summary: The copy keeps the colour the file states: HLG, HDR10 (PQ), or a BT.709, BT.601 or BT.2020 SDR picture.

features.name: A missing copy is remade
features.summary: If a copy is deleted or moved to the Trash, the project makes it again from the original the next time it opens.

features.name: Optional ffmpeg conversion
features.summary: With your own ffmpeg, a file macOS can't open can still come in, each stream copied when it can be and re-encoded when it can't.
features.where: Alert on import ▸ Repackage or Convert

features.name: Finding ffmpeg
features.summary: Frame Job looks for ffmpeg on your PATH first, then in the usual install folders, and a Terminal setting can name a particular build.

features.name: The Repackage or Convert alert
features.summary: Before anything starts, the alert names the codecs and gives the size and the time, and offers Repackage or Convert, or Cancel.
features.where: Alert on import ▸ Repackage or Convert

features.name: Do this automatically from now on
features.summary: Keeps the answer you give: Repackage or Convert means such files convert from then on without asking, Cancel means they never do.
features.where: Alert on import ▸ Do this automatically from now on

features.name: When a conversion fails
features.summary: A conversion that fails or runs out of time shows an alert, and no partial file is left behind.

features.name: A lost conversion stays missing
features.summary: Unlike a WebM copy, a deleted conversion is not remade when the project opens, and the media stays missing until relinked.

features.name: Agent imports and ffmpeg
features.summary: An agent's import never shows the ffmpeg question: unless you chose to convert automatically, the import fails and gives the reason.

features.name: The Media tab
features.summary: The inspector's Media tab lists every file the project has imported, used or not, with a search, a sort and a filter.

features.name: The item count
features.summary: The top bar holds Add Media… and a count of the files, and of how many are showing.

features.name: Search by name
features.summary: A Search by name field narrows the list as you type, ignoring case and accents as the Finder does. Esc clears it.

features.name: Sort
features.summary: A Sort popup orders the list by Import Order, Name, Duration or Kind.

features.name: Unused only
features.summary: A checkbox shows only the files no clip uses.

features.name: A media row
features.summary: Each row shows a thumbnail, the file's name and an info line for its kind.

features.name: Audio and missing badges
features.summary: Badges on the right mark a file that has audio and, in coral, a file that cannot be found.

features.name: The row's tooltip
features.summary: Hovering a row shows how to place it, and where a copied file came from.
features.where: Hover over a Media tab row

features.name: Selecting a row
features.summary: Clicking a row selects it for Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead, Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead and the sections under the list.

features.name: The row's menu
features.summary: Right-clicking a row offers Insert at Playhead, Overwrite at Playhead, Reveal in Timeline, Reveal in Finder, Relink… and Remove.

features.name: Reveal in Timeline
features.summary: Selects every clip showing this file and scrolls to the earliest one; if the selection changes, the inspector moves to the Clip tab.
features.where: Media row menu ▸ Reveal in Timeline

features.name: Reveal in Finder
features.summary: Shows the file in the Finder.
features.where: Media row menu ▸ Reveal in Finder

features.name: Remove media
features.summary: Takes the file out of the project and never deletes it from disk; an unused file goes at once, as one undo step.

features.name: Remove media used by clips
features.summary: If clips use the file Frame Job asks first, and Remove and Delete Clips removes the file and those clips as one undo step.

features.name: The Missing media sheet
features.summary: When a project opens with files missing, a sheet lists each with its old path and a Locate… button.

features.name: Locate finds siblings by name
features.summary: Choosing a file for one entry also looks in its folder for the other missing files by name, so a moved shoot is usually found with one Locate….

features.name: Relink every located file
features.summary: Relink applies every choice as one undo step, and skipped files stay missing to relink later.

features.name: Relink one file
features.summary: Points one media entry at a file you choose, missing or not.

features.name: What a relink checks
features.summary: The new file must be readable and the same kind, and the row takes on its duration, size, frame rate, and audio, video and alpha.

features.name: What a relink keeps
features.summary: A relink keeps the file's Camera Log and HDR10 peak, and keeps or finds its cursor file and any saved speech that still fits.

features.name: Consolidate Media
features.summary: Copies every file in the media list, used or not, into the package's media/ folder and points the project at the copies.

features.name: Consolidate needs a saved project
features.summary: On an untitled project the command asks "Save this project first?", offers Save…, and carries on after the save.

features.name: The Consolidating Media sheet
features.summary: A sheet shows a bar, the file being copied and Cancel.

features.name: When Consolidate Media finishes
features.summary: When it finishes the sheet says what happened and offers Show in Finder and Close.
features.where: Consolidating Media sheet ▸ Show in Finder

features.name: Consolidating files with the same name
features.summary: Two files with one name are kept apart, two entries for one file share a copy, and files already inside are not copied again.

features.name: Consolidating with missing files
features.summary: Missing files are left alone until you relink them; with nothing to do, an alert says "Nothing to consolidate." and why.

features.name: Consolidating LUTs
features.summary: LUTs are copied like footage, used or not, and the looks and Camera Logs that use one then read the copy.

features.name: Consolidating cursor files
features.summary: A recording's cursor file is copied next to its movie and named after it, and counts as one of the files copied.

features.name: Consolidating WebM, MKV and converted files
features.summary: For a WebM, an MKV or a file converted with ffmpeg, Consolidate Media copies the movie it plays from, not the file you imported.

features.name: A moved package finds its copies
features.summary: A moved or renamed consolidated package points missing media back at same-named files in its media/ folder, with no sheet.

features.name: On-device media analysis
features.summary: Frame Job studies your files on this Mac to find shots, faces, people and sound events, with no upload, no network request and no key.
features.where: Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes, Clip ▸ Follow Subject…, Clip ▸ Remove Background, Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…, File ▸ Make Vertical Version…

features.name: Analysis on demand
features.summary: A file's picture is not analysed at import, only when something asks, and only the missing part is read.

features.name: Analysis runs in the background
features.summary: Picture analysis runs at low priority, one job at a time, and sound analysis on its own queue, so the app stays usable while it works.

features.name: The Analyzing sheet
features.summary: When a menu command needs analysis the project doesn't have yet, a sheet shows each file's progress, then closes and the command goes on.
features.where: Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes, Clip ▸ Follow Subject…, Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…, File ▸ Make Vertical Version…

features.name: Stop an analysis
features.summary: Stop on the Analyzing sheet cancels the command and makes no edit, and what was already saved stays in the project for next time.

features.name: When an analysis fails
features.summary: If an analysis cannot finish, the command stops and says which file failed and why rather than editing with half an answer.

features.name: Results kept per file
features.summary: Anything found is kept for the file in the project's cache, so a second request over the same part is ready at once.

features.name: Analysis travels with the project
features.summary: The caches live inside the .framejob package, so they go wherever it goes and carry into a project made from it.

features.name: Filmstrips, waveforms and loudness
features.summary: After an open, an import or a relink, Frame Job builds thumbnails, waveforms, loudness, sound matching and voice detection in the background.

features.name: Voice detection
features.summary: Frame Job scores every 32 ms of a file's sound for speech with the bundled Silero voice model, so commands can tell a voice from noise.

features.name: Shots
features.summary: Frame Job finds the hard cuts in a video by comparing each frame's colours with the frames before it.

features.name: Faces
features.summary: Frame Job looks for faces ten times a second, keeping each face's box, how far it's turned and tilted, and how open its mouth is.
features.where: Clip ▸ Follow Subject…, File ▸ Make Vertical Version…, Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…

features.name: People and salient regions
features.summary: Frame Job finds people's head and shoulders and the regions the eye goes to first, at the same ten samples a second.
features.where: Clip ▸ Follow Subject…, File ▸ Make Vertical Version…

features.name: Person masks
features.summary: Frame Job outlines a person in every frame a clip plays, which is what Remove Background and Text Behind Subject draw with.

features.name: Foreground masks on pictures
features.summary: On a still picture, Frame Job can mask the foreground subject, whether or not it's a person.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Background ▸ Subject ▸ Foreground

features.name: Sound events
features.summary: An agent can have Frame Job score a file's first sound track for laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech. No menu uses it.

features.name: One kind of track
features.summary: Any track holds any mix of clips: video, audio, a picture, text, a shape, a graphic, a nest or an adjustment clip.

features.name: Tracks stack back to front
features.summary: Tracks are layers: the top lane is front-most and the bottom lane is at the back.

features.name: The current track
features.summary: Commands that need one track use the track of the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected.

features.name: Default track names
features.summary: A new track is named from the track count, such as Track 3, and keeps that name when you reorder the stack.

features.name: The track header and its switches
features.summary: Each track has a header on the left with its name, the Hide Video, Mute Audio, Lock Track and Solo switches, and the Mix button.
features.where: Track header: eye, speaker, lock, headphones, sliders

features.name: New Track
features.summary: Adds an empty track at the front, as the top lane.

features.name: Make a track by dropping past the stack
features.summary: Dragging clips above the top lane or below the bottom lane creates a new track for them.
features.where: Drag a clip past the top or bottom lane

features.name: Rename a track
features.summary: Double-clicking a track header opens an in-place name field.

features.name: Reorder tracks
features.summary: Dragging a track header up or down restacks the track.

features.name: Remove Track
features.summary: Removes the current track, or the track whose context menu you opened, asking first if it still holds clips.

features.name: Remove Empty Tracks
features.summary: Removes every track that holds no clips, as one undo step.

features.name: Track menu switches
features.summary: The Track menu flips the current track's Hide Video, Mute Audio, Lock Track and Solo switches.
features.where: Track ▸ Hide Video, Mute Audio, Lock Track, Solo

features.name: The track context menu
features.summary: Right-clicking a track header or the empty part of its lane opens a menu for that track, showing its own state.
features.where: Right-click or ⌃-click a track header or the empty part of its lane

features.name: Track, marker and label edits undo one at a time
features.summary: Every switch flip, rename and reorder is one undo step, and Edit ▸ Undo names the edit it will reverse.

features.name: Hide Video
features.summary: Takes a track's picture out of the preview and the export, leaving its sound playing.

features.name: Lock Track
features.summary: Protects a track: its clips can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled with the mouse, and ripples and range deletes leave them alone.

features.name: Timeline Track Height
features.summary: Picks small, medium or large track rows for every project.

features.name: Height follows what a track holds
features.summary: A track's height also depends on what it holds, so sound-only and text tracks draw shorter than picture tracks.

features.name: The clip block
features.summary: Each clip draws as one rounded block with a thin border, so its ends are always visible.

features.name: Colour by kind
features.summary: A clip's colour and the symbol on its name strip show its kind, such as green for audio and amber for text.

features.name: The name strip
features.summary: The top strip of a clip carries its kind symbol, a link symbol if it's linked, its name, a wave for During motion and its label dot.

features.name: Filmstrip thumbnails
features.summary: Thumbnails run along the picture part of a video or image clip, under a wash of its colour.

features.name: The waveform
features.summary: A clip with sound draws it as a waveform, below the filmstrip if it has both, following speed changes and ramps.

features.name: Fade handles
features.summary: Small white squares at the top corners of the audio part of a clip set its fades when dragged inward.
features.where: Drag a fade handle on a clip

features.name: The selection ring and trim grips
features.summary: A selected clip gets a 2 pt coral ring, plus a trim grip at each end when it's wide enough and its track is unlocked.

features.name: Dimmed clips
features.summary: A clip on a hidden track, or with both its picture and sound switched off, draws dimmed.

features.name: How an adjustment clip looks
features.summary: An adjustment clip is a plain rose block with only its name strip and action lane.

features.name: A ruler that follows the zoom
features.summary: The ruler's divisions adapt to the zoom, from single frames up to one hour, and its labels use the project's timecode format.

features.name: The playhead
features.summary: The playhead is a coral line down every track with a triangle head on the ruler.

features.name: The playhead is where edits happen
features.summary: Split, trim to playhead, freeze frame, paste, insert and overwrite all work at the playhead.

features.name: Click or drag the ruler to scrub
features.summary: Clicking the ruler moves the playhead there, and dragging along it scrubs while you hear the sound under the playhead.
features.where: Click or drag on the ruler

features.name: A click in a lane leaves the playhead
features.summary: A click in a lane doesn't move the playhead, except on an action band, which moves it to the end of that action.

features.name: The timeline follows the playhead
features.summary: When the playhead nears the edge of the visible part or leaves it, the view moves so it sits about a third of the way in.

features.name: Play and pause
features.summary: Space, or the toolbar's Play and Pause button, starts and stops playback from almost anywhere in the window.

features.name: J, K and L shuttle
features.summary: L plays forward and J plays in reverse, each further press stepping ×1 to ×2 to ×4, and K pauses.

features.name: Step frames
features.summary: ← and → pause and move the playhead one frame; with ⇧ they move ten.

features.name: What happens at the end
features.summary: Playback stops at the end of the timeline and the playhead stays there. On an empty timeline, Play, J and L beep.

features.name: Look-only edits redraw in place
features.summary: A change that only alters how something looks redraws the frame without interrupting playback.

features.name: Structural edits rebuild in the background
features.summary: A move, a trim, a new clip or a change to the sound rebuilds the preview in the background, keeping your place and speed.

features.name: A failed rebuild keeps playing
features.summary: If a rebuild fails, an error shows and the previous version keeps playing.

features.name: Previous and Next Edit Point
features.summary: ↑ and ↓, or the toolbar's buttons either side of Play, jump the playhead to the previous or next edit point.
features.where: Toolbar transport: Previous Edit Point, Next Edit Point

features.name: Go to Start and Go to End
features.summary: Home and End, or the transport's buttons, pause and move the playhead to the start or end of the timeline.
features.where: Toolbar transport: Go to Start, Go to End

features.name: Type a timecode to jump
features.summary: The toolbar shows the playhead's time; click it, type a time and press Return to pause and jump there.

features.name: The duration readout
features.summary: Beside the time, the toolbar shows a slash and the duration of what the timeline shows.

features.name: Move the playhead with an agent
features.summary: With set_playhead, an agent moves the playhead and the preview. It makes no undo step and doesn't pause playback.

features.name: Loop playback
features.summary: The Loop button repeats the in/out range, or the whole timeline when there's no range.

features.name: Pinch and ⌥ or ⌘ scroll to zoom
features.summary: A trackpad pinch, or scrolling with ⌥ or ⌘ held, zooms the timeline about the pointer, keeping the time under it in place.
features.where: Pinch, or ⌥ or ⌘ and scroll, over the timeline

features.name: The zoom slider
features.summary: The Timeline Zoom slider zooms about the middle of the view, across the whole zoom range.

features.name: Zoom Out and Zoom In buttons
features.summary: The − and + buttons step the timeline zoom about the middle of the view.

features.name: Fit Timeline
features.summary: Fits the whole project across the timeline pane and scrolls to the start.

features.name: Starting zoom and zoom range
features.summary: A window opens with each second 42 points wide, not fitted to the project, and the zoom runs from hours down to single frames.

features.name: Scroll the timeline
features.summary: A plain scroll or two-finger swipe moves the timeline, with the track headers and ruler staying in place.
features.where: Scroll or two-finger swipe over the timeline

features.name: Click to select
features.summary: Clicking a clip selects it alone, unless it's part of a larger selection, which then stays selected.

features.name: ⇧-click to add or remove
features.summary: ⇧-click adds a clip to the selection, or takes out one that's already selected.

features.name: Marquee selection
features.summary: Dragging from empty timeline space draws a band that selects every clip it touches; ⇧-drag adds to the selection.
features.where: Drag from a gap in a lane, the strip under the ruler or the space below the last lane

features.name: Clear the selection
features.summary: A single click on empty timeline space clears the selection.
features.where: Click an empty lane, or above or below the lanes

features.name: Select All
features.summary: Selects every clip in the timeline being edited, on locked tracks too.

features.name: Select After Playhead
features.summary: Selects every clip whose start is at or after the playhead.

features.name: Select All on Track
features.summary: Selects every clip on the current track, or on the track whose header you ⌥-click.

features.name: The selection block
features.summary: The left end of the timeline bar names what is selected.

features.name: A selection isn't saved
features.summary: A selection is never an undo step and isn't saved, so a project always opens with nothing selected.

features.name: What a drag snaps to
features.summary: Clip moves, trims, rolls and rate stretches, marker drags and ruler scrubs catch clip edges, markers, the playhead and the range.

features.name: Turn snapping on and off
features.summary: N, the Snap box or View ▸ Snapping turn snapping on or off for the timeline and the canvas together.

features.name: Hold ⌘ to suspend snapping
features.summary: Holding ⌘ turns snapping off for the current drag, on the timeline and on the canvas.
features.where: Hold ⌘ during any drag that snaps

features.name: The snap guide line
features.summary: When a drag snaps, a thin vertical guide line across the timeline marks what it caught.

features.name: Drags land on whole frames
features.summary: A drag that doesn't snap still lands on a whole frame.

features.name: What never snaps
features.summary: Slips, action band drags and fade handles never snap, and a Media tab row dropped on a lane lands on the nearest frame.

features.name: Add a marker
features.summary: Drops a marker at the playhead.

features.name: Marker flags
features.summary: Each marker draws as a small flag with a line down the ruler, in its colour.

features.name: Move a marker
features.summary: Dragging a flag along the ruler moves the marker.

features.name: Rename a marker
features.summary: Double-click a flag to type in place, or type in its row in the Document tab.

features.name: Next and Previous Marker
features.summary: Pause playback and jump the playhead to the next or previous marker.

features.name: The Document tab's Markers list
features.summary: The Document tab lists every marker in time order, each with its time, name, Chapter, Go and Delete.

features.name: Go to a marker from its row
features.summary: A marker row's Go button moves the playhead to it.

features.name: Remove a marker
features.summary: A marker row's Delete button removes it.

features.name: Chapter markers
features.summary: Turn on Chapter in a marker's row and its flag fills, and it becomes a chapter in exported MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files.

features.name: Marker colours
features.summary: Markers are red unless an agent changes them, because the Document tab has no colour control.

features.name: Markers while a nest is open
features.summary: Markers belong to the whole timeline, so an open nest hides them from the ruler.
features.where: Timeline while a nest is open

features.name: The in/out range
features.summary: A span of the timeline, shaded across the ruler and lanes, that other commands act on.

features.name: Set In
features.summary: Sets the in point at the playhead.

features.name: Set Out
features.summary: Sets the out point at the playhead.

features.name: Clear Range
features.summary: Clears the in/out range.

features.name: Crossing points
features.summary: Setting an in point after the out point moves the out point to match, and the other way round.

features.name: The range isn't saved
features.summary: The range isn't an undo step and isn't saved, and it clears when you enter or leave a nest.

features.name: Rename a clip
features.summary: A field opens over the clip's name strip so you can name it in place.
features.where: Clip ▸ Rename…, or double-click the clip

features.name: Clear a clip's name
features.summary: Emptying the name field at the top of the Clip tab clears a clip's name, so it shows what it holds again.

features.name: Label a clip
features.summary: Applies a colour label to every selected clip, shown as a small dot on its name strip.
features.where: Clip ▸ Label ▸ Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Purple, None

features.name: Names and labels for agents
features.summary: With set_clip, an agent names or labels several clips in one step.

features.name: The preview pane
features.summary: The preview shows the frame under the playhead in the canvas's shape, letterboxed in the pane to the left of the inspector.
features.where: Editor window, top left, above the timeline

features.name: Preview tags
features.summary: Small tags in the preview's top-left corner show when the picture isn't the plain one: Ungraded, Selection or SDR Version.

features.name: Other View items for the preview
features.summary: The View menu's other preview items: Safe Areas, Show Ungraded, Show Selection, Show SDR Version, Show Subjects, Scopes, Loudness Meter.

features.name: Preview Quality
features.summary: Draws the preview at Full, Half or Quarter of the canvas size and scales it back up, so heavy projects play more smoothly.
features.where: View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full, Half, Quarter

features.name: The Preview Window
features.summary: Opens the picture in its own window with no handles or guides, for a second display.

features.name: The window remembers its place
features.summary: The window remembers where you put it and stays visible when you switch to another app.

features.name: Keys in the Preview Window
features.summary: While it has focus, the playback keys, the editor's other single-letter keys and every editor ⌘ command keep working.

features.name: What an edit acts on
features.summary: Most commands act on the selected clips, and some also use the playhead, the in and out range or the current track.

features.name: Clips never push each other
features.summary: A dragged clip never shoves its neighbours aside. Only edits made to shift time, such as Ripple Delete or Insert, move other clips.

features.name: Times land on frames
features.summary: A time you drag or type lands on a whole frame of the project's frame rate, except short audio times such as a typed fade length.

features.name: One frame minimum
features.summary: Trims and rolls always leave a clip at least one frame long.

features.name: Project size limits
features.summary: A project holds up to 4,096 clips, 64 tracks, eight levels of nesting, 1,024 markers and 1,024 media files.

features.name: Drag media onto a track
features.summary: Drag a row from the Media tab onto a track to place the whole file as a clip at the drop point, moving nothing else.
features.where: Media tab ▸ drag a row onto a track

features.name: Drop media on the canvas
features.summary: Drop a Media tab row on the preview canvas to add the file at the playhead on a new track at the front.
features.where: Media tab ▸ drag a row onto the preview canvas

features.name: New clips cover the whole file
features.summary: A new clip runs the whole file from its first frame, rounded down to whole frames. A picture lands 5 seconds long.

features.name: When a media drop doesn't land
features.summary: A drop that breaks the overlap rule beeps and adds nothing. One outside the lanes or in another project's window springs back.

features.name: Insert
features.summary: Insert places a file at a point and makes room for it by pushing everything later along on every unlocked track.

features.name: Overwrite
features.summary: Overwrite clears the file's length on one track and places the file there, moving nothing.

features.name: Insert or overwrite as you drop
features.summary: Hold ⌥ at the drop to insert, or ⇧⌥ to overwrite, when dragging a Media tab row onto a track.
features.where: Media tab ▸ drag a row onto a track

features.name: Drag to move a clip
features.summary: Drag a clip's body to move it in time, and up or down to move it to another track.

features.name: Move several clips together
features.summary: Drag any one of several selected clips to move them all, keeping the same time and number of tracks between them.
features.where: Timeline ▸ drag one clip of a selection

features.name: When a drop won't go where you let go
features.summary: Over a spot the overlap rule doesn't allow, the clip stays at the last allowed position, or where it started if there was none.

features.name: One undo step per drag
features.summary: A whole drag is one undo step, however long it lasts.

features.name: Nudge one frame
features.summary: Comma and period move the selected clips one frame earlier or later.

features.name: Nudge ten frames
features.summary: With ⇧, comma and period move the selected clips ten frames.

features.name: Drag an edge to trim
features.summary: Drag either edge of a clip to trim it.

features.name: Start trim
features.summary: A start trim moves the clip's start and its place in the footage together, so the rest of the clip stays where it is.
features.where: Timeline ▸ drag a clip's start edge

features.name: End trim
features.summary: An end trim moves the clip's end and changes nothing else about the clip.
features.where: Timeline ▸ drag a clip's end edge

features.name: Trim to the playhead
features.summary: W and E trim the start or end of each selected clip the playhead is inside to the playhead.
features.where: Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead, Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead

features.name: How far a trim goes
features.summary: A clip always keeps at least one frame, and a media clip's trim stops at the start and end of its file.

features.name: Type a clip's In and Out
features.summary: Type where a clip starts and ends on the timeline, which trims its edges.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing ▸ In and Out

features.name: Read a clip's duration
features.summary: Duration shows the clip's length. You can't type in it, so change the length through In and Out.

features.name: Timing with several clips selected
features.summary: With several video or audio clips selected, Timing holds only the Reverse rows. A mixed selection has no Timing section.

features.name: Slip
features.summary: ⌥⇧-drag a clip's body to slide the footage underneath it while the clip stays in place at the same length.

features.name: Roll
features.summary: ⌥⇧-drag a clip's edge to move the cut between two touching clips: one gets longer and the other shorter by the same amount.

features.name: Move a sound clip's edge alone
features.summary: A drag, W, E or a roll on a linked sound clip moves only the sound's edge, leaving its picture where it is.
features.where: Timeline ▸ drag a linked sound clip's edge

features.name: Split
features.summary: Clip ▸ Split cuts clips in two at the playhead.

features.name: Footage stays continuous
features.summary: The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped.

features.name: Actions and word timings
features.summary: Actions stay with the piece they fall in, an action spanning the cut becomes two, and caption word timings stay on their words.

features.name: Splitting a graphic
features.summary: A split graphic carries on across the cut rather than restarting, and plays its outro once, at the true end.

features.name: Split at Shot Changes
features.summary: Cuts each selected video clip at every hard cut in the part of the file it plays, giving one clip per shot in one undo step.

features.name: What counts as a hard cut
features.summary: A hard cut is a change from one picture to another between two frames, found by comparing each frame's colours with those before it.

features.name: Found on this Mac and cached
features.summary: Shot changes are found on the Mac with nothing sent anywhere and no key needed, and kept in the project's cache.

features.name: While the cuts are found
features.summary: The Analyzing sheet shows each file with a bar while cuts are found, and Stop closes it and changes nothing.

features.name: Cuts land on the frame grid
features.summary: Each shot cut lands on the project's frame grid, worked out through the clip's speed, speed ramp and reversal.

features.name: Shot splits on locked tracks
features.summary: A selected clip on a locked track is still cut, with its linked sound when that sound is on an unlocked track.

features.name: The clip limit for shot splits
features.summary: If the splits would take the project past 4,096 clips, nothing is split and the inspector says how many clips it would add and how many fit.

features.name: Delete
features.summary: Edit ▸ Delete removes the selected clips and leaves gaps.

features.name: Ripple Delete
features.summary: Edit ▸ Ripple Delete removes the selected clips and closes each hole they leave, moving everything later on every unlocked track left.

features.name: Lift
features.summary: With a range set and nothing selected, ⌫ removes what's in the range on every unlocked track and moves nothing.
features.where: Edit ▸ Delete with a range and no selection

features.name: Ripple Delete a range
features.summary: With a range set and nothing selected, ⌘⌫ removes what's in the range on every unlocked track and closes the hole.
features.where: Edit ▸ Ripple Delete with a range and no selection

features.name: Choose a delete
features.summary: Each delete key acts on the selection, or on the in and out range when nothing is selected. Only ⌘⌫ closes the hole.

features.name: How a ripple closes holes
features.summary: Each hole closes with one shift of everything after it, so clips that touched before still touch.

features.name: Ripple delete several ranges
features.summary: Agents cut a list of time ranges out of the timeline as one undo step, as Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words do.

features.name: Delete keys in text fields
features.summary: ⌫ and ⌘⌫ still edit text while you type in a field, because both menu items are greyed out there.

features.name: Close Gap
features.summary: Clip ▸ Close Gap closes the gap under the playhead on the current track, sliding everything after it left on every unlocked track.

features.name: Double-click a gap
features.summary: Double-click an empty stretch of a lane to close that gap, moving everything after it on every unlocked track left by the gap's length.
features.where: Timeline ▸ double-click an empty stretch of a lane

features.name: When a gap won't close
features.summary: A gap closes completely or not at all. If it can't, Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.

features.name: Insert time
features.summary: Agents can open empty room: clips on unlocked tracks and markers at or after a point move later. ⌥-drop insert does it too.

features.name: Open room by hand
features.summary: Select After Playhead, then drag or ⇧-nudge the clips later to open room on the timeline.

features.name: Duplicate
features.summary: Edit ▸ Duplicate puts a copy of each selected clip on the same track, starting right after the selection's span.

features.name: ⌥-drag a copy
features.summary: Hold ⌥ when you press on a clip to drag copies and leave the originals in place.

features.name: Copy
features.summary: Edit ▸ Copy puts the selected clips on the clipboard with a note of their media files, to paste here or in another project.

features.name: Cut
features.summary: Edit ▸ Cut copies the selected clips, then deletes them and leaves gaps, as ⌫ does.

features.name: Paste
features.summary: Edit ▸ Paste pastes the clipboard's clips at the playhead, then selects them.

features.name: Paste keeps the arrangement
features.summary: The earliest clip lands at the playhead, the others keep their distance from it, and each keeps its place back from the front track.

features.name: When a paste has no room
features.summary: A pasted clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new track at the front rather than being dropped.

features.name: Paste between projects
features.summary: You can paste clips into another project, and any media files that project lacks are added to its Media tab.

features.name: A detached sound comes along
features.summary: A selected picture brings its detached sound, so the pair pastes as a pair; a selected detached sound is copied on its own.

features.name: Copied clips as text
features.summary: Pasted into a text editor, copied clips arrive as a one-line summary.
features.where: Edit ▸ Copy, then paste in another app

features.name: Paste Attributes
features.summary: Edit ▸ Paste Attributes puts the look and sound settings of the earliest copied clip onto every selected clip, in one undo step.

features.name: Paste Attributes: the Video group
features.summary: The Video group carries everything about the picture: position, scale, rotation, crop, opacity, effects and grade.

features.name: Paste Attributes: the Audio group
features.summary: The Audio group carries everything about the sound: volume, pan, fades and effects.

features.name: Paste Attributes: the Text group
features.summary: The Text group carries font, size, colours, layout and animation, while the target keeps its own words and their timings.

features.name: Paste Attributes: the Shape group
features.summary: The Shape group carries fill, stroke, gradient and the rest of the style, while the target keeps its kind, size and end points.

features.name: What Paste Attributes leaves alone
features.summary: The target keeps its place, length, speed, animation actions, transition, name, label and which halves are switched on.

features.name: Paste attributes across a mixed selection
features.summary: An agent can paste attributes across a mixed selection without stopping, skipping clips that cannot take a group.

features.name: Qualifiers and adjustment clips
features.summary: A qualifier is copied only from one adjustment clip to another, and some picture settings can't land on an adjustment clip.

features.name: Turn a clip's picture or sound off
features.summary: Commands such as Detach Audio switch off a clip's picture or sound while it stays in place, and that half adds nothing.

features.name: Nest
features.summary: Clip ▸ Nest collapses the selected clips into one clip that moves, trims, fades and transforms as a group.

features.name: Where the nest clip lands
features.summary: The nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used, runs from the earliest start to the latest end, and is selected.

features.name: What a nest keeps
features.summary: Inside the nest, clips keep their properties, actions, transitions, relative timing and stacking order.

features.name: A nest's fixed canvas size
features.summary: A nest's canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest, and later size changes don't re-lay out what's inside.

features.name: Naming a nest
features.summary: Nests are named "Nest 1", "Nest 2" and so on, and you rename one through the menu or the Clip tab.

features.name: Un-nest
features.summary: Clip ▸ Un-nest opens every selected nest clip back out in one undo step and selects what came out.

features.name: What Un-nest discards
features.summary: Un-nesting discards the nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume.

features.name: Nests inside nests
features.summary: Nests can contain nests, up to eight levels deep.

features.name: Open Nest
features.summary: Go inside a nest to edit its contents in place, instead of un-nesting.

features.name: Close Nest
features.summary: Come out of a nest one level.

features.name: The breadcrumb
features.summary: While a nest is open, the corner above the track headers shows a path such as "Timeline › Intro", and clicking it goes out one level.

features.name: What you see inside
features.summary: Inside, the timeline shows the nest's own tracks and clips from zero, and the canvas shows the group without the nest clip's settings.

features.name: The playhead maps through
features.summary: The playhead moves with you into and out of a nest, so the frame under it doesn't change.

features.name: Going in and out isn't an edit
features.summary: Entering or leaving a nest makes no undo step and does not mark the project as changed.

features.name: Edits inside a nest
features.summary: Every clip edit works inside a nest, in the nest's own times, and each is one step on the project's single undo history.

features.name: Media and settings stay project-wide
features.summary: Adding, relinking or removing media and changing the Document tab still work with a nest open, and they change the whole project.

features.name: Limits count the whole project
features.summary: Clip, track and nesting-depth limits count the whole project even while you edit inside a nest.

features.name: Shared copies
features.summary: Split, Duplicate and ⌥-drag copies of a nest clip share one nest, so editing inside any of them changes them all.

features.name: Independent copies
features.summary: Duplicate a nest clip, un-nest the copy and nest its clips again to get a nest you can edit on its own.
features.where: Edit ▸ Duplicate, then Clip ▸ Un-nest and Clip ▸ Nest

features.name: Trimming a nest hides, it doesn't cut
features.summary: Trimming a nest clip changes how much of the nest plays and cuts nothing, so Un-nest still gives everything back.
features.where: Timeline ▸ drag a nest clip's edge

features.name: The preview canvas
features.summary: The canvas shows the composition at the playhead, at the project's size, centred in the preview pane.

features.name: Canvas size and rate caption
features.summary: A small line under the picture states the canvas size and frame rate.

features.name: Layers stack back to front
features.summary: A track higher in the timeline draws in front of the ones below it, and any kind of picture clip can share a track.

features.name: What you can do on the canvas
features.summary: Select, move, scale, rotate and crop a clip directly on the picture, with the same placement the Picture tab shows as numbers.

features.name: Hidden and locked tracks on the canvas
features.summary: Clips on hidden tracks are not drawn and can't be clicked; clips on locked tracks are drawn but can't be selected or moved on the canvas.

features.name: Canvas modes
features.summary: Tools that wait for a click or drag show a crosshair and a hint at the top of the preview. Only one can be on at a time, and Esc ends it.

features.name: The zoom popup
features.summary: A toolbar popup sets how large the picture appears: Fit, 50%, 100% or 200%.
features.where: The zoom popup in the toolbar

features.name: Zoom In, Zoom Out and Zoom to Fit
features.summary: View menu commands step the preview through its four zoom stops, or go straight back to Fit.
features.where: View ▸ Zoom In, Zoom Out, Zoom to Fit

features.name: Pinch and scroll to zoom
features.summary: A trackpad pinch, or scrolling with ⌥ or ⌘ held, steps through the zoom stops.

features.name: Pan a zoomed canvas
features.summary: When the zoomed canvas is bigger than the pane, scroll or hold Space and drag to pan it.

features.name: Space on the canvas
features.summary: After you've clicked the canvas, Space still plays and pauses when you release it, and holding it to drag pans instead.

features.name: Click to select a layer
features.summary: Clicking the picture selects the front-most visible clip under the pointer at the playhead.

features.name: Add or remove a clip with ⇧-click
features.summary: ⇧-click adds a clip to the selection or removes it.

features.name: Click empty canvas to deselect
features.summary: Clicking empty canvas clears the selection and leaves crop mode.

features.name: The selection frame and handles
features.summary: Every selected clip at the playhead gets an outline, and the front-most also gets eight square handles and a round rotation grip.

features.name: Selecting matte clips
features.summary: A clip on a matte track can be selected and dragged inside its own box even though it draws nothing there.

features.name: Drag to move
features.summary: Drag inside a clip's box to move it, and every selected clip moves by the same amount.
features.where: Drag a clip in the preview

features.name: Nudge with the arrow keys
features.summary: With the canvas focused and a selected clip showing at the playhead, the arrow keys move it 1 pixel, or 10 with ⇧.
features.where: The arrow keys, after clicking the canvas

features.name: Scale with the eight handles
features.summary: Drag a corner or edge handle to scale the clip, with the opposite handle pinned in place.
features.where: Drag a square handle in the preview

features.name: Scale about the centre
features.summary: Hold ⌥ while scaling to keep the clip's centre still instead of the opposite handle.

features.name: Rotate with the grip
features.summary: Drag the round grip above the top edge to rotate the clip about its centre.

features.name: Snap the angle
features.summary: Hold ⇧ while rotating to snap the angle to 15° steps.

features.name: Cancel a drag
features.summary: Press Esc during a canvas drag to put everything back, with no undo step.

features.name: The fixed pivot
features.summary: Rotation, the Scale field and a ⌥ scale drag all pivot on the centre of the clip's uncropped picture.

features.name: One undo step per drag
features.summary: Each canvas drag is one undo step, and a click that moves nothing adds no step.

features.name: What a move snaps to
features.summary: While you drag a clip to move it, its box snaps to the canvas and to other visible layers.
features.where: Drag a clip with snapping on

features.name: Snap guide lines
features.summary: A guide line is drawn across the canvas on each axis that snapped.

features.name: Suspend snapping for one drag
features.summary: Hold ⌘ during a drag to stop snapping for as long as it's down.

features.name: Safe area guides
features.summary: Two guide frames over the picture mark the 90 % title-safe and 80 % action-safe areas.

features.name: The Crop section
features.summary: Type how many source pixels to cut from each edge of a video clip, image clip or freeze frame.

features.name: Crop mode
features.summary: Press C, double-click a video clip, image clip or freeze frame, or use Crop on Canvas to crop the selected clip with handles on the canvas.
features.where: C, a double-click on the clip, or Inspector ▸ Clip ▸ Picture ▸ Crop ▸ Crop on Canvas

features.name: Crop handles
features.summary: In crop mode the eight handles trim the clip's edges, and the area being cut away shows as a faint white shape.
features.where: Drag a crop handle in crop mode

features.name: Leaving crop mode
features.summary: Return, keypad Enter, Esc, C, Crop on Canvas or a click on empty canvas leave crop mode from any focus but typing, and your crop stays.
features.where: Return, anywhere but a text field

features.name: A crop removes edges in place
features.summary: A crop never shifts the picture, and its amounts stay correct when you scale the clip later.

features.name: The Picture tab's sections
features.summary: The Clip tab's Picture sub-tab holds a clip's placement and picture effects, and which sections show depends on the selection.

features.name: How the sections behave
features.summary: Sections fold, show a summary while closed, and edit every selected clip at once.

features.name: Picture settings for agents
features.summary: An agent changes the placement and look of any number of clips with set_video, sending only the settings to change.

features.name: The Transform section
features.summary: Holds a clip's scale, position, rotation, opacity, blend and motion blur, for every clip that draws.

features.name: Scale
features.summary: Sets the clip's size as a percentage, where 100 % is its native pixels.

features.name: Position X and Y
features.summary: Places the clip in canvas pixels, measured from the canvas centre.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Position X, Position Y

features.name: Rotation
features.summary: Turns the clip in degrees about its centre; a positive angle turns clockwise on screen.

features.name: Opacity
features.summary: Sets how see-through the clip is.

features.name: Fit to Canvas
features.summary: Scales each selected clip so its whole picture fits the canvas, and centres it.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Fit to Canvas

features.name: Fill Canvas
features.summary: Scales each selected clip until it covers the whole canvas, and centres it.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Fill Canvas

features.name: Reset Transform
features.summary: Puts position, scale, rotation, opacity, blend and motion blur back to their defaults in one step.

features.name: No stretching on pictures
features.summary: A video, image or nest always keeps its proportions. Only shapes, text and graphics can change on one axis.

features.name: The Blend popup
features.summary: Chooses how a layer combines with what is under it.

features.name: Normal blend mode
features.summary: Draws over what is underneath.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend ▸ Normal

features.name: Multiply blend mode
features.summary: Darkens by multiplying with what is underneath.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend ▸ Multiply

features.name: Screen blend mode
features.summary: Lightens, the inverse of multiply.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend ▸ Screen

features.name: Add blend mode
features.summary: Adds the colours together.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend ▸ Add

features.name: Overlay blend mode
features.summary: Multiplies where what's underneath is dark, and screens where it's light.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend ▸ Overlay

features.name: Darken blend mode
features.summary: Keeps the darker of the two colours.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend ▸ Darken

features.name: Lighten blend mode
features.summary: Keeps the lighter of the two colours.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend ▸ Lighten

features.name: Difference blend mode
features.summary: Gives the absolute difference of the two colours.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend ▸ Difference

features.name: Warning when nothing is behind a blend
features.summary: The Transform section warns when a blend has nothing under it to work against.

features.name: Blend during a transition
features.summary: A layer draws as Normal for as long as it is in a transition, whatever blend mode it has.

features.name: Corner Radius
features.summary: Rounds the corners of a video clip, image clip or freeze frame, following any crop.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Corner Radius ▸ Radius

features.name: A background gets its own track
features.summary: Each background command puts one clip on a new back-most track and selects it.
features.where: Clip ▸ Add Background, Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background

features.name: Add Background: Solid Color
features.summary: Puts a canvas-sized white rectangle named "Background" behind everything, starting at 0 and as long as the timeline.

features.name: Add Background: Image
features.summary: Puts a picture you choose behind everything, scaled to fill the canvas and as long as the timeline.

features.name: Add Blurred Background
features.summary: Puts a muted, blurred, canvas-filling copy of the selected clip behind everything, the usual backdrop for a screen recording.

features.name: Matte tracks
features.summary: A matte track cuts the track directly behind it: its clips are never drawn, and what they show decides where the track behind can be seen.

features.name: Setting a matte
features.summary: Choose a mode from Track ▸ Matte, or right-click a track for its Matte submenu.
features.where: Track ▸ Matte, or right-click a track's header ▸ Matte

features.name: Matte mode: Off
features.summary: An ordinary track, which is every track's default.

features.name: Matte mode: Alpha
features.summary: The track behind shows where the matte clip is opaque.

features.name: Matte mode: Inverted Alpha
features.summary: The track behind shows where the matte clip is transparent.

features.name: Matte mode: Luma
features.summary: The track behind shows where the matte clip is bright.

features.name: Matte mode: Inverted Luma
features.summary: The track behind shows where the matte clip is dark.

features.name: Gaps in a matte track
features.summary: Where the matte track has no clip, the track behind shows uncut.

features.name: Turning a cut off for a while
features.summary: Hide Video on the matte track, or turning off a matte clip's picture, turns the cut off and shows the track behind whole.
features.where: Hide Video on the matte track

features.name: A matte with nothing to cut
features.summary: A matte on the back-most track, or directly in front of another matte track, cuts nothing and still draws nothing.

features.name: What shapes a matte
features.summary: Most of a matte clip's settings, from position and crop to filters and actions, shape the cut, so a moving title can wipe footage on.

features.name: What a matte ignores
features.summary: A matte clip's blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect, but they are kept and apply again when the track stops being a matte.

features.name: A matte clip's sound
features.summary: A matte clip's sound still plays.

features.name: Adjustment clips and mattes
features.summary: On a track cut by a matte, an adjustment clip grades only inside the matte; on a matte track it does nothing.

features.name: The matte note on the Clip tab
features.summary: With every selected clip on a matte track, each Clip sub-tab shows a note saying what the matte does, and every control still works.

features.name: How a matte track looks
features.summary: A matte track's header carries a tag, its clips draw at half opacity with dashed outlines, and a bracket joins it to the track it cuts.

features.name: Mattes inside a nest
features.summary: A matte track works inside a nest as it does on the timeline, and a nest clip can itself be a matte or be cut by one.

features.name: Nesting a matte
features.summary: Nest keeps a track's matte only when the track it cuts is nested with it.

features.name: Un-nesting a matte
features.summary: Un-nest lines the nest's front-most non-matte track up with the nest clip's track, so the picture comes back as it was.

features.name: Transitions across matted tracks
features.summary: Mattes work through transitions. A Cross Dissolve or Zoom involving a nest draws each side whole, then mixes the two.

features.name: Add a text clip
features.summary: Press T or click Add Text in the timeline bar to put a five-second title at the playhead.

features.name: Trim a text clip to any length
features.summary: A text clip has no source file, so you can trim it to any length.
features.where: Drag a text clip's edge on the timeline

features.name: Type a text clip's words
features.summary: Type the words in the Content box. Return applies them and ⇧Return starts a new line.

features.name: Place a text clip and add effects
features.summary: A text clip also has a Picture sub-tab for its position, scale, rotation, opacity and effects.

features.name: Restyle a text clip from an agent
features.summary: An agent can change any mix of a text clip's words and typography in one undo step.

features.name: Font Family
features.summary: Choose from every font family installed on the Mac, plus the faces the app ships with.

features.name: Font Style
features.summary: Pick one of the family's faces, such as Regular or SemiBold.

features.name: Font Size
features.summary: Set the text size in pixels.

features.name: Text Color
features.summary: Set the colour of the text.

features.name: Text Align
features.summary: Align text left, centre or right.

features.name: Vertical alignment
features.summary: Align text to the top, middle or bottom of its box, which moves it by a pixel or two at most.

features.name: UPPERCASE
features.summary: Show the text in capitals without changing what you typed.

features.name: Line spacing
features.summary: Set the space between lines as a multiple of the font's line height.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Style ▸ Line spacing

features.name: Tracking
features.summary: Set the spacing between letters.

features.name: Reset the text style
features.summary: Reset on the Style section puts colour, alignment, case, line spacing and tracking back to their defaults.

features.name: Edit text on the canvas
features.summary: Double-click a text clip in the preview to type straight into it.
features.where: Double-click a text clip in the preview

features.name: Apply canvas text
features.summary: Return, keypad Enter or a click elsewhere applies the text and closes the editor.
features.where: Return or keypad Enter in the canvas text editor

features.name: New line in canvas text
features.summary: Return with ⇧, ⌥, ⌘ or ⌃ starts a new line.
features.where: ⇧Return, ⌥Return, ⌘Return or ⌃Return in the canvas text editor

features.name: Leave the canvas editor with Esc
features.summary: Esc closes an unchanged editor at once. Over changed text, a sheet offers Apply, Revert and Cancel.
features.where: Esc in the canvas text editor

features.name: Input methods in canvas text
features.summary: While an input method is composing, Return and Esc go to the input method.

features.name: Text presets
features.summary: One click gives a text clip a font, size, alignment, backdrop and position sized to your canvas.

features.name: Title preset
features.summary: A large centred title.

features.name: Subtitle preset
features.summary: A smaller centred line below the middle.

features.name: Lower Third preset
features.summary: A left-aligned name strap on a plate.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Presets ▸ Lower Third

features.name: Caption preset
features.summary: A small caption line near the bottom, on a plate.

features.name: Text Outline
features.summary: Draw a stroke around the letters.

features.name: Outline Width
features.summary: Set the outline's thickness.

features.name: Outline Color
features.summary: Set the outline's colour.

features.name: Text Backdrop
features.summary: Put a rounded plate behind the text.

features.name: Backdrop Fill
features.summary: Set the plate's colour and opacity.

features.name: Backdrop Padding
features.summary: Set the space between the text and the plate's edge.

features.name: Backdrop Radius
features.summary: Round the plate's corners.

features.name: Text Box mode
features.summary: Choose Auto-size, where the box fits the words, or Fixed width, where the words wrap.

features.name: Text Box Width
features.summary: Set the width the text wraps at.

features.name: Set the wrap width with the side handles
features.summary: Drag a text clip's left or right handle on the canvas to set its wrap width.
features.where: Drag a text clip's left or right handle on the canvas

features.name: Text Reveal
features.summary: Choose how the text arrives and leaves: None, Typewriter, Word Fade or Line Rise.

features.name: Typewriter reveal
features.summary: The text types on, character by character.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Reveal ▸ Reveal ▸ Typewriter

features.name: Word Fade reveal
features.summary: Words fade in one after another.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Reveal ▸ Reveal ▸ Word Fade

features.name: Line Rise reveal
features.summary: Lines rise into place.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Reveal ▸ Reveal ▸ Line Rise

features.name: Reveal In and Out durations
