features.summary: Each EQ part has a typed Frequency and, by its kind, a Gain, a Q or a Slope.

features.name: Ride the level
features.summary: Turns the leveller on, evening out a voice that moves on and off the microphone by bringing each phrase toward a target.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Leveller ▸ Ride the level

features.name: Leveller target
features.summary: Where it aims, in dB from the clip's loudness.

features.name: Leveller Max Boost
features.summary: The most it turns the clip up.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Leveller ▸ Max Boost

features.name: Leveller Max Cut
features.summary: The most it turns the clip down.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Leveller ▸ Max Cut

features.name: Leveller response
features.summary: How smoothly it follows the voice within a phrase: shorter changes are smoothed out.

features.name: Leveller Status and Loudness readouts
features.summary: Readouts say where the leveller aims on this clip, what it waits for or why it isn't levelling, and the loudness it's measured from.

features.name: Smooth volume levels
features.summary: Turns the compressor on, evening out loud and quiet passages by turning down what goes above the threshold.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Compressor ▸ Smooth volume levels

features.name: Compressor threshold
features.summary: The level above which it starts turning the sound down.

features.name: Compressor ratio
features.summary: How strongly it turns down sound above the threshold.

features.name: Compressor attack
features.summary: How quickly it reacts when the level rises.

features.name: Compressor release
features.summary: How quickly it lets go when the level falls.

features.name: Compressor makeup
features.summary: Gain added afterwards to make up what the compressor took away.

features.name: Limit peaks
features.summary: Turns on a true-peak limiter that looks between samples and a little ahead, holding the clip's peaks under a ceiling.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Limiter ▸ Limit peaks

features.name: Limiter ceiling
features.summary: The highest true peak the clip may reach, after its volume.

features.name: Limiter release
features.summary: How quickly the level recovers after a peak.

features.name: Limiter latency compensation
features.summary: Looking ahead delays the sound by 3.3 ms, so Frame Job starts that track's clips 3.3 ms early and they stay on their frames.

features.name: Voice Effect
features.summary: Put one of sixteen effects, grouped Voice, Tone, Space and Character, on the clip's sound, or None.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect

features.name: Voice: Pitch
features.summary: Shifts the voice up or down without changing its speed.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Voice: Pitch

features.name: Voice: High
features.summary: Shifts the voice up 5 semitones and thins and brightens it, for a small, high voice.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Voice: High

features.name: Voice: Deep
features.summary: Shifts the voice down 5 semitones and warms it with low weight.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Voice: Deep

features.name: Voice: Robot
features.summary: Makes the voice metallic and buzzing with a ring modulator.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Voice: Robot

features.name: Tone: Bass
features.summary: Boosts the lows by up to 10 dB.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Tone: Bass

features.name: Tone: Treble
features.summary: Boosts the highs by up to 10 dB.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Tone: Treble

features.name: Tone: Bright
features.summary: Lifts the presence and air.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Tone: Bright

features.name: Tone: Telephone
features.summary: Squeezes the sound into the narrow band of a phone line.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Tone: Telephone

features.name: Tone: Radio
features.summary: Squeezes the sound into a narrow band with a radio tower's crackle.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Tone: Radio

features.name: Character: Lo-Fi
features.summary: Makes the sound gritty and dull, like a low-resolution recording.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Character: Lo-Fi

features.name: Character: Distorted
features.summary: Overdrives the sound into heavy distortion.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Character: Distorted

features.name: Space: Echo
features.summary: Repeats the sound every quarter of a second, each repeat darkened above 6 kHz.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Space: Echo

features.name: Space: Room
features.summary: Puts the sound in a medium room.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Space: Room

features.name: Space: Hall
features.summary: Puts the sound in a large hall.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Space: Hall

features.name: Space: Plate
features.summary: Adds a plate reverb.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Space: Plate

features.name: Space: Cathedral
features.summary: Puts the sound in a cathedral, with a long tail.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Effect ▸ Space: Cathedral

features.name: Voice Effect amount
features.summary: How much of the effect you hear, from 0 to 100 %, with every boost, mix and shift scaling with it.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Amount

features.name: Voice Effect pitch
features.summary: The shift in semitones, from −12 to 12, for Voice: Pitch, Voice: High and Voice: Deep only.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Pitch

features.name: Voice Effect status
features.summary: Shows where the effect's render has got to, such as Rendering…, Ready or Plays without it at this speed.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect ▸ Status

features.name: Voice Effect's background render
features.summary: The effect is worked out once per clip in the background; until ready the clip plays without it.

features.name: Ducking
features.summary: Lower every other clip while this one plays, usually so music drops under a voice-over.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck other audio

features.name: Duck by
features.summary: Clip Length keeps the others down for the clip's whole length; Speech only while this clip's speech plays.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck by

features.name: Ducking level
features.summary: How loud the other clips are while this one plays.

features.name: Ducking attack
features.summary: How long the other clips take to fall to Level, from this clip's first frame.

features.name: Ducking release
features.summary: How long they take to come back up, starting after this clip ends.

features.name: Duck by Speech
features.summary: The others go down only around this clip's stretches of speech, using speech detected on your Mac.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck by ▸ Speech

features.name: Duck by Speech pre-roll
features.summary: With Duck by Speech, how long before each stretch of speech the others start going down.

features.name: Duck by Speech hold
features.summary: With Duck by Speech, how long after each stretch of speech the others stay down before the release.

features.name: The yellow line on a clip ducking by speech
features.summary: A clip that ducks by speech has a thin yellow line across its waveform, high at full level and low where the others are ducked.
features.where: Timeline ▸ a clip ducking by speech

features.name: Give a file its own speech with an agent
features.summary: An agent can give a file stretches of speech of its own with set_media_speech, in place of the detected ones.

features.name: Detach Audio
features.summary: Splits each selected clip's sound onto a linked clip of its own on the track below.

features.name: Attach Audio
features.summary: Merges each detached sound in the selection back into its picture.

features.name: Linked clip marks
features.summary: Linked picture and sound each show a link symbol after their kind symbol, and selecting one draws a dashed ring around the other.

features.name: How a clip with its audio off looks
features.summary: A clip whose audio is off shows no waveform and no fade handles; a clip with picture and sound both off is drawn dimmed.

features.name: What stays in sync
features.summary: A linked picture and sound stay in step through moves, splits, ripple edits, slips and deletes, unless a lock holds one half.

features.name: Deleting one half
features.summary: Deleting a picture takes its sound, but deleting only the detached sound leaves the picture, silent, with its link gone.
features.where: Timeline ▸ select the sound half and press ⌫

features.name: A detached sound with actions or a ramp
features.summary: The new sound clip gets a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working and a ramped clip's sound keeps the same ramp.

features.name: J-cut
features.summary: Detach a shot's sound and drag its start edge left, so the sound begins before its picture.
features.where: Timeline ▸ drag a detached sound clip's start edge

features.name: L-cut
features.summary: Detach a shot's sound and drag its end edge right, so it runs on under the next shot.
features.where: Timeline ▸ drag a detached sound clip's end edge

features.name: Mute a track
features.summary: Silences every clip on the track; the picture is unaffected.

features.name: Solo a track
features.summary: Silences the tracks beside it: the other timeline tracks or, inside a nest, that nest's other tracks.

features.name: How a solo shows on silenced tracks
features.summary: Under a solo, waveforms on silenced tracks draw faded while their speaker switches stay unlit.

features.name: The Track Mix panel
features.summary: A small panel beside the header holds the track's volume, pan, compressor, limiter and Reset.
features.where: Track ▸ Mix…, or the sliders switch in the track header

features.name: Track volume
features.summary: The track's level, from Off to +12 dB, applied on top of every clip on it.

features.name: Track pan
features.summary: Leans the track's sound left or right.

features.name: Reset a track's mix
features.summary: Puts volume back to 0 dB, pan to centre, and turns the track's compressor and limiter off.

features.name: Track volume in a nest
features.summary: A clip inside a nest plays through its own track inside the nest and through the track the nest clip sits on.

features.name: What hears track volume
features.summary: The preview, exports, the level meter and Remove Silences include track volume. Normalize, the Loudness readout and a clip's limiter don't.

features.name: A track's own dynamics
features.summary: A track can have its own compressor and limiter acting on its whole sound, after each clip's processing and the track's volume and pan.

features.name: Track compressor
features.summary: Turns on a compressor over the track's whole sound, with Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release and Makeup.

features.name: Track limiter
features.summary: Turns on a true-peak limiter on what the track hands the mix, after its compressor, with Ceiling and Release.

features.name: A track as a nest's bus
features.summary: A compressor or limiter on the track holding a nest clip acts on everything inside the nest together.

features.name: Exact in the export, approximate in the preview
features.summary: An export runs a track's compressor and limiter exactly, while the preview approximates them where the track's clips overlap.

features.name: What hears track dynamics
features.summary: The preview, both meters and exports hear them. Normalize, the Loudness readout, Enhance Voice, Match Audio and a scrub don't.

features.name: Audio scrubbing
features.summary: Clicking or dragging along the ruler plays about 80 ms of the mix forward from each new frame.

features.name: The level meter
features.summary: A meter in the timeline bar, left of the zoom controls, shows the mix you are hearing while the timeline plays.

features.name: Two channel rows
features.summary: One row per channel on a −60 to 0 dB scale.

features.name: RMS bar and peak wash
features.summary: A solid bar shows the average level with a lighter wash behind it for the instantaneous peak.

features.name: Peak-hold mark
features.summary: A mark stays at the highest recent level for about 1.2 seconds, then falls.

features.name: Clip cell
features.summary: A cell at the right end of each row lights for 2 seconds when a sample reaches full scale.

features.name: The Loudness Meter
features.summary: A column beside the preview measures the mix you hear to EBU R 128 and ITU-R BS.1770 while it plays at normal speed.

features.name: M and S bars
features.summary: Two bars show Momentary and Short-term loudness on a scale from −48 to 0 LUFS.

features.name: The target line
features.summary: The Normalize row's target is drawn across the meter's scale as a thin accent line.

features.name: The four figures
features.summary: The column lists Momentary, Short-term, Integrated and True peak max.

features.name: Reset the Loudness Meter
features.summary: The Reset button at the top of the column starts measuring again, and the meter restarts itself on a jump.

features.name: Measuring only at normal speed
features.summary: At any other speed Momentary and Short-term show '—', and Integrated and True peak max keep their values.

features.name: The note under the figures
features.summary: A note under the figures says what is being measured and when it cannot be trusted.

features.name: Synchronize Audio
features.summary: Lines up two or more clips by their sound, such as a camera and a separate recorder, with each clip on its own track.

features.name: The anchor
features.summary: One clip stays where it is and every other clip slides along its own track to it.

features.name: Matching by sound
features.summary: Frame Job compares each file's analysed sound, speech first and trimmed parts first, so gain, microphone and room don't stop a match.

features.name: The waveform check
features.summary: A match is used only if the waveforms also line up, which keeps two takes of the same words apart and fine-tunes the offset.

features.name: Drift correction
features.summary: When clips overlap for at least 60 seconds, clock drift is measured and corrected by playing the clip at a slightly different speed.

features.name: The head trim
features.summary: A clip that would have to start before 0:00 loses that much from its start, and starts at 0:00 in sync.

features.name: Moves land on whole frames
features.summary: Clips move by a whole number of frames, so up to half a frame of constant offset can remain.

features.name: The Synchronizing Audio sheet
features.summary: Matching runs in the background behind a sheet with a progress bar and Cancel, and nothing moves until a match is found.

features.name: Which clips it takes
features.summary: It needs at least two selected clips that can play sound. Nests, stills, titles and clips with no sound are left out without a message.

features.name: When Synchronize Audio won't run
features.summary: If any clip can't be lined up, nothing moves, Frame Job beeps and the foot of the inspector lists every reason.

features.name: Confident matches
features.summary: A match whose best candidate has a confidence of at least 10 and at least 1.5 above the next is applied straight away.

features.name: The Weak match sheet
features.summary: A weak match, confidence at least 4 within about 3 seconds of where the clip sits, is never applied without asking.
features.where: Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio ▸ Weak match sheet

features.name: When nothing matches
features.summary: If nothing matches, the foot of the inspector names the offsets found and their confidences, so you can move the clip near one and retry.

features.name: Two commands for a spoken recording
features.summary: Remove Silences cuts the dead air and Remove Filler Words cuts the ums and uhs from a spoken recording, and both cut the same way.
features.where: Clip ▸ Remove Silences…, Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…

features.name: Preview shading on the timeline
features.summary: While a clean-up sheet is open, every span it would remove is shaded on the timeline ruler and lanes.
features.where: Timeline ruler and lanes, while a clean-up sheet is open

features.name: The cut count
features.summary: The sheet reads how many cuts it would make and how much time they remove, so you know the result before pressing Remove.
features.where: Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words sheets

features.name: One undo step
features.summary: Remove cuts every span and closes the timeline over each one as a single undo step, so one ⌘Z restores everything.

features.name: A ripple across every unlocked track
features.summary: A clean-up cut is a ripple delete across every unlocked track, not only the clips analysed, so the picture stays with its voice-over.

features.name: Markers keep their place
features.summary: Markers stay where they are when a clean-up cut closes the timeline.

features.name: Frame-accurate edges
features.summary: Each cut's start rounds up to the next frame and its end rounds down, so a cut never clips the start of the next word.

features.name: Nests are protected
features.summary: A clean-up cut never reaches into a nest clip. To clean up the audio inside one, open it and run the command there.

features.name: Transitions are protected
features.summary: A clean-up cut never reaches into a transition's overlap or the area around it.

features.name: The rest of the editor waits
features.summary: Playback pauses when a clean-up sheet opens, and other editing commands are unavailable until you close it.
features.where: Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words sheets

features.name: Cut edges in a reversed clip
features.summary: In Voice mode, a Remove Silences cut edge in a reversed clip can be off by up to 32 ms.

features.name: Make the cut from an agent
features.summary: An agent passes the ranges from detect_silence or detect_fillers to ripple_delete_ranges, which makes the same cut as Remove.

features.name: Remove Silences
features.summary: Finds the dead air in a spoken recording, shows it on the timeline and cuts it as one edit.

features.name: Which clips are measured
features.summary: In: chooses whether quiet is measured over Selected clips or All audible clips. The cut still reaches every unlocked track.

features.name: Longer than
features.summary: Sets the shortest quiet stretch worth cutting, 0.5 s by default, so short pauses such as the gap between two words stay.

features.name: Keep at ends
features.summary: Sets how much of each quiet stretch to keep at each end, 0.1 s by default, so speech doesn't start or stop abruptly.
features.where: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… ▸ Keep at ends:

features.name: Quieter than and Level if no voice
features.summary: A slider from −80 to −10 dBFS, at −40 by default, sets the level that counts as quiet.
features.where: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… ▸ Quieter than: or Level if no voice:

features.name: Numbers outside a field's range
features.summary: A number outside a field's range stays in the field, and Remove beeps until you fix it.
features.where: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… ▸ Longer than: or Keep at ends:

features.name: The count follows the controls
features.summary: The count and the shading update as you change a control, and for a number field when you leave it.

features.name: Timeline gaps are left alone
features.summary: Remove Silences leaves alone the gaps you placed between clips. Close Gap is the command for those.

features.name: When nothing is audible
features.summary: A line under the count tells you when nothing the sheet is measuring makes a sound, so nothing was analysed.

features.name: When analysis is still running
features.summary: The sheet names the files still being analysed and updates as each one finishes, so you can wait with it open.

features.name: Relinking restarts the analysis
features.summary: Relinking a file starts its analysis again. If an agent does it with the sheet open, the old results clear at once.

features.name: Quiet inside a nest
features.summary: The sheet says when a long quiet stretch ran across a nest and tells you to open it, because there may be dead air inside.

features.name: Find silences with an agent
features.summary: With detect_silence an agent reads the ranges the sheet would cut, changing nothing, and ripple_delete_ranges makes the cut.

features.name: Judge by
features.summary: Judge by picks how a moment is tested: Voice cuts where nobody is talking, Level cuts purely by loudness.

features.name: Voice mode
features.summary: In Voice mode quiet means nobody is talking: a voice model on your Mac listens to each file once and keeps the result with the project.
features.where: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… ▸ Judge by: Voice

features.name: Level mode
features.summary: In Level mode quiet means the sound in the mix is at or below the threshold.
features.where: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… ▸ Judge by: Level

features.name: Clips with no voice are judged by level
features.summary: In Voice mode, a clip with no voice in it at all, such as music or a tone, is judged by level instead, and the sheet names it.
features.where: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… ▸ Level if no voice:

features.name: When the voice model can't be used
features.summary: If the voice model can't be used on this Mac, the sheet opens in Level mode with Voice greyed out and says why.

features.name: Voice confidence
features.summary: An agent can set how sure the voice model must be for a moment to count as speech; the sheet has no control for it.

features.name: Silence is measured in the mix
features.summary: Silence is measured in the mix, as you hear it, not in the raw file.

features.name: Every clip being measured has to be quiet
features.summary: A stretch is silent only where every clip being measured is quiet, so a music bed holds up the pauses until you measure only the voice.
features.where: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… ▸ In: Selected clips

features.name: Muted clips are left out
features.summary: A muted clip is left out of the analysis entirely, so a muted music bed is never read as one long silence covering the whole song.

features.name: Nothing is cut before analysis finishes
features.summary: Nothing inside a file is offered for cutting until its analysis is ready, except a part the mix has already made quiet.

features.name: Limits of Voice mode
features.summary: A soft word can read as quiet, and so can music around a little speech. Raise Keep at ends: or measure Selected clips.
features.where: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… ▸ Keep at ends:

features.name: Remove Filler Words
features.summary: Finds the ums and uhs in your speech and cuts them at the words' own timings, as one edit.

features.name: Which words are fillers
features.summary: Fillers are a fixed list of eleven words, such as um, uh and er, ignoring capitals and punctuation. You can't change the list.

features.name: Which clips are read
features.summary: Remove Filler Words reads the selected clips when the selection includes speech from a media file, otherwise every clip.

features.name: A run of fillers is one cut
features.summary: Each run of consecutive fillers becomes one cut, with nothing to tune.

features.name: Neighbouring words are kept
features.summary: A filler cut stops short of the words on either side, and up to a frame of the filler can remain at each end.

features.name: Fillers left in whole
features.summary: A filler too short to cut, or whose cut would reach another clip's word, a nest, or an overlap between two clips on one track or the area around it, stays in whole, and the sheet counts it.

features.name: Clips on locked tracks aren't read
features.summary: A clip on a locked track isn't read, because the cut can neither cut nor move it, and the sheet says how many there are.

features.name: Clips with no words to read
features.summary: A clip that plays in reverse, has its sound off, or whose file is missing or has no audio track is passed over without a note.

features.name: Protection needs a transcript
features.summary: A filler cut is kept away from speech in another clip only when that clip's file has a kept AssemblyAI transcript.

features.name: The service can miss a filler
features.summary: A filler AssemblyAI doesn't return isn't cut, and one it returns that isn't on the list stays in, both in the cut and in captions.

features.name: Find filler words with an agent
features.summary: With detect_fillers an agent reads the ranges the sheet would cut, changing nothing, and ripple_delete_ranges makes the cut.

features.name: Filler words need a cloud transcript
features.summary: Filler words come only from an AssemblyAI transcript made with filler words, because transcription on your Mac doesn't report them.

features.name: The menu item with no key
features.summary: With no key the menu item is greyed and reads that it needs your AssemblyAI key, with a tooltip saying where to set one.

features.name: Using an existing transcript with no key
features.summary: If a file the command would read already has a filler transcript, the command stays on and cuts that file's fillers with no key.

features.name: Every AssemblyAI transcription asks for fillers
features.summary: Any file you caption with AssemblyAI is already ready for Remove Filler Words, with no second upload.

features.name: The list of files with no transcript
features.summary: Each file the sheet reads that has no filler transcript gets a row with its name, an upload and cost estimate, and a Transcribe button.

features.name: Where the audio goes
features.summary: Above the rows, the sheet says where the audio goes before anything is sent.

features.name: Transcribe a file for filler words
features.summary: Transcribe makes a paid upload of one file's audio to AssemblyAI, and updates only that file's kept transcript.

features.name: Progress and Stop
features.summary: While a run goes, the row shows its progress, its button reads Stop, the other rows' buttons are disabled and Remove is disabled.

features.name: When a run ends
features.summary: When a run finishes the file drops off the list and its fillers join the count. If it doesn't, the file stays listed and the note says why.

features.name: When Transcribe is disabled
features.summary: Transcribe is dimmed with no API key, while another file's run is going, and in the rare project with no folder to keep transcripts in.

features.name: Transcribing an unsaved project
features.summary: A project you haven't saved yet can be transcribed, and its transcript is kept with the project when you save.

features.name: The transcript also serves captions
features.summary: A filler transcript also serves Generate Captions, with no new upload or bill, if you ask for the same language, speakers and vocabulary.

features.name: Captions stay clean
features.summary: Filler words never reach captions made from an AssemblyAI transcript. Captions made on this Mac aren't filtered.

features.name: Transcribe for filler words with an agent
features.summary: With transcribe_for_fillers an agent makes the same paid upload of one file as the Transcribe button, but it has no Stop.

features.name: Cut a false start with the Assistant
features.summary: Ask the Assistant to cut a phrase the speaker abandoned or said again: it tells you which words it will cut, then cuts them in one step.

features.name: Remove fillers and silences by asking
features.summary: Ask the Assistant to take out silences, or fillers in files that already have a filler transcript, as the sheets would.

features.name: The Assistant won't start a paid transcription
features.summary: The Assistant can't start a paid filler transcription, so you press Transcribe in the sheet yourself.

features.name: Captions are ordinary text clips
features.summary: Every caption is a text clip on a track of its own at the front of the stack, so it draws over everything else.

features.name: Captions burn in with no extra step
features.summary: The preview, a rendered frame and an exported movie all show captions, because they are part of the picture.

features.name: Two kinds of caption: subtitles and word captions
features.summary: Generate classic two-line subtitles, or large captions in one of five styles where the word being said stands out.

features.name: Caption track names
features.summary: The first caption track is named Captions, then Captions 2, Captions 3 and so on, so separate runs can be told apart in the track headers.

features.name: Choosing the caption track
features.summary: Nothing marks a track as the caption track, so Export Captions lists every track of text clips for you to choose from.

features.name: Captions land on frames and never overlap
features.summary: Every caption starts and ends on a frame of the project, and captions on one track never overlap.
features.where: File ▸ Import Captions… or File ▸ Generate Captions…

features.name: Captions inside a nest
features.summary: The caption commands work on the timeline you have open, so with a nest open they work inside that nest.
features.where: File ▸ Import Captions…, Generate Captions… or Export Captions…

features.name: Import Captions
features.summary: File ▸ Import Captions… reads a SubRip (.srt) or WebVTT (.vtt) file onto a new caption track, one text clip per cue, as a single undo step.

features.name: Caption file variations it copes with
features.summary: Frame Job copes with common caption file variations, such as old line endings, a missing index line, short times, and UTF-16, Windows-1252 or Latin-1 text.

features.name: Markup stripped on import
features.summary: Formatting tags and overrides are removed and common HTML entities are decoded.

features.name: Line breaks kept
features.summary: The file's own line breaks are kept, and long lines also wrap inside the caption box.

features.name: Malformed entries are reported
features.summary: Bad entries are skipped and listed by line number, never dropped silently.

features.name: When a caption file can't be read
features.summary: If no caption in a file can be read, nothing is imported and a message gives the first three reasons.

features.name: Generate Captions
features.summary: File ▸ Generate Captions… transcribes the speech in your clips onto a new caption track, as ordinary text clips.

features.name: Choose what to transcribe
features.summary: From chooses what to transcribe: Selected clips, In/out range or Whole timeline.

features.name: Choose a speech engine
features.summary: Engine chooses where the words are recognised: On this Mac or AssemblyAI.

features.name: Choose the spoken language
features.summary: Language sets the spoken language of the run, from a list that depends on the engine.

features.name: Choose a caption style
features.summary: Style picks Subtitles or one of the five word caption styles.

features.name: Sample preview
features.summary: A sample page under the style and its look boxes shows the style on this canvas before you run anything.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ preview under Style

features.name: Replace existing captions
features.summary: With a word style chosen, Replace swaps out earlier caption tracks over the same clips instead of adding another.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ Replace: existing captions

features.name: The sheet remembers its choices
features.summary: Generate Captions reopens with your last engine, Style and three look boxes.

features.name: Summary line and note
features.summary: Under the rows, a summary gives the size of the run, and a note explains anything stopping it.

features.name: Progress
features.summary: While a run goes, the card shows a progress bar, "Transcribing N clips…" and a detail line.

features.name: Cancel a run
features.summary: Cancel stops a run, closing the sheet mid-run also stops it, and nothing is placed.

features.name: The run report
features.summary: Placing the captions is one undo step, and a run with something to report keeps the card open to say so.

features.name: Generating captions from an agent
features.summary: The transcribe tool does what the sheet does, and can return the captions without placing them so an agent can check them first.

features.name: Which clips can be transcribed
features.summary: A clip can be transcribed if it plays forwards from a movie or sound file with an audio track, its audio is on and its file is present. Whole timeline and In/out range read only clips you can hear.

features.name: Why a clip is skipped
features.summary: The sheet leaves a clip it can't read out of its count, and an agent that names the clip is told why.

features.name: Retimed clips land correctly
features.summary: On a sped-up, slowed or speed-ramped clip, each word lands where it is heard on the timeline.

features.name: The 10-hour and 4,096-clip limits
features.summary: AssemblyAI takes at most 10 hours per file, and captions that would take a project past 4,096 clips aren't placed.

features.name: Transcribe on this Mac
features.summary: With Engine set to On this Mac, each clip's own part of its media is extracted and recognised locally, and nothing is uploaded.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ Engine ▸ On this Mac

features.name: No permission prompt
features.summary: macOS shows no permission prompt, because the recogniser reads an extracted audio file and never touches the microphone.

features.name: On-device languages
features.summary: Language lists every language this Mac's recogniser supports, and marks one with no speech model as not installed.

features.name: Download a speech language
features.summary: A language whose model is missing can be installed from a Download button under the Language pop-up.

features.name: Every run recognises the audio again
features.summary: Nothing is kept between runs for captions made on this Mac, so every run, restyling included, takes the time again.

features.name: The pause note
features.summary: With On this Mac and a word style chosen, a note says on-device words rarely carry a pause.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ under the look boxes

features.name: Transcribe with AssemblyAI
features.summary: With Engine set to AssemblyAI, your files' audio is transcribed in the cloud on your own key, then deleted there once the words are back.

features.name: Generate needs a key, unless the words are cached
features.summary: With no key saved, the sheet says where to set one and Generate is greyed, unless every file is already transcribed.

features.name: Split the words by speaker
features.summary: Speakers asks AssemblyAI to split the words by speaker, so a change of speaker always starts a new cue or page.

features.name: Vocabulary for names and jargon
features.summary: Vocabulary sends AssemblyAI the names and jargon to expect, separated by commas, up to 1,000 terms.

features.name: Language detection and languages
features.summary: A cloud run can leave the language to Detect automatically, or name one of 18 languages, with English listed four ways.

features.name: Detected language in the report
features.summary: With Detect automatically, the run report gives each file's detected language and how confident AssemblyAI was.

features.name: Fallback model in the report
features.summary: If AssemblyAI used a different model than the one asked for, the run report says so.

features.name: The price before you press Generate
features.summary: The summary line prices the run at AssemblyAI's published rate, updating as you change the controls.

features.name: Why each file uploads
features.summary: Hovering over the summary gives one line per file that is not already transcribed, saying why, followed by the dated rate.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ hover the summary line

features.name: One transcript cached per media
features.summary: Each file's transcript is kept in the project package, so a later run with the same settings uploads nothing and costs nothing.

features.name: Untitled projects
features.summary: An untitled project can be transcribed too: its transcripts stay in a temporary folder until it is saved, then go into the project package.

features.name: Transcribe again
features.summary: Transcribe again ignores any cached transcript and uploads again, which is a paid upload.

features.name: Filler words stay out of captions
features.summary: AssemblyAI's words include fillers, but captions and the sheet's preview leave them out.

features.name: When a file fails
features.summary: One file's failure does not end a run: its clips are listed with the reason, and captions from the other files are still placed.

features.name: What is uploaded and billed
features.summary: The whole audio of each file behind your clips is uploaded and billed, not only the parts in use, and the video stays on your Mac.

features.name: The transcript is deleted after reading
features.summary: Once the words have been read back, Frame Job asks AssemblyAI to delete its copy, automatically.

features.name: Unconfirmed deletes are retried
features.summary: An unconfirmed delete is retried at the start of the next AssemblyAI run in the project, with a key for the same account and region.

features.name: A pending delete holds a file back
features.summary: While a delete is pending, that file is not uploaded again until it clears.

features.name: Save your AssemblyAI key
features.summary: Paste your own AssemblyAI key into Settings and press Save or Return.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription ▸ AssemblyAI API key:

features.name: Remove the key
features.summary: Remove deletes the saved key.

features.name: Where the key is kept
features.summary: The key is saved in a file only you can read, not in the Keychain, and is never passed on the command line.

features.name: A key from the environment
features.summary: If no key is saved, Frame Job also accepts one from the RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY environment variable, useful when launching from a terminal.

features.name: Verify your key
features.summary: Verify checks that the key works in your region with AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, transcribing and billing nothing.

features.name: AssemblyAI region
features.summary: Region chooses the AssemblyAI data centre your audio goes to: United States or European Union.

features.name: Account Page
features.summary: Account Page opens your AssemblyAI dashboard in the browser, where you get a key and see what you have spent.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription ▸ Account Page

features.name: The Transcription info button
features.summary: The ⓘ beside the heading explains what is uploaded, what is deleted, the published rate and where the key is kept.

features.name: What the key turns on
features.summary: Your AssemblyAI key turns on the AssemblyAI engine of Generate Captions and Remove Filler Words, which finds fillers only through AssemblyAI.

features.name: Only a person sets the key
features.summary: No agent tool can read or change the key or the region: only a person sets them, in Settings.

features.name: The Subtitles style
features.summary: The Subtitles style makes classic two-line cues as text clips.

features.name: Speaker colours
features.summary: With Speakers on, each speaker's cues take their own colour, in the order the speakers first appear.

features.name: The Caption preset
features.summary: Each cue uses the Caption text preset, and on a canvas taller than wide the box sits higher.

features.name: Word caption pages
features.summary: The five word styles make large captions for shorts and reels: each clip holds a page of timed words, with the spoken word marked.

features.name: Highlight
features.summary: The spoken word turns yellow and pops to 112%.

features.name: Pill
features.summary: The spoken word sits on a violet pill.

features.name: Karaoke
features.summary: Words turn yellow as they are said and stay yellow, while words still to come are dimmed white.

features.name: Build
features.summary: Words appear one by one, and the newest is yellow and pops to 115%.

features.name: One Word
features.summary: One large white word shows at a time, popping to 120%.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ Style ▸ One Word

features.name: Bundled typefaces
features.summary: Montserrat Black, Montserrat ExtraBold, Anton and Bebas Neue ship inside the app, so there's nothing to install.

features.name: Pages are filled to their measured width
features.summary: A page holds as many words as fit, up to 86% of the canvas width, measured in its style on your canvas.

features.name: Where a page breaks
features.summary: A page ends early at a pause of 0.25 s or more, at the end of a sentence, after 3 seconds or at a change of speaker.

features.name: A word too wide for the frame
features.summary: A single word too wide for the frame shrinks, down to 80% of the style's size, before it wraps.

features.name: How long a page stays up
features.summary: A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, or runs up to the next page if that starts sooner, so the row doesn't blink.

features.name: The sheet's two-frame preview
features.summary: A word style's preview shows two frames, with the first word active in the top frame and the second in the bottom one.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ preview under Style

features.name: Three looks for word captions
features.summary: Three checkboxes under the Style pop-up each add a look to a word style's pages.

features.name: Slide the pill
features.summary: The pill slides from the previous word to the one being said instead of jumping.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ Slide the pill

features.name: Fill words as spoken
features.summary: The word being said fills from left to right as it is spoken.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ Fill words as spoken

features.name: Dim in pauses
features.summary: The page fades to half opacity during a pause, then comes back before the next word.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ Dim in pauses

features.name: Change word colours
features.summary: No inspector section changes a page's word colours, pop or pill: generate again with another style, or ask an agent.

features.name: Restyle by generating again
features.summary: A style is fixed when the captions are generated: to change it, generate again over the same clips with Replace on.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ Replace: existing captions

features.name: Which tracks Replace may remove
features.summary: Replace works only for a word style, on text tracks named Captions or Captions N whose clips all overlap what's being transcribed.
features.where: File ▸ Generate Captions… ▸ Replace: existing captions

features.name: Change a run of captions together
features.summary: Select a run of captions and restyle them together in the inspector's Text sections; each page keeps its own words and word timing.

features.name: Re-lay Captions for This Canvas
features.summary: After a canvas size change, this command pages word captions again for the new width from the words they already hold, as one undo step.
features.where: File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas

features.name: What a re-lay keeps
features.summary: Your corrected words are kept and each page stays inside its own clip, but hand changes such as a colour or size go.
features.where: File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas

features.name: Tracks kept as placed
features.summary: A track that cannot be re-laid is kept as placed, and a sheet after the edit names each one and why.
features.where: File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas

features.name: When Re-lay Captions is available
features.summary: The item is greyed with no caption track it can re-lay, while a sheet is open, and while a recording runs.
features.where: File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas

features.name: Edit captions in the Text sections
features.summary: Captions are text clips, so the inspector's Clip tab edits them under Text: Content, Font, Style, Outline, Backdrop, Box, Reveal and Presets.

features.name: Case on a word page
features.summary: The style's capitals come from UPPERCASE: turn it off to show a page as written.

features.name: Change the words on a page
features.summary: Keeping the same number of words keeps each word's timing, and changing the number drops it, so the page shows plainly.

features.name: Reveals don't work on a word caption page
features.summary: The text reveals (Typewriter, Word Fade and Line Rise) don't work on a word caption page, and their rows are greyed.

features.name: Trimming, splitting and moving a page
features.summary: Trimming and splitting keep each word on the speech it times, and dragging a page moves its words with it.

features.name: Word timings for agents
features.summary: With set_text, an agent can rewrite a page's word timings and its word style, which the inspector can't.

features.name: Newly revealed speech stays uncaptioned
features.summary: When a speed-up or ramp plays further into the file, the new part gets no captions until you generate again.

features.name: Export Captions
features.summary: File ▸ Export Captions… writes one caption track out as SubRip (.srt) or WebVTT (.vtt), and changes nothing in the project.

features.name: Choose the track to export
features.summary: Track picks which track to write, front-most first, with each row reading like "Captions — 12 cues (track 4)".

features.name: Format: SubRip or WebVTT
features.summary: Format picks SubRip (.srt) or WebVTT (.vtt), and changing it changes the file name's extension.

features.name: One cue per text clip
features.summary: Each text clip on the track becomes one cue, at the time and with the words it has now, so a caption you dragged exports where you dragged it.

features.name: Frame-exact round trips
features.summary: A track exported and imported again puts every cue back on the frame it came from, at every ordinary frame rate.

features.name: The Transcript tab
features.summary: The Transcript tab shows what's said in your project as text you can read and click.

features.name: Open the Transcript
features.summary: View ▸ Transcript shows the tab with the text ready for its keys; you can also click Transcript in the inspector's tab strip.

features.name: Every word you would hear
features.summary: The tab lists every word you would hear when the timeline plays, in order: clips on every track, and clips inside nests where they play.

features.name: Paragraphs and timecodes
features.summary: The words come in paragraphs, each with its timecode above it.

features.name: The bar
features.summary: A bar above the text holds the tab's choices and notes, and stays put while the text scrolls.

features.name: Words from
features.summary: Words from chooses whose words to show: All tracks, or one track by name.

features.name: Transcript language
features.summary: Language chooses the language files are read in on this Mac.

features.name: Read and Stop
features.summary: While a file is being transcribed a note shows its progress with a Stop button, and after Stop a Read button carries on.

features.name: Clips with no words
features.summary: A clip with no words is listed under the pop-ups with the reason.

features.name: The same speech on two tracks
features.summary: When two clips carry the same speech, a note names the pair so you can mute one and read it once.

features.name: AssemblyAI first, otherwise this Mac
features.summary: If a file already has an AssemblyAI transcript, the tab uses it; otherwise the tab transcribes the file on this Mac the first time you look.

features.name: Kept per file and language
features.summary: What this Mac heard is kept in the project per file and language, so the next look is immediate.

features.name: One file at a time, playhead first
features.summary: Files are read one at a time, starting with the one under the playhead, and each file's words appear as soon as it is done.

features.name: When no speech model is installed
features.summary: If your Mac has no speech model installed, the tab says so and points you to the download.

features.name: Ramped clips and following edits
features.summary: Words are placed through a clip's speed, including a ramp, and editing the timeline updates the text right away.

features.name: The word being spoken
features.summary: While the video plays, the word being spoken is highlighted.

features.name: The text scrolls with playback
features.summary: The text scrolls to keep the spoken word in view.

features.name: Click a word to jump
features.summary: Clicking a word moves the playhead to it and selects it.

features.name: Click a timecode to jump
features.summary: Clicking a paragraph's timecode moves the playhead to the start of that paragraph.

features.name: A selected clip scrolls to its words
features.summary: Clicking a clip on the timeline or canvas while the Transcript shows scrolls its first word to the top.
features.where: Timeline or canvas, click a clip

features.name: Loop plays the selected words
features.summary: Loop plays the shaded range, so a cut can be heard before you delete.

features.name: Selecting words
features.summary: Click a word, drag across a run, or extend with ⇧-click or ⇧ and an arrow, and ⌘A selects every word.

features.name: The selection is the in/out range
features.summary: Whatever you select becomes the timeline's in/out range, so the timeline shades exactly what will go.

features.name: Delete Words
features.summary: Select words and press ⌫: the words and the sound under them come out of every unlocked track and the gap closes, as one undo step.

features.name: Where a word cut falls
features.summary: A cut runs from the first word's start to the start of the next word you keep, so the pause before stays and the pause after goes.

features.name: Where a word starts
features.summary: For words read on this Mac, the tab moves each start to where its sound begins, so a cut keeps no slice of the pause.

features.name: Words that can't be cut
features.summary: Some words are shown faint: a cut at them would break something, so they can't be deleted, and holding the pointer over one says why.
features.where: Inspector ▸ Transcript, hover a faint word

features.name: Overlapping words on other tracks
features.summary: If a word on another track runs into your selection, the tab adds it first, so you see everything the cut takes.

features.name: When the tab won't cut
features.summary: When a cut can't go ahead, the tab beeps, keeps your selection and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector.

features.name: How exact a word cut is
features.summary: Word edges come from the transcript, so in fast speech a cut can take the end of the word before it or leave a sliver of a deleted word.

features.name: Pauses in the transcript
features.summary: A stop of more than a second between two words of one clip shows in grey as its length, such as [2.4 s].

features.name: Select a pause
features.summary: Clicking a pause selects it on its own, makes the part that would go the in/out range, and moves the playhead to the start of that cut.

features.name: Delete Pause
features.summary: With a pause selected, ⌫ shortens it, keeping 0.2 s at each end, and closes the gap on every unlocked track, as one undo step.

features.name: Move word by word
features.summary: ← and → select the previous or next word and move the playhead to it.

features.name: Move line by line
features.summary: ↑ and ↓ select the nearest word on the line above or below and move the playhead to it.

features.name: Extend the selection
features.summary: ⇧ with an arrow grows the selection without moving the playhead.

features.name: Select every word
features.summary: ⌘A selects every word.

features.name: Clear the selection
features.summary: ⎋ clears the selected words or pause, along with the range they set.

features.name: Delete the selection
features.summary: ⌫ or ⌦ deletes the selected words and closes the gap, or shortens the selected pause.

features.name: Timeline keys keep working
features.summary: Every other key works as it does on the timeline while the transcript text has the keyboard.

features.name: One grade everywhere
features.summary: The preview, Save Frame… and every export draw a grade the same way.

features.name: Ungraded clips stay untouched
features.summary: A clip you haven't graded renders exactly as it would without a grade.

features.name: The Color sub-tab
features.summary: A sub-tab of the Clip inspector that holds every grading control for the selected clips.

features.name: What can be graded
features.summary: Video clips, image clips, stills (freeze frames) and adjustment clips can take a grade.

features.name: Mixed selections
features.summary: Mixing a text, shape, graphic or nest clip into the selection hides the tab, while an audio-only clip does not.

features.name: Sections only adjustment clips show
features.summary: The Adjustment and Qualifier sections show only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip.

features.name: Section summaries
features.summary: Each section's header shows a short summary of its state.

features.name: Reset a section
features.summary: A section's Reset, shown while it differs from its default, returns only that section to neutral.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color, section header ▸ Reset

features.name: Which section opens
features.summary: If no section is open, the tab opens the first one you haven't closed yourself.

features.name: Grade several clips at once
features.summary: With several clips selected, a control changes only its own value on each clip and keeps their other values.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color with several clips selected

features.name: Undo in the Color tab
features.summary: A slider drag or a typed value is one undo step named after its control.

features.name: The fixed grade order
features.summary: The grade always applies in one order: Color, Light, Wheels, Curves, then the Look.

features.name: Filters around the grade
features.summary: The Picture tab's filters act on either side of the grade, which matters when you combine them with one.

features.name: The Light section
features.summary: Nine tone and white-balance controls, each a slider with a number field beside it.

features.name: Exposure
features.summary: Brightens or darkens the picture in stops, from −3 to +3 EV, with black staying black.

features.name: Temperature
features.summary: Makes the picture warmer (more red, less blue) or cooler (more blue, less red).

features.name: Tint
features.summary: Shifts the picture toward magenta (positive) or green (negative).

features.name: Highlights
features.summary: Lifts or lowers the brighter half of the tones.

features.name: Shadows
features.summary: Lifts or lowers the darker half of the tones.

features.name: Whites
features.summary: Stretches the tones toward white, with black held.

features.name: Blacks
features.summary: Raises (positive) or deepens (negative) the dark end of the tones, with white held.

features.name: Vibrance
features.summary: Changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it.

features.name: Fade
features.summary: Lifts black toward 10 % and lowers white toward 95 %, for a washed-out film look.

features.name: Set Light and Color with an agent
features.summary: One set_video call can set any of the nine Light and four Color controls together.

features.name: The Color section
features.summary: Four sliders for overall Brightness, Contrast, Saturation and Hue.

features.name: Brightness
features.summary: Raises or lowers every level.

features.name: Contrast
features.summary: Spreads the tones apart or pulls them together.

features.name: Saturation
features.summary: Gives more or less colour overall.

features.name: Hue
features.summary: Turns every colour around the colour wheel.

features.name: The Wheels section
features.summary: Three colour wheels side by side, Lift, Gamma and Gain, each with a colour disc, a master strip and a number field.

features.name: Lift
features.summary: Moves black and holds white, so it mostly affects the shadows.

features.name: Gamma
features.summary: Moves the middle tones and holds both ends.

features.name: Gain
features.summary: Moves white and holds black, so it mostly affects the highlights.

features.name: Drag the puck
features.summary: Dragging on a disc pushes the wheel's tonal range toward a colour: the direction picks the hue, the distance the strength.

features.name: Wheels match the vectorscope
features.summary: Each hue on a disc sits where the vectorscope draws it, so dragging toward a colour moves the trace toward it.

features.name: Fine drag on a wheel
features.summary: Holding ⌥ moves a puck or a strip at a tenth of the speed, and a strip doesn't jump to the pointer.

features.name: Reset a wheel's push
features.summary: Double-clicking a disc returns the push to the centre and leaves the wheel's brightness alone.

features.name: Reading the push
features.summary: Hovering a disc shows its push as a hue angle and strength, or Neutral when the puck is centred.

features.name: Master strip
features.summary: The strip under each disc sets that wheel's master brightness.

features.name: Reset a wheel's master
features.summary: Double-clicking the strip returns the master to 0.

features.name: Master field
features.summary: Type a wheel's master value directly in the field under its strip.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Wheels ▸ master field

features.name: Set the wheels with an agent
features.summary: An agent can set each wheel's push and brightness as exact numbers, the only way to enter a push by number.

features.name: The Curves section
features.summary: A square plot with a channel picker above it and the selected point's fields below it.

features.name: The channel picker
features.summary: Six cells above the plot choose which channel you edit: Master, Red, Green, Blue, Hue and Sat.

features.name: Master curve
features.summary: A tone curve on all three colours, for contrast and the black and white points.

features.name: Red curve
features.summary: A tone curve on the red channel only.

features.name: Green curve
features.summary: A tone curve on the green channel only.

features.name: Blue curve
features.summary: A tone curve on the blue channel only.

features.name: Other curves behind the plot
features.summary: Tone channels you've changed show as faint lines in their own colour behind the curve you're editing.

features.name: The changed-channel dot
features.summary: A dot under a picker cell means that channel has been changed.

features.name: Point limits
features.summary: A curve holds 2 to 16 points and runs smoothly through them without overshooting.

features.name: Add a point
features.summary: Clicking the plot away from a point adds one on the curve above or below the click, ready to drag.

features.name: A stray click changes nothing
features.summary: A point added to a straight channel isn't saved until you move it, nudge it or type a value.

features.name: Drag a point
features.summary: Dragging moves a point, which stays inside the plot and can't pass its neighbours.

features.name: Fine drag on a curve
features.summary: ⌥-drag moves a point at a tenth of the speed.

features.name: Axis lock
features.summary: ⇧-drag locks the point to the axis you moved along most.

features.name: Nudge a point
features.summary: The arrow keys nudge the selected point, and ⇧ with an arrow nudges it ten times as far.

features.name: Delete a point
features.summary: Remove the selected point with ⌫ or ⌦, the Delete button below the plot, or a double-click on the point.
features.where: Curves plot: ⌫ or ⌦, or double-click a point

features.name: Deselect a point
features.summary: Esc deselects the point and hands the keyboard back to the editor.

features.name: The plot and the keyboard
features.summary: While a point is selected the plot has the keyboard, but keys it doesn't use still reach the editor.

features.name: In and Out fields
features.summary: Below the plot, the In and Out fields let you type the selected point's position.
features.where: Below the Curves plot: In, Out

features.name: Hover readout
features.summary: While the pointer is over the plot, and during a drag, a label shows its position and the curve's value there.

features.name: Undo in Curves
features.summary: Each drag, nudge, deletion or typed value is one undo step named Curves.

features.name: Reset one channel
features.summary: Right-click a channel's cell and choose its Reset item to straighten that channel alone.
features.where: Curves picker: right-click ▸ Reset Master, Reset Red, Reset Green, Reset Blue, Reset Hue or Reset Sat

features.name: Reset all curves
features.summary: The Curves section's Reset straightens all six channels in one undo step.

features.name: Write curves with an agent
features.summary: An agent writes a whole channel as a list of 2 to 16 points, and the list replaces that channel.

features.name: The two hue channels
features.summary: The Hue and Sat channels turn or saturate one colour at a time, on a plot in degrees over a spectrum strip.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Curves ▸ Hue, Sat

features.name: Hue vs Hue
features.summary: Shifts a chosen hue toward another with brightness kept, such as making the greens more teal.

features.name: Hue vs Sat
features.summary: Saturates or mutes a chosen hue.

features.name: The spectrum strip
features.summary: A hue channel plots in degrees with a spectrum strip under it, so you can see which colour each point sits on.
features.where: Curves plot on Hue or Sat

features.name: Hue curve safeguards
features.summary: A hue curve never tints a grey, and its points never cross the 0°/360° wrap.
features.where: Curves plot on Hue or Sat

features.name: Write hue curves with an agent
features.summary: An agent writes hue_hue and hue_sat whole, each as a list of 2 to 16 hue and value pairs.

features.name: The Look gallery
features.summary: A 3 × 3 grid of tiles, None and the eight looks, each a thumbnail of the first selected clip with that look applied.

features.name: Live thumbnails
features.summary: Each tile shows the actual frame with that look, refreshed a moment after the playhead stops or an edit lands.

features.name: Warm
features.summary: A warmer white balance with golden highlights.

features.name: Cool
features.summary: A cooler white balance with blue shadows.

features.name: Teal & Orange
features.summary: Teal shadows and orange highlights, with more contrast and vibrance.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look ▸ Teal & Orange

features.name: Vivid
features.summary: More contrast and strong vibrance, with deeper blacks and brighter whites.

features.name: Faded
features.summary: Low contrast, muted colour and lifted blacks, for a washed-out picture.

features.name: Vintage
features.summary: Muted and warm, with a fade, green-tinted shadows and yellow-tinted highlights.

features.name: Dramatic
features.summary: Darker, contrasty and desaturated, with cool shadows.

features.name: Black & White
features.summary: Monochrome, with all colour removed and more contrast.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look ▸ Black & White

features.name: Apply a look
features.summary: Clicking a tile puts that look on every selected clip.

features.name: The outlined tile
features.summary: The tile of the look every selected clip shares is outlined in the accent colour.

features.name: Remove a look
features.summary: The None tile, the section's Reset or Clip ▸ Look ▸ None takes the look off and leaves the rest of the grade.
features.where: Look gallery ▸ None, or Clip ▸ Look ▸ None

features.name: Look Amount
features.summary: Sets how much of the look applies, from 0 to 100%.

features.name: Apply a look from the menu
features.summary: The menu does what the gallery does: the eight looks, then any imported LUTs, then None.

features.name: The Look summary
features.summary: The section header reads the look and its amount, for example Warm 80%.

features.name: Looks on stills and adjustment clips
features.summary: A look works on video, image and still clips, and on adjustment clips.

features.name: Set a look with an agent
features.summary: An agent sets a look by kind with set_video, with an optional amount, and removes it with look: null.

features.name: Supported .cube files
features.summary: Frame Job reads 3D LUTs in a text .cube file of up to 32 MiB, and shows an error for anything else.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look ▸ Import LUT…

features.name: Import LUT…
features.summary: The button under the gallery picks a .cube file and applies it to the selected clips.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look ▸ Import LUT…

features.name: Add a LUT with Add Media…
features.summary: File ▸ Add Media… adds a .cube file to the project, to use as a look or a Camera Log conversion.

features.name: Drop a LUT on the Media tab
features.summary: Dropping a .cube file on the Media tab adds it to the project.

features.name: LUT rows on the Media tab
features.summary: A LUT appears in the media list with a cube icon and never goes on the timeline.

features.name: Imported tiles
features.summary: Each LUT gets a tile in the gallery's Imported group, previewing it on your frame.

features.name: LUTs in Clip ▸ Look
features.summary: Each LUT gets an item in Clip ▸ Look between the eight looks and None.

features.name: A LUT is a look
features.summary: A LUT is applied at the same step as a built-in look and uses the same Amount row.

features.name: A changed file
features.summary: If you change the file on disk, the new table is read at the next frame drawn.

features.name: A missing or broken file
features.summary: If the file goes missing or can't be read, the clip draws without its look and keeps the rest of its grade.

features.name: A LUT can't be placed as a clip
features.summary: An agent can't place a LUT as a clip, and the error says how to apply it instead.

features.name: Removing a LUT in use
features.summary: Removing a LUT in use asks first, counting its uses. Its button names what it clears and keeps the clips.
features.where: Media tab ▸ right-click a LUT row ▸ Remove

features.name: A LUT in an HDR project
features.summary: The Look section warns that in an HLG project a .cube LUT reads its values as Rec. 709.

features.name: Apply a LUT with an agent
features.summary: An agent imports the .cube with import_media, then sets it as a look by its media id.

features.name: What an adjustment clip is
features.summary: A clip with no picture of its own that grades everything already drawn behind it for as long as it lasts.

features.name: Insert Adjustment Clip
features.summary: One menu command places an adjustment clip, as one undo step named Add Adjustment Clip.

features.name: What an adjustment clip covers
features.summary: The new clip covers the In–Out range, or else the selected clips, or else the whole timeline.

features.name: Which track an adjustment clip goes on
features.summary: The new clip goes on the front track when it has room and isn't a matte track, otherwise on a new front track named Adjustment.

features.name: The full grade
features.summary: An adjustment clip's Color tab has Light, Color, Wheels, Curves and Look, plus Adjustment and Qualifier.

features.name: No Picture sub-tab
features.summary: An adjustment clip has nothing to place or crop, so its sub-tabs are Color and Clip.

features.name: Adjustment clip Strength
features.summary: Sets how much of the grade is mixed over the picture behind the clip.

features.name: No adjustment clips in nests
features.summary: An adjustment clip can't go inside a nest, and can't be nested.

features.name: No transitions or overlaps on adjustment clips
features.summary: An adjustment clip can't take a transition or overlap another clip on its track.

features.name: No blur, sharpen, pixelate or blend modes
features.summary: An adjustment clip can't take a blur, sharpen or pixelate filter or a blend mode, as it has no pixels of its own.

features.name: Grade a graphic
features.summary: Graphics have no Color sub-tab; put an adjustment clip above one to grade it.

features.name: Add an adjustment clip with an agent
features.summary: An agent places an adjustment clip on a named track at a named time, then grades it with set_video.

features.name: The Qualifier section
features.summary: Limits an adjustment clip's grade to the pixels behind it that match up to three ranges of hue, saturation and luma.

features.name: The Qualifier summary
features.summary: The section header says which ranges are on, for example hue · sat · inverted · blur 20%.

features.name: Turning a range on
features.summary: Turning a range's checkbox on starts the range at its default.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ range checkbox

features.name: Hue range
features.summary: Picks pixels by hue, on a strip of the colour spectrum.

features.name: Saturation range
features.summary: Picks pixels by saturation, on a strip from neutral to fully saturated.

features.name: Luma range
features.summary: Picks pixels by brightness, on a strip from black to white.

features.name: Low and High never cross
features.summary: A typed Low is held at or below High, and a typed High at or above Low.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Saturation or Luma ▸ Low, High

features.name: How ranges combine
features.summary: A pixel must fall inside every range that is on, and each range falls off smoothly across its softness outside each edge.

features.name: Reading a strip
features.summary: Each range has a strip that dims everything outside the range, the soft edges half as much, so you can see on the scale what is picked.

features.name: Dragging a strip
features.summary: A strip's block knobs set the width or the edges, its small squares the softness, and its band moves the whole range.
features.where: Qualifier strip: drag a block knob, a small square or the band

features.name: Fine drag on a qualifier strip
features.summary: Holding ⌥ moves a strip handle at a tenth of the speed.

features.name: Reset a range
features.summary: Double-clicking a strip resets the range to its default.

features.name: Invert a qualifier
features.summary: Grades everything except what the ranges pick.

features.name: Blur a qualifier's selection
features.summary: Blurs the selection, not the picture: a speckled selection on noisy footage turns clean and the grade blends into its surroundings.

features.name: Animate a qualifier
features.summary: An action can animate a qualifier's numbers.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier, with an action selected

features.name: Set a qualifier with an agent
features.summary: An agent sets a qualifier with set_video: it can turn a range on, change part of one, or turn one off.

features.name: Pick from Canvas
features.summary: Press the button and click the preview to centre the ranges on that colour.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas, then click the preview

features.name: What a pick sets on Hue
features.summary: Hue turns on if it was off and centres on the colour you clicked. Clicking a near-grey turns it off.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas

features.name: What a pick sets on Saturation
features.summary: The Saturation range is turned on if needed and centred on the colour's saturation.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas

features.name: What a pick sets on Luma
features.summary: Luma moves to the colour's brightness only if it was already on.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas

features.name: Width and softness are kept
features.summary: A range that was already on keeps its width and softness.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas

features.name: Cancelling a pick
features.summary: Esc or pressing the button again cancels the pick, and so does changing the selection.
features.where: Esc, or press Pick from Canvas again

features.name: One preview tool at a time
features.summary: Starting Pick from Canvas cancels any other tool waiting on the preview, and starting one of those cancels a pick.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas

features.name: A pick inside an action
features.summary: With an action selected, the picked ranges go to the action's end state.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas, with an action selected

features.name: Show Selection
features.summary: Draws the qualifier's selection in grey in place of the graded picture: white is fully graded, black untouched, grey in between.

features.name: The Selection tag
features.summary: A Selection tag appears in the preview's top-left corner while Show Selection is on.

features.name: It follows the selection
features.summary: Show Selection follows the first selected adjustment clip and turns off when none is selected.

features.name: Preview only
features.summary: It affects only this window's preview and the Preview Window, never an export or Save Frame….

features.name: Draw the selection with an agent
features.summary: An agent can render an adjustment clip's selection as grey.

features.name: Show Ungraded
features.summary: A before/after switch that shows this window's preview, and the Preview Window, as if no clip were graded.

features.name: The Ungraded tag
features.summary: An Ungraded tag appears in the preview's top-left corner while Show Ungraded is on.

features.name: What it leaves on
features.summary: A camera-log conversion on the media, filters, the chroma key and placement are not part of the grade, so they stay on.

features.name: Grade view tools are never saved
features.summary: Show Ungraded, Show Selection and the scopes affect only the window's preview, and nothing about them is saved or exported.

features.name: Draw an ungraded frame with an agent
features.summary: An agent can render a frame as if no clip were graded.

features.name: The Scopes panel
features.summary: A 248 pt column between the picture and the inspector that measures the picture while you grade.

features.name: Two slots and their popups
features.summary: The panel holds two stacked slots, each with a popup that picks one of four scopes.

features.name: The slot caption
features.summary: A faint caption at each slot's top right says what the scope reads.

features.name: Scopes in a short pane
features.summary: If the preview pane is too short for both slots they shrink together, and below 360 pt only the top slot shows.

features.name: Live scopes
features.summary: The scopes follow the picture live while it plays, and update after each edit while it's paused.

features.name: Scopes follow the preview
features.summary: Because they read the preview's frame, scopes follow Show Ungraded, Show Selection and Show SDR Version.

features.name: Measure scopes with an agent
features.summary: An agent measures any of the four scopes on any frame with render_frame, without opening the panel.

features.name: Waveform
features.summary: Shows the picture's luma (Y′) by position across the frame, left to right.
features.where: Scopes panel ▸ a slot's popup ▸ Waveform

features.name: RGB Parade
features.summary: Shows red, green and blue as three side-by-side waveforms, each with its own clip marks.
features.where: Scopes panel ▸ a slot's popup ▸ Parade

features.name: Clip marks
features.summary: Red marks on the top and bottom edges of the Waveform and Parade show where highlights and shadows clip.

features.name: Clipping readouts
features.summary: Under the Waveform and the Histogram, Highlights clipped and Shadows clipped show a share of the frame.
features.where: Scopes panel ▸ under a Waveform or Histogram slot

features.name: Measure the Waveform and Parade with an agent
features.summary: An agent measures a frame's waveform or parade and gets clipping figures and the raw counts.

features.name: Vectorscope
features.summary: Plots the picture's colour by hue and strength, with Cb running across and Cr up.
features.where: Scopes panel ▸ a slot's popup ▸ Vectorscope

features.name: Vectorscope targets
features.summary: Six boxes mark where the 75 % colour bars land: red, magenta, blue, cyan, green and yellow.

features.name: The skin line
features.summary: A line running up and to the left from the centre marks where skin tones fall.

features.name: Vectorscope zoom
features.summary: The 1× 2× 4× cells in the scope's bottom-right corner zoom in on a low-saturation picture, to show small casts.

features.name: Measure the Vectorscope with an agent
features.summary: An agent measures a frame's vectorscope and chooses its zoom.

features.name: Histogram
features.summary: Shows how many pixels sit at each level: red, green and blue counts as tinted fills, with luma as a white line.
features.where: Scopes panel ▸ a slot's popup ▸ Histogram

features.name: Measure the Histogram with an agent
features.summary: An agent measures a frame's histogram.

features.name: Grading inside an action
features.summary: With an action selected, a control change goes to the action's end state and ramps there from the clip's own value.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ action lane, then Clip tab ▸ Color

features.name: Row marks and the tab badge
features.summary: The row marks (◆) and the Color tab's ◆N badge show which settings the selected action animates.

features.name: What ramps smoothly
features.summary: Light, Color, wheels, Strength, the look's Amount and the qualifier's numbers ramp smoothly.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color, with an action selected

features.name: A hue centre takes the short way
features.summary: An animated qualifier hue centre takes the short way round the colour wheel.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier ▸ Hue, with an action selected

features.name: Curves animate
features.summary: Curves animate between any two curves, even with different numbers of points, and from or to a straight line.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Curves, with an action selected

features.name: Resetting a curve inside an action
features.summary: Inside an action, a channel's Reset or Set end value to default writes a straight curve to the action's end, so it animates back to neutral.

features.name: A look switches instead
features.summary: Turning a look on or off, or changing it, applies to the clip itself, not to the action, even with an action selected.

features.name: A qualifier range switches
features.summary: A range turned on or off in an action switches whole at its end.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier, with an action selected

features.name: Clear in a section header
features.summary: While an action animates a grade section, its header shows Clear in place of Reset, to take it out of the action.

features.name: Take one row out of an action
features.summary: Right-clicking a grade row offers Remove from action N or Set end value to default.

features.name: How a wheel disc shows an action
features.summary: The disc shows a hollow square at the action's start value, the puck in the action colour, and a coral mark at the playhead's value.

features.name: How a wheel strip shows an action
features.summary: The strip fills in the action colour from the start value, with a coral tick at the playhead's value.
