features.name: How the curve plot shows an action
features.summary: The plot shows the action's start curve dashed, and the edited curve and its points in the action colour.

features.name: How a qualifier strip shows an action
features.summary: The band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour.

features.name: How sliders show an action
features.summary: Grade sliders carry the same action marks as everywhere else in the inspector.

features.name: Copy a grade with Paste Attributes
features.summary: Copy a graded clip, select others and choose Paste Attributes: its video settings replace theirs in one undo step.
features.where: Edit ▸ Copy, then Edit ▸ Paste Attributes

features.name: Paste only some settings with an agent
features.summary: An agent can list which groups to paste, such as only the picture settings and not the sound.

features.name: A qualifier between clips
features.summary: Paste Attributes copies a qualifier only between adjustment clips.

features.name: When a paste stops
features.summary: If the copied clip has a blur, sharpen or pixelate filter or a blend mode, a paste onto an adjustment clip shows an error.

features.name: LUTs travel with a paste
features.summary: Pasting a clip with a LUT look into another project brings the LUT into that project's media.
features.where: Edit ▸ Paste or Edit ▸ Paste Attributes

features.name: Automatic source conversion
features.summary: Each frame of a source is converted once into the colour the project works in, so most footage needs no setting.

features.name: SDR-only projects stay untouched
features.summary: An SDR project holding only Rec. 709 sources isn't converted at all: its pixels and labels stay exactly as they are.

features.name: Rec. 709 and untagged sources
features.summary: Rec. 709 or unlabelled video, stills and recordings are drawn as they are in SDR and lifted to reference white in HDR (HLG).

features.name: HLG video
features.summary: HLG video such as iPhone HDR has its highlights rolled off in an SDR project and kept above white in an HDR (HLG) project.

features.name: PQ / HDR10 video
features.summary: A PQ (HDR10) file rolls off at its own peak in an SDR project and becomes real HDR, up to 1,000 cd/m², in HDR (HLG).

features.name: Wide-gamut SDR sources
features.summary: A BT.2020 or P3 D65 source with an SDR transfer curve is converted to the project's colours, not drawn with the wrong ones.

features.name: sRGB-transfer sources
features.summary: A source labelled with the sRGB transfer is read as sRGB rather than as Rec. 709.

features.name: Full-range files
features.summary: S-Log3 and V-Log files stored in full range are read as full range, from the flag in the file.

features.name: Camera log in each kind of project
features.summary: Log footage with a built-in Camera Log curve looks normal in an SDR project and becomes real HDR in an HDR (HLG) project.

features.name: HDR stills
features.summary: A PNG or HEIC still labelled HLG or PQ is treated as HDR, the way a video of the same kind is, rather than read as SDR.

features.name: Gain-map HDR photos
features.summary: An iPhone HDR photo with a gain map shows its HDR highlights in an HDR (HLG) project and its ordinary picture in SDR.

features.name: The same conversion everywhere
features.summary: The conversion is the same in the preview, every export and saved frames, and filmstrips and thumbnails follow it.

features.name: Show Ungraded keeps the conversion
features.summary: View ▸ Show Ungraded turns off the grades but leaves the source conversion on, because the conversion is how the file is read.

features.name: Camera Log section
features.summary: The Media tab's Camera Log section tells Frame Job which curve a video file was shot with, so flat log footage displays correctly.

features.name: A setting on the file
features.summary: Camera Log is set on the media file, so every clip of that file follows it, reversed clips included.

features.name: Camera Log undo step
features.summary: Changing a file's Camera Log is one undo step, named Camera Log.

features.name: Camera Log status line and header
features.summary: A line under the Log popup says what's set and whether it came from the file, and the section's header repeats the setting.

features.name: Log popup: None
features.summary: No conversion: the file shows its log picture as recorded.
features.where: Media tab ▸ Camera Log ▸ Log ▸ None

features.name: Log popup: Apple Log
features.summary: Converts footage shot in Apple Log, using the Apple Log curve and the BT.2020 camera gamut.
features.where: Media tab ▸ Camera Log ▸ Log ▸ Apple Log

features.name: Log popup: Apple Log 2
features.summary: Converts footage shot in Apple Log 2, which is the Apple Log curve with Apple Wide Gamut.
features.where: Media tab ▸ Camera Log ▸ Log ▸ Apple Log 2

features.name: Log popup: S-Log3
features.summary: Converts Sony S-Log3 footage, with two rows for its gamut: S-Log3 / S-Gamut3.Cine and S-Log3 / S-Gamut3.

features.name: Log popup: V-Log
features.summary: Converts Panasonic V-Log footage with V-Gamut, shown as V-Log / V-Gamut.
features.where: Media tab ▸ Camera Log ▸ Log ▸ V-Log / V-Gamut

features.name: Log popup: C-Log2
features.summary: Converts Canon Log 2 footage, with two rows for its gamut: C-Log2 / Cinema Gamut and C-Log2 / BT.2020.

features.name: Log popup: C-Log3
features.summary: Converts Canon Log 3 footage, with two rows for its gamut: C-Log3 / Cinema Gamut and C-Log3 / BT.2020.

features.name: How a curve is displayed
features.summary: Each built-in curve follows its maker's published curve and gamut, and Frame Job's display transform turns it into a normal-looking picture.

features.name: Detection on import
features.summary: An iPhone Apple Log or Apple Log 2 file is recognised by its label when you import it, so it looks like normal video straight away.

features.name: Thumbnails follow Camera Log
features.summary: Changing a file's Camera Log redraws its Media tab thumbnails and timeline filmstrip to show the converted picture.

features.name: Camera Log runs before the grade
features.summary: The conversion happens before the chroma key and every grade step, and Show Ungraded keeps it.

features.name: Which files take Camera Log
features.summary: Camera Log is for video files only: the popup is disabled for an audio file, an image or a LUT.

features.name: Set Camera Log with an agent
features.summary: Agents set or clear a file's Camera Log with set_media_color, and read it back from get_project.

features.name: Use LUT…
features.summary: Use LUT… picks a .cube file, adds it to the project and makes it this file's log conversion to Rec. 709, in one undo step.
features.where: Media tab ▸ Camera Log ▸ Log ▸ Use LUT…

features.name: A LUT already in the project
features.summary: Each .cube LUT already in the project is offered in the Log popup as LUT: name, so other files can use it as their conversion.
features.where: Media tab ▸ Camera Log ▸ Log ▸ LUT: name

features.name: A Camera Log LUT counts as used
features.summary: A LUT that is some file's Camera Log counts as used: Unused only hides it, and Remove asks first.

features.name: Removing a Camera Log LUT
features.summary: Removing a LUT in use says how many files lose it, and Remove and Clear Camera Log sends them back to no conversion.
features.where: Media tab ▸ right-click the LUT ▸ Remove

features.name: Camera Log and looks: converting twice
features.summary: Camera Log is applied before any look, and the Look section warns when a .cube look sits on a file Camera Log converts.

features.name: Peak read at import
features.summary: Import reads a PQ file's peak from its HDR10 metadata, so its highlights roll off to white at the brightness the file names.

features.name: HDR10 section
features.summary: The Media tab's HDR10 section shows and changes the selected PQ file's peak.

features.name: Peak
features.summary: Typing a value in Peak overrides the brightness a PQ file's highlights roll off to white at.

features.name: Use File's
features.summary: Use File's clears the override and goes back to the peak the file's HDR10 metadata names.

features.name: Where the peak came from
features.summary: A line under the controls says where the peak came from.

features.name: PQ Peak undo step
features.summary: Each peak change is one undo step, PQ Peak, and in the app changing the peak or the Camera Log keeps the other.

features.name: Set a PQ peak with an agent
features.summary: Agents set a PQ file's peak with set_media_color's peak, and read the file's own reading from get_project.

features.name: Limits of the peak
features.summary: Only a PQ file has a peak, and it's read once, at import, so relinking the file doesn't read it again.

features.name: Dynamic Range
features.summary: The Document tab's Dynamic Range popup sets whether the project works in SDR (Rec. 709, the default) or HDR (HLG).

features.name: Dynamic Range undo step
features.summary: Switching the project's dynamic range is one undo step, Dynamic Range.

features.name: Colour row in the Document section
features.summary: The Document section's Colour row shows the project's dynamic range.

features.name: The HDR (HLG) working space
features.summary: An HDR project composes every frame in HLG-encoded BT.2020, so HDR footage keeps its range through to the file.
features.where: Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Dynamic Range ▸ HDR (HLG)

features.name: SDR material lifted to reference white
features.summary: In an HDR (HLG) project SDR material is lifted so its white sits at HDR reference white, and HDR highlights rise above it.

features.name: Drawn layers and generated content
features.summary: In an HDR (HLG) project text, captions, shapes, SDR stills, graphics and background colours are lifted to reference white.

features.name: Grades keep their settings
features.summary: Switching dynamic range changes no grade value.

features.name: The chroma key across a switch
features.summary: A chroma key keeps keying the colour it was picked on after a switch to HDR (HLG), exactly or very nearly.

features.name: Pick from Canvas in an HDR project
features.summary: In an HDR (HLG) project Pick from Canvas stores the key colour as an SDR project shows it.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Chroma Key ▸ Pick from Canvas

features.name: Qualifiers read the HLG signal
features.summary: An adjustment clip's qualifier ranges are measured on the HLG values in an HDR (HLG) project, so re-pick them after switching.

features.name: Show SDR Version
features.summary: View ▸ Show SDR Version puts the project's SDR version in the preview: the picture 8-bit formats and JPEG frames get.

features.name: It belongs to the window
features.summary: Show SDR Version belongs to the window: it reaches the preview and the Preview Window, and never an export or a saved frame.

features.name: The SDR Version tag
features.summary: A tag reading "SDR Version" sits in the preview's top-left corner while the view is on.

features.name: What the SDR version is
features.summary: The SDR version brings the HLG master back to Rec. 709, unchanged to a little below reference white, with highlights rolled off.

features.name: Draw the SDR version with an agent
features.summary: An agent draws the same picture with render_frame's sdr_version.

features.name: Scopes read the HLG signal
features.summary: In an HDR (HLG) project View ▸ Scopes reads the HLG signal, with scales and targets to match.

features.name: Waveform and Parade in cd/m²
features.summary: In an HDR (HLG) project the Waveform and Parade label every line in cd/m²: 0, 10, 51, 203 and 1000 at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %.

features.name: The reference white line
features.summary: The 75 % line, HDR reference white, is dashed: titles and SDR material sit on it, and HDR highlights rise above it.

features.name: BT.2020 luma and vectorscope targets
features.summary: In an HDR (HLG) project luma and the vectorscope use BT.2020's weights, and the vectorscope's targets are BT.2020's too.

features.name: Scope captions in an HDR project
features.summary: Each scope slot's caption names what it reads.

features.name: HDR scope numbers for agents
features.summary: In an HDR (HLG) project each scope's JSON from render_frame adds the signal, and the Waveform, Parade and Histogram add a scale.

features.name: Blending
features.summary: The Document tab's Blending popup sets how layers mix where they overlap: in opacity, dissolves, soft edges, blend modes and glows.

features.name: Encoded
features.summary: Layers blend on their encoded values, as most editors do.

features.name: Linear light
features.summary: Layers blend as light, so a dissolve between saturated clips keeps its brightness instead of dipping dark at the midpoint.
features.where: Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Blending ▸ Linear light

features.name: What Blending leaves alone
features.summary: Blending changes no clip and no grade, so a grade looks the same either way.

features.name: Dynamic Range on the export sheet
features.summary: In an HDR (HLG) project the export sheet gets a Dynamic Range row under Format: HDR (HLG), HDR10 (PQ) or SDR version.

features.name: HDR (HLG)
features.summary: Writes the BT.2100 HLG master, the row's default.

features.name: HDR10 (PQ)
features.summary: Writes an HDR10 file: BT.2100 PQ mastered at 1,000 cd/m², with fixed mastering metadata.

features.name: SDR version
features.summary: Writes the project's SDR version in Rec. 709.
features.where: File ▸ Export… ▸ Dynamic Range ▸ SDR version

features.name: Which formats carry HDR
features.summary: Six formats can carry an HDR picture, each at 10 bits or more, and every other video format writes the SDR version.

features.name: VP9 and HDR
features.summary: VP9 (WebM) writes HLG and HDR10 as 10-bit VP9 Profile 2, and the SDR version as 8-bit Profile 0.

features.name: Fixed HDR10 metadata
features.summary: An HDR10 file carries fixed metadata that is always accurate, because its picture never goes above 1,000 cd/m².

features.name: HDR export errors for agents
features.summary: An agent asking export for a picture the format or project can't carry gets a message saying what will work.

features.name: See which picture an export wrote
features.summary: Once export_status reports a video job done in an HDR (HLG) project, its dynamic_range names the picture written.

features.name: 16-bit float compositing
features.summary: Every video source is decoded and every frame composited at 16-bit float, so gradients from a 10-bit file survive grading.

features.name: 10-bit exports
features.summary: HEVC 10-bit, both AV1 formats and ProRes keep the depth, VP9 (WebM) for HLG and HDR10 only; other video formats are 8-bit.

features.name: Deep stills
features.summary: A still deeper than 8 bits per channel, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC, is drawn at 16-bit float.

features.name: What stays 8-bit
features.summary: Text, shapes, captions, graphics, thumbnails and screen recordings are 8-bit, and still sit at reference white in HDR (HLG).

features.name: Graphic clips
features.summary: A motion graphic that sits on a track like any clip, drawn fresh on every frame by a small JavaScript module kept in your project.

features.name: Modules
features.summary: A module is one file in your project, graphics/<name>.js, that draws an SVG picture for any frame Frame Job asks for.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder

features.name: Clips sharing one module
features.summary: Many clips can be drawn by one module, each with its own property values, size and timeline.

features.name: Graphic properties
features.summary: Each property a module declares becomes a control in the inspector, and a value you don't set draws with the module's own default.

features.name: Same frame, same pixels
features.summary: A graphic always draws the same pixels for the same frame and settings, so the preview and an export show the same graphic.

features.name: Module names
features.summary: A module's name is its file name without .js: lowercase letters, digits and -, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.

features.name: Gradients don't band
features.summary: A fixed, very fine pattern keeps dark gradients shading smoothly. Choose 10-bit or ProRes to keep that in an export.

features.name: The graphics folder
features.summary: Each project keeps its graphics in a graphics/ folder inside the .framejob package, holding modules, fonts/, assets/ and history/.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder

features.name: Graphics in an untitled project
features.summary: An unsaved project can use graphics: they are kept in a temporary folder and move into the package when you first save it.

features.name: Templates are copied into the project
features.summary: Inserting a template writes your own editable copy into graphics/ under a free name, so each insert can be edited on its own.

features.name: A graphics-only timeline
features.summary: A timeline of nothing but graphics, text, shapes and images still plays and exports.

features.name: Graphics in HDR projects
features.summary: In an HDR (HLG) project, graphics draw at reference white, 203 cd/m², so a white graphic matches SDR white.

features.name: Graphics limits
features.summary: The fixed limits in one list, such as 8192 pixels a side, 64 property values a clip and 10 kept versions of each module.

features.name: The Insert Graphic sheet
features.summary: A sheet for choosing a bundled template, a project graphic or a file of your own, with categories, a list and a looping preview.

features.name: Graphic categories
features.summary: The left list files graphics by category, with This Project first when your project holds a module.

features.name: The graphics list
features.summary: The middle list shows the chosen category's graphics sorted by title, with a module that doesn't compile in grey.

features.name: The looping preview
features.summary: The chosen graphic plays on a loop over a checkerboard, at the project's canvas shape, with its title and one-line description under it.

features.name: Insert a graphic
features.summary: Insert, Return or a double-click on a graphic places the chosen graphic at the playhead, selects the new clip and closes the sheet.

features.name: Cancel the Insert Graphic sheet
features.summary: Cancel or Esc closes the sheet without changing anything.

features.name: Insert from This Project
features.summary: Choosing a graphic under This Project places another clip drawn by that module, with nothing copied.

features.name: Insert from a file
features.summary: From File… closes the sheet so you can pick a .js module to copy in and place, or a .fjgraphic package to import.

features.name: How From File… names a module
features.summary: From File… names the module after the file you chose, changed as needed to make a valid name that isn't taken.

features.name: Where an inserted graphic lands
features.summary: An inserted graphic goes at the playhead on the front track if it fits there, otherwise on a new track above everything.

features.name: Default length and size
features.summary: A new clip takes the length and size its module gives, otherwise 5 seconds and the canvas's size.

features.name: A module that doesn't compile
features.summary: If the module doesn't compile, no clip is placed and Frame Job shows its first error, with the line when it knows it.

features.name: A graphic clip on the timeline
features.summary: A graphic clip is teal with no thumbnails, and its strip shows a {} symbol and reads Graphic until you name it.

features.name: The 23 bundled templates
features.summary: Frame Job ships 23 ready-made graphics in four categories, drawn by code and fully editable once inserted.

features.name: Templates at any canvas shape
features.summary: Seventeen templates stay inside the title-safe area in landscape, portrait and square, fitting or wrapping long text.

features.name: Templates end clean
features.summary: Seventeen templates have an accent colour and leave in about their last 15 frames, so the last frame is bare.

features.name: Template fonts and glyphs
features.summary: Templates use bundled fonts and generic vector glyphs only, never a brand's artwork.

features.name: Arrow highlight
features.summary: A rounded box drawn on around a spot, an arrow growing toward it from the side nearer the frame's centre, and a label at the arrow's tail.

features.name: Bar chart
features.summary: A titled bar chart whose bars grow in turn, from comma-separated values and labels.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Data & Time ▸ Bar chart

features.name: Callout
features.summary: A circle that draws itself round a spot on the frame, with an arrow and a label.

features.name: Chapter card
features.summary: A full-frame card with a large outlined chapter number, a kicker, an accent rule drawing across and the title rising into view.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Titles & Text ▸ Chapter card

features.name: Countdown
features.summary: A timer counting down or up one step a second inside a ring that empties or fills, pulsing each second and flashing at the end.

features.name: Counter
features.summary: A number counting from one value to another with thousands separators, a prefix and a label.

features.name: Donut chart
features.summary: A titled donut whose slices sweep in turn, the first slice's share counting up in the centre, with a legend.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Data & Time ▸ Donut chart

features.name: End screen
features.summary: A full-frame card with a title, two 16:9 placeholders for the video elements you add when you publish, and a subscribe circle.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Social & YouTube ▸ End screen

features.name: Gauge
features.summary: A 270° dial whose accent arc and needle swing to a value while the figure counts up, with its units and a label.

features.name: Handle tag
features.summary: An accent tile holding a generic glyph and a pill with your @handle, at a corner.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Social & YouTube ▸ Handle tag

features.name: Keyboard keys
features.summary: A shortcut such as cmd+shift+4 drawn as keycaps that pop in and are pressed in turn, with a label under them.

features.name: Kinetic type
features.summary: A sentence shown word by word, each word springing in, with an accent colour.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Titles & Text ▸ Kinetic type

features.name: Line chart
features.summary: A titled line drawn on through comma-separated values, a dot popping at each point, an optional area fill and the last value called out.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Data & Time ▸ Line chart

features.name: Logo reveal
features.summary: A full-frame card on which an accent bar sweeps across to reveal your logo or a text mark, then settles into a rule over a tagline.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Titles & Text ▸ Logo reveal

features.name: Lower third
features.summary: A name and subtitle that slide in from the left and fade out, with or without a dark box, placed left, centre or right.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Titles & Text ▸ Lower third

features.name: News ticker
features.summary: A band along the foot of the frame with a headline box and items, typed with | between them, crawling right to left.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Titles & Text ▸ News ticker

features.name: Progress bar
features.summary: A labelled bar on a plate whose fill grows to a percentage, the figure counting, with a shine across it, at the bottom, centre or top.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Data & Time ▸ Progress bar

features.name: Quote card
features.summary: A full-frame card with a large quote mark, the quote's lines fading up in turn, and the attribution sliding in.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Titles & Text ▸ Quote card

features.name: Social popup
features.summary: A notification card at a corner with a generic avatar and handle, its heart, bubble or share arrow popping as the count goes up by one.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Social & YouTube ▸ Social popup

features.name: Step badge
features.summary: A numbered accent circle popping in at a corner, with a label panel wiping out from behind it.

features.name: Subscribe button
features.summary: A button a cursor clicks: it turns grey with a check and its done label, then a bell pops in beside it and rings after a second click.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Social & YouTube ▸ Subscribe button

features.name: Title card
features.summary: A title fitted to the frame with a kicker above it, over a two-colour gradient. The text fades in and out, and the gradient stays.
features.where: Insert ▸ Graphic… ▸ Titles & Text ▸ Title card

features.name: Window frame
features.summary: A browser or app window's frame, with a title bar, three dots and a title or address field, to sit over a recording on the track below.

features.name: Export a graphic
features.summary: Export… saves the chosen graphic as a .fjgraphic file holding its module and only the project fonts and pictures it uses.

features.name: What a package finds to pack
features.summary: To find the fonts and pictures a graphic uses, Frame Job draws it and packs what it saw, so check the file list after an export.

features.name: The .fjgraphic file
features.summary: A package is an uncompressed zip of a manifest, the module, fonts/ and assets/, and two exports by one version are byte-identical.

features.name: Open a .fjgraphic from the Finder
features.summary: Double-click a .fjgraphic, use Open With, drop it on the Dock icon or open it from a browser's downloads to import it.

features.name: Import with From File…
features.summary: Choosing a .fjgraphic with From File… puts up the Import Graphic sheet for that same project.

features.name: The Import Graphic sheet
features.summary: Before anything is copied, a sheet shows the graphic's title and description, and what will happen to its module, fonts and pictures.

features.name: After an import
features.summary: Import copies the files into graphics/ and opens the Insert Graphic sheet on This Project with the graphic chosen, ready to insert.

features.name: Name clashes on import
features.summary: An import never replaces a file: identical files are reused, a different module or font gets a new name, and a different picture stops it.

features.name: Package checks
features.summary: Frame Job checks a package before copying anything, and a damaged, compressed, altered or newer one isn't imported. The message says why.

features.name: The Graphic sub-tab
features.summary: When every selected clip is a graphic, the Clip tab gains a Graphic sub-tab with Source, Properties, Size and Timeline sections.

features.name: The Picture sub-tab on a graphic
features.summary: A graphic has the usual layer settings, such as Transform, Shadow and Filters, so you can move and fade it, but no Crop or Chroma Key.

features.name: The Clip sub-tab on a graphic
features.summary: A graphic has Timing, Transition and Motion presets in the Clip sub-tab, but no Speed section.

features.name: Name, File and Revision
features.summary: The Source section shows what draws the clip: its Name, File and Revision.

features.name: Open in Editor
features.summary: Open in Editor opens the module in the app your Mac uses for .js files; save there and the preview redraws within a moment.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Open in Editor

features.name: Reveal in Finder
features.summary: Reveal in Finder shows the module's file.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder

features.name: A missing module
features.summary: When the module file is gone, Source shows an error, Revision reads missing and its buttons are dimmed.

features.name: Errors and warnings in Source
features.summary: Under the buttons, Source lists what the module says about the clip: compile errors and warnings, then what its first frame reported.

features.name: Open a diagnostic
features.summary: Click a diagnostic, or its Open button, to open the module in your editor. This opens the file, not the line.

features.name: Problems in the graphics folder
features.summary: Under In the graphics folder, Source lists what Frame Job skipped or couldn't watch, each with a Reveal button.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ In the graphics folder

features.name: Several modules selected
features.summary: When the selected clips are drawn by different modules, Source names them and asks you to select one module's clips to edit its properties.

features.name: Move clips to another module
features.summary: To move clips to a module that already exists, delete them and insert that module again, or have an agent do it with set_graphic.

features.name: Property rows
features.summary: One row appears per property the module declares, in the module's own order, with the module's label and its help text as the tooltip.

features.name: Number properties
features.summary: A number property is a value field, with a slider when the module gives both a minimum and a maximum.

features.name: Text properties
features.summary: A text property is a one-line field the width of the inspector, or a text area when the module marks it multi-line.

features.name: Checkbox properties
features.summary: A property that's either on or off is a checkbox.

features.name: Pop-up properties
features.summary: A property with a fixed list of choices is a pop-up of the module's options.

features.name: Colour properties
features.summary: A colour property is a swatch that opens the macOS colour panel, and a colour you can see through keeps its opacity.

features.name: Picture properties
features.summary: A picture property is a pop-up of None, every picture in the project's graphics, and any name referred to but missing from the folder.

features.name: Reset a graphic's properties
features.summary: Reset on the Properties header clears every value stored on the selected clips, so the module draws its own defaults.

features.name: A value at the default is not stored
features.summary: With no action selected, setting a value back to the module's default clears it, so the clip follows that default if it changes later.

features.name: Edit several clips of one module
features.summary: With several clips of one module selected, a change to a property row applies to all of them.

features.name: Leftover values
features.summary: A value for a property the module no longer has stays listed, dimmed, below the rows, with ⌫ to remove it.

features.name: Width and Height
features.summary: Width and Height set the size a graphic draws at, 1 to 8192 pixels a side, so text and shapes stay sharp.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Size ▸ Width, Height

features.name: Fit to Canvas
features.summary: Fit to Canvas sets the size to the canvas's and centres the clip at scale 1.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Size ▸ Fit to Canvas

features.name: The graphic's own timeline
features.summary: A graphic has a timeline of its own, counted from its first frame, shown in the Timeline section.

features.name: The graphic's In point
features.summary: In shows the graphic frame the clip's first frame shows. You can't type it: trimming the front, rolling and splitting move it.

features.name: Pin a graphic's Length
features.summary: Typing a Length pins the graphic's own timeline, so the animation keeps its pace when the clip's length changes.

features.name: Follow Clip
features.summary: With Follow Clip on, the default, the graphic's timeline ends when the clip ends, so lengthening the clip moves its outro to the new end.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Timeline ▸ Follow Clip

features.name: Length pinned shorter than the clip
features.summary: When Length is pinned shorter than the clip, frames keep counting past it but the graphic's progress stays at its end.

features.name: Trim a graphic like footage
features.summary: Trimming the front of a graphic clip cuts into its animation, and trimming the end never changes a pinned Length.

features.name: Graphics and transitions
features.summary: A transition that gives a graphic clip extra frames at its head moves In back by the same amount, so the picture stays in step.

features.name: Graphics and a frame-rate change
features.summary: Changing the project's frame rate snaps In and a pinned Length to the nearest frame on the new grid.

features.name: Canvas-sized graphics are re-sized
features.summary: Make Vertical Version re-sizes a graphic exactly the old canvas's size to the new canvas, so it lays itself out again on the new frame.

features.name: Templates measured by the short side
features.summary: Every bundled template measures itself by the short side of the size it draws at, so it fits a tall frame.

features.name: Older template copies are updated
features.summary: Older copies of six templates are recognised, and rewritten with the current template in the copy that Make a copy opens.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Make a copy

features.name: Your own height-sized modules are named
features.summary: A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height (ctx.height / 1080) is named in the summary, as it may not fit the frame.

features.name: Animate a graphic's properties
features.summary: Add an action to a graphic clip, select it, and set in the Graphic sub-tab the values its properties should end at.

features.name: Numbers and colours ramp
features.summary: Across an action, numbers and colours move along the action's curve, with colours blending through OKLab.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties, action selected

features.name: Text, checkboxes, menus and pictures switch
features.summary: Text, checkboxes, pop-ups and pictures hold their value through an action, then change as it ends. Their rows say "at end".
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties, action selected

features.name: Keep a property out of animation
features.summary: A module can mark a property animate: false, so no action animates it. Its row shows ⊘ and edits the clip even with an action selected.

features.name: Action values must fit the module
features.summary: A value you put in an action is checked against the module as it is now, including any minimum and maximum.

features.name: Where an animated property starts
features.summary: An action starts from the value in force, or, if the clip holds none, from the module's default when an action first names it.

features.name: The ◆N badge
features.summary: The Graphic sub-tab shows a ◆N badge counting how many properties the selected action animates.

features.name: Paste Graphic Properties
features.summary: Pastes a copied graphic clip's properties, text and colours included, onto every selected clip drawn by the same graphic.

features.name: Paste Attributes leaves graphic properties alone
features.summary: Paste Attributes copies a clip's look, such as its position and opacity, and never carries a graphic's properties.

features.name: Copying a graphic clip
features.summary: Copying and pasting a graphic clip pastes a clip that names its module; the module's .js file, fonts and pictures are not copied.

features.name: Add Font to Graphics
features.summary: Copies a .ttf or .otf file into the project's graphics/fonts/ folder, and every graphic in the project can then use it.

features.name: Exact font family names
features.summary: A module must use the family name Frame Job reads from the font file, which can differ from the name Font Book shows.

features.name: Bundled fonts
features.summary: Graphics can draw with seven bundled families on every Mac, with nothing to install.

features.name: Generic font families
features.summary: serif, sans-serif and monospace draw in bundled faces: Source Serif 4, Source Sans 3 and IBM Plex Mono.

features.name: System fonts are never used
features.summary: Graphics never use the fonts installed on your Mac, only the bundled ones and those you add, so a project draws the same everywhere.

features.name: Add Image to Graphics
features.summary: Copies a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ picture into graphics/assets/, where a module can draw it and a picture property lists it.

features.name: Picture names made legal
features.summary: A picture whose name a module can't refer to is added under a legal name, and a notice says which.

features.name: Dropping files in the folder
features.summary: Fonts and pictures may also be put straight into graphics/fonts/ and graphics/assets/ with the Finder or any tool.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder

features.name: Edit in any editor
features.summary: A module is an ordinary file in the project package's graphics/ folder, so you can edit it in any editor or with your own tools.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder

features.name: Live reload
features.summary: When a module, font or picture changes, the paused preview redraws and the inspector updates within a moment, with no reimport.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Open in Editor

features.name: How many files are watched
features.summary: Frame Job watches the graphics folder, its fonts/ and assets/ folders, and the first 16 files one by one.

features.name: Reading a module's errors and warnings
features.summary: An error means nothing drew and a warning means the graphic drew anyway, each with its line and column when they're known.

features.name: The error card
features.summary: A graphic that fails draws a dark red error card in its own box, in place of the graphic, in the preview and in stills.

features.name: Kept versions
features.summary: Whenever Frame Job sees a module's code replaced while the project is open, it keeps the old code, up to the last 10 versions.

features.name: API.md and API.d.ts beside your modules
features.summary: Frame Job keeps the reference and its TypeScript definitions in graphics/, for an editor or an agent working in the folder.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder

features.name: Rename Graphic
features.summary: Renames a module, and every clip drawn by it, on the timeline and inside nests, follows the new name.

features.name: Undo a rename
features.summary: When a clip uses the module, undo puts the clips and the module's file back under the old name, and redo moves both forward.

features.name: Delete Graphic
features.summary: Deletes a module no clip uses, keeping its code so it can be restored.

features.name: Restore Graphic Version
features.summary: Puts back the newest kept version of a module's code, deleted modules included.

features.name: Duplicate as New Graphic
features.summary: Writes a copy of the module under a new name and switches the selected clips to it, so you can change one clip's look alone.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Duplicate as New Graphic…

features.name: When a rename, delete or restore can't go ahead
features.summary: These sheets close without a message on success. When Frame Job can't do it, it beeps, gives the reason and leaves the sheet open.
features.where: File ▸ Rename Graphic…, Delete Graphic…, Restore Graphic Version…

features.name: Show video inside a graphic
features.summary: Put a graphic on the track directly above a video and make its track a matte, and the video shows only where the graphic draws.

features.name: Drawing ahead while playing
features.summary: While a preview plays forward, Frame Job draws upcoming graphic frames on spare processor cores ahead of the playhead.

features.name: Kept frames
features.summary: A window keeps the graphic frames it has drawn in memory while it is open, so a stretch you play again comes from memory.

features.name: The memory budget
features.summary: Frames drawn ahead and frames kept share one budget, a quarter of your Mac's physical memory, and less when memory is short.

features.name: Repeat frames skip the draw
features.summary: When a frame's SVG matches one already drawn, such as during a hold or in a static graphic, Frame Job reuses that picture.

features.name: The picture cache
features.summary: PNG and JPEG pictures a graphic draws are decoded once and cached, so image-heavy graphics draw faster.

features.name: Background render
features.summary: When you leave Frame Job alone, the window you last played or moved the playhead in draws its graphics ahead of the paused playhead.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Playback ▸ Background render

features.name: Start after … seconds
features.summary: How long Frame Job must be left alone before Background render starts, from 1 to 60 seconds, 5 by default.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Playback ▸ Start after … seconds

features.name: What stops Background render
features.summary: Any activity in Frame Job stops the pass at once, and it starts again after the same wait.

features.name: Exports keep the code they started with
features.summary: An export draws each graphic as its module stood when you started or queued it, whatever you edit next.

features.name: Parallel rendering
features.summary: An export draws its graphics ahead on worker threads, one fewer than the Mac's active cores.

features.name: A broken graphic stops an export starting
features.summary: An export that would draw a missing module or one that doesn't compile isn't started, and the message names each graphic and its error.

features.name: A graphic failing mid-export
features.summary: A graphic that fails partway through stops the export at that frame, names the graphic, and writes no file.

features.name: Graphic warnings in an export
features.summary: Warnings a graphic gives while drawing don't stop the export, and a finished export reports each one with its name and frame.

features.name: The frozen clock
features.summary: The clock inside a graphic is frozen, so nothing depends on when it's drawn and an export matches the preview.

features.name: Make a graphic with an agent
features.summary: An agent can read the API, write a module, look at it, add fonts and pictures, place it, change it, animate it and check the frame.

features.name: Read the API
features.summary: graphic_reference returns the whole graphics API as Markdown, for an agent to read once before writing a graphic.

features.name: Write a module
features.summary: write_graphic saves graphics/<name>.js, compiles it and reports the result, so an agent can fix it and write again.

features.name: Look at frames on a contact sheet
features.summary: render_graphic draws a module without placing a clip: up to 16 frames on a PNG contact sheet, each frame's number under it.

features.name: One frame's SVG
features.summary: render_graphic with format svg returns one frame's SVG text, its problems and the ctx it was drawn with.

features.name: List and insert graphics
features.summary: list_graphics lists what the Insert Graphic sheet shows, in its order, and insert_graphic is its Insert.

features.name: Place a graphic clip with an agent
features.summary: add_graphic_clip places a clip drawn by a module already in graphics/ on a chosen track and time.

features.name: Change graphic clips with an agent
features.summary: set_graphic changes what graphic clips are drawn from: another module, the size, the length or the properties.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties, Size, Timeline

features.name: Read a module or the folder
features.summary: get_graphic reads one module, or with no name lists the whole graphics folder.

features.name: Edit the folder with file tools
features.summary: An agent may also edit the graphics folder with its own file tools, and the app sees the change within a moment.

features.name: What undo covers for an agent
features.summary: File writes in graphics/ are not undo steps and don't mark the project edited, while placing and changing clips are undo steps.

features.name: Graphics in render_frame
features.summary: When a graphic in the frame failed or warned, render_frame names it, its frame and the problem, and a failed one draws its error card.

features.name: The Assistant and graphics
features.summary: The Assistant tab can write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics.

features.name: The shape of a module
features.summary: A graphic is one JavaScript ES module exporting render, with optional meta and schema, and render returns an SVG string for each frame.

features.name: A module's meta
features.summary: A module's meta gives its name, a new clip's default length and size, and a category and description for the Insert Graphic sheet.

features.name: The ctx argument
features.summary: render receives ctx with the project's frame rate, the time, the graphic's length and progress, and the sizes.

features.name: Resolution-independent drawing
features.summary: Writing every coordinate against ctx.width and ctx.height lets one graphic draw at any size or shape.

features.name: The schema
features.summary: A module's schema declares its properties, which become inspector controls and the props render receives.

features.name: Property types
features.summary: A schema entry's type is string, number, boolean, color, enum or asset.

features.name: Stored values that don't fit
features.summary: props always has every schema key, and a stored value that doesn't fit gives a warning: the default is drawn and the frame still draws.

features.name: The SVG the engine draws
features.summary: Frame Job draws render's SVG with resvg, including text, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG images, and compressed SVGZ.

features.name: The sandbox
features.summary: A graphic runs in a sandbox with no import, eval, Function, Math.random, fetch, files, clock, performance, WebAssembly or Intl.

features.name: Modern JavaScript
features.summary: Modern syntax works in a module, such as template literals, ??, ?., destructuring and replaceAll.

features.name: The time budget
features.summary: Each frame has 250 ms to draw in the preview and 2 s in an export, so a runaway graphic reports an error instead of hanging.

features.name: Size and memory limits
features.summary: Each module gets 64 MiB of heap and 1 MiB of stack, a graphic is at most 8192 pixels a side, and its SVG at most 8 MiB.

features.name: The graphics reference
features.summary: Help ▸ Graphics Reference opens the whole graphics API reference in your default Markdown app, with or without a project open.

features.name: svg()
features.summary: svg(ctx, body, {background}) writes the root element with the right size and viewBox.

features.name: interpolate()
features.summary: interpolate maps a value through matching input and output ranges.

features.name: Easing
features.summary: Easing gives ready-made curves for interpolate.

features.name: spring()
features.summary: spring gives a physical spring from one value to another.

features.name: interpolateColors()
features.summary: interpolateColors blends colours in OKLab, so a blend looks even.

features.name: random()
features.summary: random(seed) returns a repeatable number from 0 up to, but not including, 1, from a number or string seed.

features.name: noise2D() and noise3D()
features.summary: noise2D and noise3D give smooth simplex noise for organic motion.

features.name: Path helpers
features.summary: getLength, getPointAtLength and evolvePath measure an SVG path and draw it on.

features.name: measureText()
features.summary: measureText(text, font) measures text with the same fonts the graphic draws.

features.name: wrapText()
features.summary: wrapText(text, maxWidth, font) breaks text into lines that fit.

features.name: fitText()
features.summary: fitText(text, maxWidth, font, {min, max}) returns the largest whole font size at which text fits on one line.

features.name: textLines()
features.summary: textLines(lines, {x, y, lineHeight, anchor, fill, font}) writes a text element with one tspan per line.

features.name: escapeXml()
features.summary: escapeXml(s) escapes & < > " ' so a prop is safe to write into markup.

features.name: formatNumber()
features.summary: formatNumber(n, {decimals, separator}) groups thousands.

features.name: asset()
features.summary: asset(name) returns the href of a file in graphics/assets/ for an image element.

features.name: Worked examples
features.summary: The reference ends with six complete modules, each showing a common move, that you can copy into a graphic as written.

features.name: What Frame Job finds in the picture
features.summary: Frame Job finds who and what is in a clip's picture on this Mac with Apple's Vision framework, with nothing uploaded and no key needed.

features.name: People in the picture
features.summary: Finds each person's head and shoulders as a box, which can stand in for their face while the face can't be found.

features.name: No face recognition
features.summary: Frame Job never puts a name to a face or recognises anyone, and nothing links a box in one sample to a box in the next.

features.name: Show Subjects
features.summary: Draws what has been found for the selected clip at the playhead over the preview.

features.name: What the outlines mean
features.summary: Faces are outlined in yellow, people in teal and salient regions in purple with a dashed line.

features.name: The boxes stay on the picture
features.summary: The boxes sit on the clip's picture wherever it is placed, and follow its speed, speed ramps and reversal.

features.name: The Not analyzed note
features.summary: When nothing has been found for the clip's picture at the playhead, the preview says so at the clip's top-left corner.

features.name: Show Subjects is per window
features.summary: Each window has its own setting, off in a new window and not remembered between launches, and it never changes an export or a saved frame.

features.name: Follow Subject
features.summary: Frames each selected movie clip on its subject with eased moves on its action lane, on the current canvas.

features.name: Follow
features.summary: Chooses what the frame stays on: Subject, Faces, People, Salient Region or Center.

features.name: Zoom
features.summary: Sets how tight the frame is, 100 to 400 %.

features.name: Where Empty
features.summary: Sets what the frame shows while there's nothing to follow: Show Whole or Center.

features.name: Follow Subject's summary
features.summary: Under the controls, the sheet says what Follow will do before you press it.

features.name: Analysis before framing
features.summary: Clips not yet analysed get the Analyzing sheet first, while faces, people and shot changes are found on this Mac, then they're framed.

features.name: It starts from the whole picture
features.summary: Each clip is framed from the whole picture: its own positions and scales are replaced, and its volume, crop and other actions stay.

features.name: How following moves: easing
features.summary: The frame eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put.

features.name: How following moves: cuts
features.summary: The frame cuts with the picture at each shot change, landing on the first frame of the new shot.

features.name: How following moves: a lost subject
features.summary: When the subject is lost the frame holds for a second, then follows someone else in the shot or eases to your Where Empty choice.

features.name: How following moves: coming back
features.summary: The frame comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s.

features.name: How following moves: two people
features.summary: The frame holds two people together when both fit in it.

features.name: The blurred Backgrounds track
features.summary: Where the frame shows the whole picture, a blurred copy of the clip goes on a new Backgrounds track at the back.

features.name: Every move is an action
features.summary: Every move is an ordinary action on the clip's action lane: select one and drag the picture on the canvas to nudge where its frame ends.

features.name: Undo Follow Subject
features.summary: Edit ▸ Undo Follow Subject takes the whole command back in one step.

features.name: Screen recordings are skipped
features.summary: A screen recording with a cursor file isn't followed by faces: it's left unanalysed and listed under the summary with the reason.

features.name: Clips it cannot frame
features.summary: A selected movie clip that cannot be followed is listed under the summary with the reason, and the others are still framed.

features.name: Make Vertical Version
features.summary: Makes a tall or square version of a landscape edit, for a phone, a reel or a square post, from the whole timeline in one step.

features.name: Shape
features.summary: Picks 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1, each shown with the size it makes.

features.name: Follow
features.summary: Chooses what each movie clip follows, as in Follow Subject, with one more choice, Speaker.

features.name: Zoom
features.summary: Sets how tight the frame is, 100 to 400 %, where 100 % is the smallest scale at which a picture covers the new canvas.

features.name: Where Empty
features.summary: Sets what a followed clip shows while there is nothing to follow, as in Follow Subject.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Where Empty

features.name: Make a copy
features.summary: Opens the vertical version as a new untitled project, leaving this one unchanged; unticked, this project becomes the vertical version.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Make a copy

features.name: Make Vertical's summary
features.summary: Under the controls, the sheet says what Make will do before you press it.

features.name: Analysis before making
features.summary: Movies not yet analysed get the Analyzing sheet first, while faces, people and shot changes are found on this Mac, then the version is made.

features.name: Making another shape
features.summary: What was found is kept in this project's cache and carried into the copy, so making another shape afterwards needs no analysis.

features.name: Undo Make Vertical
features.summary: It's one undo step: in the copy, Edit ▸ Undo Make Vertical gives back the landscape edit; in place, it takes the command back.

features.name: Keeping a vertical sharp
features.summary: A vertical canvas shows part of a landscape picture enlarged, so shoot 4K for footage you mean to make vertical.

features.name: How a clip is judged
features.summary: Each clip with a picture on the top-level timeline is treated by what it is, judged on the old canvas.

features.name: Full-frame movies follow their subject
features.summary: A movie clip that fills the old frame follows what you chose in Follow, with its own moves and actions kept inside the framing.

features.name: Screen recordings follow the pointer
features.summary: A screen recording with its cursor file follows the pointer instead of a face.

features.name: Camera layouts are re-laid
features.summary: Each camera layout switch is made again for the new canvas at the same time, length and curve, Side by Side becoming Stacked on a tall one.

features.name: A layout changed by hand
features.summary: A camera changed by hand after its switch is kept as placed, with its screen, and the summary says so.

features.name: Stills, pictures and nests are centred
features.summary: A still, picture or nest that fills the frame is centred.

features.name: Everything else is kept as placed
features.summary: Titles, other graphics, shapes, a picture-in-picture and any clip that doesn't fill the frame are moved and scaled to the new canvas.

features.name: Blurred copies and background plates
features.summary: A blurred copy behind a clip is removed when that clip is framed, otherwise re-filled to cover the new canvas, as a background plate is.

features.name: Word captions are paged again
features.summary: Word captions are split into pages again for the narrow frame, keeping every correction, as File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas does.

features.name: Follow Speaker
features.summary: With Follow on Speaker, a wide shot of two to four people that plays beside their microphones cuts to whoever is talking.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Follow ▸ Speaker

features.name: Microphones
features.summary: A checkbox for each track holding a sound file: tick the ones that belong to the people in the shot, two to four.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Follow ▸ Speaker ▸ Microphones

features.name: Faces
features.summary: One row per ticked microphone, with a pop-up of the faces Frame Job found in the longest shot it can frame this way.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Follow ▸ Speaker ▸ Faces

features.name: The automatic match
features.summary: Frame Job matches each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks, and sets the pop-ups when the match is clear.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Follow ▸ Speaker ▸ Faces

features.name: Choose a face
features.summary: When the match isn't clear, each pop-up says Choose a face and you pick each microphone's face yourself.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Follow ▸ Speaker ▸ Faces

features.name: When Make is offered
features.summary: Make is offered once two to four microphones are ticked, a shot plays beside two of them and every ticked microphone has a face of its own.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Follow ▸ Speaker

features.name: The sheet comes back after analysis
features.summary: With Speaker, the sheet comes back after the analysis with your choices kept, so you can confirm who's on each microphone before Make.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Follow ▸ Speaker

features.name: Camera Layout
features.summary: Switches a camera clip and the screen behind it between layouts as they play: move the playhead to the moment and choose one.

features.name: Corner
features.summary: The camera in a square-cornered box in the corner you choose, showing its whole picture.

features.name: Rounded Corner
features.summary: The same corner box with rounded corners.

features.name: Circle
features.summary: The largest square of the camera picture, cropped to a circle in the corner you choose.

features.name: Side by Side
features.summary: The screen fitted in the left two-thirds and the camera cropped to fill the right third.
features.where: Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ Side by Side

features.name: Stacked
features.summary: The screen across the top and the camera cropped to fill the rest below it.

features.name: Camera Full
features.summary: The camera fills the canvas.

features.name: Screen Only
features.summary: The camera is hidden, though its sound carries on, and the screen goes to its full placement.

features.name: Which clips it uses
features.summary: The camera and screen are worked out from the selection and the playhead, or the track named Camera when nothing is selected.

features.name: The switch
features.summary: A switch eases over 0.5 s from the playhead, as a layout action on each clip that you can retime on its action lane.

features.name: How far a layout reaches
features.summary: A layout holds until the next switch, so a camera cut into pieces stays in the corner.

features.name: When a switch can't be made
features.summary: A switch that can't be made changes nothing: Frame Job beeps and the foot of the inspector gives the reason.

features.name: The Layout section
features.summary: With one video clip selected, the Picture sub-tab's Layout section makes the same switch and lets you choose how long it takes.

features.name: Layout
features.summary: Choose Corner, Side by Side, Stacked, Camera Full or Screen Only.

features.name: Shape
features.summary: Choose Square, Rounded or Circle for a corner layout.

features.name: Corner
features.summary: Choose which canvas corner the camera sits in.

features.name: Duration
features.summary: Sets how long the switch takes, from 0.01 to 10 s, starting at 0.5 s.

features.name: Switch at Playhead
features.summary: Does what the menu does, with this clip as the camera and the clip drawing behind it as the screen.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Layout ▸ Switch at Playhead

features.name: The crop centred on the person
features.summary: Circle, Side by Side and Stacked centre the camera's crop on the person when its person masks already exist for every frame it plays.

features.name: A layout meets a zoom
features.summary: Frame Job won't switch when a clip it would move holds a zoom or another moving action after the playhead.

features.name: Lay out the clips in a nest?
features.summary: When a nest would let a switch go ahead, a sheet offers to nest those clips first, so the layout moves the nest and the zoom plays inside it.

features.name: Reframe a clip with an agent
features.summary: An agent fits one clip to the current canvas, say a landscape recording on a 1080 × 1920 canvas, with every framing choice in its hands.

features.name: Agent framing: follow a subject
features.summary: Follows a face; where there is none, a person; where there is neither, a salient region.

features.name: Agent framing: follow faces, people or salient regions
features.summary: Follows only faces, only people or only salient regions.

features.name: Agent framing: follow the pointer
features.summary: Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer, from its media's cursor file.

features.name: Agent framing: follow the speaker
features.summary: Frames a wide shot of two to four people on whoever is talking, each person with a microphone of their own.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Follow ▸ Speaker

features.name: Agent framing: hold on the centre
features.summary: Holds the frame on the middle of the picture for the whole clip.

features.name: Agent framing: show the whole picture
features.summary: Shows the whole picture for the whole clip, scaled to fit the canvas.

features.name: Agent framing: lay out camera layouts again
features.summary: Lays a camera clip's camera layouts, and its screen's, out again on the current canvas.

features.name: Agent framing: rescale from an older canvas
features.summary: Rescales a clip from the canvas it was placed on to the current one, its actions' positions and scales moving with it.

features.name: Agent framing: how tight the frame is
features.summary: Sets how tight the frame is, from 1 to 4, where 1 is the scale that fills the canvas.

features.name: Written as ordinary edits
features.summary: The framing is written as the clip's position and scale and one action per move, each of which you can change afterwards like any other.

features.name: Undo Reframe Clip
features.summary: Edit ▸ Undo Reframe Clip takes the whole framing back in one step.

features.name: A clip that already has actions
features.summary: A clip keeps the actions it has: a zoom or pan still happens inside the new framing, and a volume or speed action does what it did.

features.name: A shot change inside an action
features.summary: A shot change inside an action cuts it in three, so a steady volume change sounds as it did and an eased one eases again on each side.

features.name: Agent framing: start from the whole picture
features.summary: An agent can replace the clip's own moves: every position and scale its actions set is removed first, then the clip is framed.

features.name: Agent framing: a blurred copy behind
features.summary: An agent can name a track behind the clip, and a blurred copy goes there where the framing shows the whole picture.

features.name: Agent framing: waiting for analysis
features.summary: If the part of the file a clip plays hasn't been analysed, it's analysed first, and the agent waits up to a minute.

features.name: When an agent can't frame a clip
features.summary: A clip that can't be framed is left as it was, and the agent is told why.

features.name: Multicam on ordinary tracks
features.summary: A show filmed with several cameras is cut as ordinary clips on ordinary tracks, one track per camera, with no special multicam clip.

features.name: One camera per track, lined up in time
features.summary: Put each camera's recording on a track of its own and line them up in time.

features.name: Camera names come from track names
features.summary: Name each track after its camera, because the track names are what Switch Angle and the Switch by Speaker sheet list.

features.name: The program track
features.summary: Paste a camera's clip onto a new track in front of the others and split it into shots, or let Switch by Speaker write it.

features.name: Camera tracks can stay shown or be hidden
features.summary: The camera tracks stay underneath the program, shown or hidden, and they still work as angles either way.
features.where: The hide switch in the track header, or Hide Video in its right-click menu

features.name: Choosing the microphones
features.summary: Select separate microphone files with the cameras and they're the microphones; with none, each camera with sound is its own.
features.where: Switch by Speaker sheet ▸ Microphone pop-ups

features.name: Switch by Speaker
features.summary: Cuts a whole program track from a conversation by listening to each microphone and showing whoever is talking.

features.name: Synchronize Audio first
features.summary: Switch by Speaker trusts where the clips sit, so the recordings must be in sync before you run it.

features.name: When Switch by Speaker is available
features.summary: The item is available when the selection holds pictures on two or more tracks and a clip with its sound on.

features.name: Speaker rows
features.summary: One row per person pairs that person's microphone with the camera that shows them.
features.where: Switch by Speaker sheet ▸ Speaker rows

features.name: The range it cuts
features.summary: The cut covers the In–Out range when one is set, otherwise the selected camera clips' whole length.

features.name: The summary line
features.summary: The line under the controls says what Switch will do, or every reason it can't go ahead.
features.where: Switch by Speaker sheet, summary under the controls

features.name: A camera linked to its detached sound
features.summary: A camera clip linked to its detached sound stops the cut if it crosses the range, and the sheet names the clip.

features.name: One undo step
features.summary: Pressing Switch applies the whole cut as a single undo step named Switch by Speaker.

features.name: The new Program track
features.summary: Switch adds a track named Program in front of the cameras, with a silent piece of the chosen camera for each shot.

features.name: Camera tracks hidden after switching
features.summary: Switch hides the camera tracks so only the program shows; a track with other material stays, its pictures off in the range.

features.name: What stays untouched
features.summary: Nothing outside the range changes and the microphones aren't edited, so you hear the same sound unless you mute the cameras.

features.name: Wide
features.summary: Your wide shot: it opens the cut and shows during crosstalk, long monologues and gaps in another camera.

features.name: Minimum shot
features.summary: Sets the shortest shot, from 0.5 to 30 s; a shorter one merges into a neighbour that covers it.
features.where: Switch by Speaker sheet ▸ Minimum shot

features.name: Cut before speech
features.summary: Sets how long before a new speaker's first word the cut comes.

features.name: Late cuts under heavy bleed
features.summary: With heavy bleed in a noisy room a cut can land later than Cut before speech asks.

features.name: Crosstalk shows
features.summary: Chooses what is shown while two people talk at once for a second or more.

features.name: Ignore bleed
features.summary: Sets how far below a microphone's own speaker a voice must be to count as bleed, never as that person talking.
features.where: Switch by Speaker sheet ▸ Ignore bleed

features.name: Cut to the wide after
features.summary: Breaks up a long monologue with the wide for one minimum shot.
features.where: Switch by Speaker sheet ▸ Cut to the wide after

features.name: Mute the cameras' own sound
features.summary: Switches the cameras' scratch sound off inside the range.
features.where: Switch by Speaker sheet ▸ Mute the cameras' own sound

features.name: Write to
features.summary: Writes the new cut over an earlier Program track instead of adding another track.
features.where: Switch by Speaker sheet ▸ Write to

features.name: Remembered values
features.summary: Minimum shot, Cut, Crosstalk and Ignore bleed are kept for next time when you change one and press Switch.

features.name: One microphone for everyone
features.summary: With one shared microphone, Switch by Speaker decides who talks from the cameras' pictures.

features.name: The Analyzing sheet for faces
features.summary: When a camera's faces have not been found yet, an Analyzing sheet finds them on this Mac before the Switch by Speaker sheet opens.
features.where: Analyzing sheet, then the Switch by Speaker sheet

features.name: The one-microphone sheet
features.summary: For one shared microphone the sheet has one Microphone pop-up and lists the Cameras.
features.where: Switch by Speaker sheet ▸ Microphone, Cameras

features.name: Wide in the one-microphone form
features.summary: Choose a Wide to show it during crosstalk; that camera then takes no part in deciding who talks.

features.name: Faces only guess
features.summary: The summary warns that faces only guess who is talking, so look through the result.

features.name: Switch Angle
features.summary: Replaces one shot with another camera's picture, to fix a single cut or pick shots by hand.

features.name: The camera list
features.summary: The submenu lists, front first, up to nine other tracks whose video clips cover the shot's whole span.

features.name: Tracks with the same name
features.summary: Two listed tracks with the same name are told apart by their position from the back.

features.name: No Covering Angle
features.summary: The submenu holds one greyed item when there is nothing to switch to.
features.where: Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ No Covering Angle

features.name: Greyed camera items
features.summary: Cameras are listed but greyed when the shot's track is locked, the shot is linked to detached sound, or a sheet is open.

features.name: The shot is replaced in sync
features.summary: The new clip sits on the shot's own track, over the same span, and shows the camera's own frame at every moment.

features.name: A camera that stopped and started
features.summary: A shot crossing the end of one camera clip and the start of the next becomes two pieces, one from each file.

features.name: Overlapping camera clips
features.summary: Where two of a camera's clips overlap, the later one takes over at its own start.

features.name: What a switched shot keeps
features.summary: The shot keeps its span, whether its picture and sound are on, and the transitions at both of its edges.

features.name: What a switched shot loses
features.summary: A punch-in, a grade or an action on the old shot isn't copied; the new piece has the camera clip's settings.

features.name: Undo and selection
features.summary: The whole switch is one undo step, Switch Angle, and the new pieces are selected afterwards.

features.name: A transition that no longer fits
features.summary: A transition the camera's piece is too short for is dropped, leaving a plain cut, and the undo step says so.

features.name: When a switch fails
features.summary: When a switch can't be done nothing changes, and Frame Job beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector.

features.name: Copy pieces of a clip to another track (agents)
features.summary: An agent can copy parts of a clip onto another track at the same times, so a piece of a synced camera stays in sync.

features.name: Shortest turn that cuts (agents)
features.summary: An agent can set the shortest turn that cuts, from 0.2 to 10 s, a value the sheet doesn't show.

features.name: How far a microphone must lead (agents)
features.summary: An agent can set how far one active microphone must lead the others to count alone, a value the sheet doesn't show.

features.name: Preview a cut without editing (agents)
features.summary: With apply: false, an agent sees the shots and how many edits and clips they'd make, and nothing in the project moves.

features.name: Check which mode ran (agents)
features.summary: Every result says whether microphones or faces decided, and with faces a note warns that the cuts are a guess.

features.name: Waiting for faces (agents)
features.summary: Where the sheet would show Analyzing, an agent's call waits up to 60 seconds for faces, then stops and keeps what it found.

features.name: When Switch by Speaker won't run (agents)
features.summary: A call that can't run changes nothing, and most reasons are named together so they can be fixed in one go.

features.name: The New Recording panel
features.summary: One floating panel holds every recording choice: a display, a window, a camera or the microphone, straight into a project.

features.name: The panel floats without taking focus
features.summary: The panel stays above other windows and can be clicked while the app you are about to record stays in front.

features.name: Return and Esc in the panel
features.summary: Return presses Record and Esc presses Close, when the panel has keyboard focus.

features.name: The panel stays on screen as it grows
features.summary: The panel pushes itself back onto its display when the countdown or a note makes it taller, so Cancel never ends up under the Dock.

features.name: Choose what to record (Source)
features.summary: Chooses what to record: one row per connected display by name, then Window…, Camera and Microphone Only.

features.name: The panel's defaults
features.summary: Until you change it, the panel records the main display at 60 fps and Nominal size, with System Audio on and no microphone.

features.name: Controls grey out to fit the source
features.summary: Rows that do not apply to the chosen source grey out and keep their values, so nothing jumps.

features.name: The size note
features.summary: A line under Size says what you will get for the chosen source.

features.name: The panel's footnote
features.summary: The text at the bottom left shows where recordings are saved, or the elapsed time during a camera recording or voice-over.

features.name: The panel remembers your choices
features.summary: The panel reopens with your last display, devices, switches, rate, size and boxes, between launches.

features.name: Choose where it lands (Record Into)
features.summary: Chooses where the recording lands: New Project, or any open project by name.

features.name: Record with an agent
features.summary: An agent can record for 1 to 600 seconds with record_screen, with no panel and no countdown.

features.name: Record a display
features.summary: Choose a display by name in Source to record the whole of it.

features.name: Include Frame Job windows
features.summary: Puts Frame Job's own editor and preview windows into a display recording, and into the window picker's list.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ Include Frame Job windows

features.name: Recording frame rate (Rate)
features.summary: Sets the most frames per second the file may hold, 30 or 60 fps, and the frame rate of a new project made from the recording.

features.name: Recording size (Size)
features.summary: Records at the display's point size, Nominal (points), or at every pixel, Best (pixels), which is twice the points on a Retina display.

features.name: The panel hides while it records
features.summary: The panel leaves the screen once a display or window recording starts, so it isn't in the picture, and the menu-bar item takes over.

features.name: Record a window
features.summary: Choose Window… and pick a window with macOS's picker: the recording is that window alone, at its own size.

features.name: Which windows the picker lists
features.summary: With Include Frame Job windows off the picker lists none of Frame Job's windows; with it on it lists them, but never the recorder panel.

features.name: Record needs a picked window
features.summary: Pressing Record on Window… with nothing picked says so and starts no countdown, rather than recording the wrong thing.

features.name: Record a camera on its own
features.summary: With Source set to Camera, Frame Job records the chosen camera at the chosen format's highest frame rate, with no screen.

features.name: Choose a camera
features.summary: Chooses which connected camera to record, listing each by name.

features.name: Camera format
features.summary: Chooses the size and frame rate the camera records at, with Best first.

features.name: The best format
features.summary: Best is the largest format wider than tall that reaches 30 fps or more, at that format's highest rate.

features.name: Live camera preview
features.summary: A live picture under Format shows the chosen camera at the chosen format, as the movie will record it.

features.name: The camera's warm-up
features.summary: The camera starts as soon as the panel shows it, and a cold camera gets up to a second to settle, so the recording starts steady.

features.name: The panel stays up while a camera records
features.summary: The panel stays up while a camera records, with the meter live, the time in the footnote, and Stop and Pause or Resume buttons.

features.name: Where a camera recording lands
features.summary: The movie lands on the front track if it fits, else a new front track, with any microphone on a new back track named Microphone.

features.name: Record the camera too
features.summary: With a display or Window… as the source, also records the chosen camera beside the screen, for a talking head over a screencast.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ Record the camera too

features.name: Camera layout
features.summary: Chooses how the camera lands beside the screen: Corner, Rounded Corner, Circle, Side by Side or Camera Full.

features.name: How far a landed layout reaches
features.summary: The layout starts at the camera clip's first frame and ends with that stretch's screen or camera clip, whichever is later.

features.name: Remove the camera's background when it lands
features.summary: Runs Clip ▸ Remove Background on the camera's clips as soon as they land, as its own undo step.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ Remove the camera's background when it lands

features.name: The Camera track
features.summary: Each stretch's camera movie goes on one new track named Camera, in front of everything, lined up with its screen clip.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ Record the camera too

features.name: Camera clips stay ordinary clips
features.summary: Each camera clip can be moved or given another layout afterwards, with Clip ▸ Camera Layout.

features.name: Record a voice-over
features.summary: Choose Microphone Only to record narration with no picture, from the playhead.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Microphone Only

features.name: The panel stays up during a voice-over
features.summary: The panel stays up with the meter live, the time in the footnote, and Stop and Pause or Resume buttons.

features.name: Where a voice-over lands
features.summary: Each stretch's file lands end to end from the playhead on one new back track named Microphone, as one Add Recording undo step.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Microphone Only

features.name: Record what your Mac plays (System Audio)
