features.summary: Records what the Mac plays, from every app but Frame Job, as the movie's own stereo 48 kHz sound track.

features.name: Frame Job's own sound is never recorded
features.summary: System audio leaves out Frame Job, so you can play the timeline during a recording and its sound will not be in the file.

features.name: Record your voice (Microphone)
features.summary: Picks Off or a connected microphone to record beside the picture, into a second file and never into the movie.

features.name: The recorder's level meter
features.summary: A meter beside Microphone shows your level from the countdown on, so the 3, 2, 1 is your chance to check it.

features.name: Your first words are kept
features.summary: The microphone starts during the countdown, so the recording's first words are in the file.

features.name: The microphone stays separate and aligned
features.summary: The microphone file lands on one new back track named Microphone, lined up with the picture, so you can set each level on its own.

features.name: Devices plugged in and removed
features.summary: The Camera, Format and Microphone popups follow devices you plug in or remove, whenever the panel is idle.

features.name: The three-second countdown
features.summary: Pressing Record checks permissions, then counts 3, 2, 1 in the panel; you can cancel it.

features.name: The Record button's states
features.summary: The panel's main button reads Record, Cancel, Starting…, Stop, Stopping… and Adding… as the recording moves along.

features.name: A start that fails or is abandoned
features.summary: A recording that hasn't started within 20 seconds fails with a note instead of hanging, and you can stop while the button reads Starting…

features.name: One recording at a time
features.summary: Press Record while another recording runs or is paused, even an agent's, and after the countdown the panel says one is in progress.

features.name: Pause and Resume
features.summary: Pause a running recording and carry on later, from the menu-bar item, the File menu, or the panel for a camera or voice-over.

features.name: Stop Recording
features.summary: Stops a running or paused recording and adds it to your project; while one runs, File ▸ New Recording… reads Stop Recording.

features.name: The Welcome window during a recording
features.summary: The Welcome window's New Recording… never stops a recording: it beeps during your screen recording, otherwise it shows the panel.

features.name: Stop from macOS's indicator
features.summary: Stopping from macOS's own screen-recording indicator ends the recording and still adds it, with a note.

features.name: Paused recordings are stretches
features.summary: A pause ends the current file and a resume starts a new one, so each stretch of the recording has its own set of files.

features.name: A recording carries on if the panel closes
features.summary: Closing the panel during a camera recording or voice-over leaves it running, under the menu-bar item and File ▸ Stop Recording.

features.name: Quit is held during a recording
features.summary: Choosing Quit during a recording does not quit: it puts the recording's controls in front of you.

features.name: Stop an agent's recording
features.summary: You can pause or stop an agent's recording from the same menu-bar item or the File menu, and what was recorded still lands.

features.name: The recording menu-bar item
features.summary: While a recording runs the menu bar shows a coral ● and the elapsed time, and ❚❚ with the time held still while paused.

features.name: Pause, Resume and Stop from the menu bar
features.summary: The item's menu offers Pause Recording and Stop Recording, or Resume Recording and Stop Recording while paused.

features.name: The keyboard mark
features.summary: While a recording records shortcuts, a ⌨︎ mark follows the ● or ❚❚ and the menu starts with a greyed-out Recording keyboard shortcuts row.

features.name: A fixed width
features.summary: The item is sized once, so other menu-bar items don't shift as the seconds go by or at a pause.

features.name: If macOS hides the item
features.summary: macOS may drop the item from a crowded menu bar or behind the notch; File ▸ Stop Recording and Pause Recording still work.

features.name: Landing in an open project
features.summary: A finished recording goes in at the chosen project's playhead as ordinary media, inside a nest if one is open.

features.name: Stretches land touching on one track
features.summary: A paused recording lands one clip per stretch, back to back on one track, never overlapping and never joined by a transition.

features.name: Landed clips are selected
features.summary: Every landed clip, microphone and camera included, is selected after the recording lands.

features.name: One undo removes a landed recording
features.summary: Everything landed in an open project is one undo step, Add Recording, which removes the clips and media and leaves the files on disk.

features.name: Landing as a new project
features.summary: With New Project chosen, the recording opens as a new untitled project named after its file, at the movie's size and your Rate.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ Record Into ▸ New Project

features.name: Landing waits for a drag
features.summary: If you are dragging in the timeline when a recording ends, the landing waits for the drag, up to 20 seconds.

features.name: The chosen project closed
features.summary: If the project you chose closes while recording, the recording opens as a new project and the note says so.

features.name: When the panel comes back
features.summary: The panel returns on its own, with a note, only if it was on screen when recording began and there's something to report.

features.name: Enhance the microphone when it lands
features.summary: Runs Enhance Voice on the recording's microphone clips once they have landed and been analysed, as its own undo step.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ Enhance the microphone when it lands

features.name: Zoom in on clicks
features.summary: After the recording lands, runs Auto Zoom on its screen clips.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ When it lands ▸ Zoom in on clicks

features.name: Show shortcuts
features.summary: After the recording lands, runs Add Shortcut Overlays on its screen clips, at the bottom in the dark theme.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ When it lands ▸ Show shortcuts

features.name: Speed up typing
features.summary: After the recording lands and its speech is detected, runs Speed Up Typing on its screen clips with the sheet's last values.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ When it lands ▸ Speed up typing

features.name: The fixed order
features.summary: Remove Background, Enhance Voice, Auto Zoom, Add Shortcut Overlays and Speed Up Typing run in that order, each its own undo step.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ When it lands

features.name: Problems show at the inspector's foot
features.summary: If a landing step cannot run, the inspector's foot says why, with no beep and no sheet; a step with nothing to do stays quiet.

features.name: The Recordings folder
features.summary: Recordings are saved in ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings, created the first time it is needed, and never inside the project package.

features.name: Dated names and collisions
features.summary: Files are named by date and time, such as Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov, and (2), (3) and so on are added if a name is taken.

features.name: The screen movie
features.summary: A screen recording is a QuickTime .mov in HEVC where your Mac offers it, else H.264, with system audio as one stereo 48 kHz track.

features.name: The microphone file
features.summary: The microphone is written beside the movie as <movie name> (Microphone).m4a, an AAC file kept apart from the system sound.

features.name: Voice-over files
features.summary: A voice-over is an AAC file named Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a, one file per stretch between pauses.
features.where: New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Microphone Only

features.name: Camera files
features.summary: A camera recording is a QuickTime .mov at the camera's format, in HEVC where that size allows it, else H.264, with no sound of its own.

features.name: Variable frame rate from a still screen
features.summary: macOS delivers frames only when the screen changes, so a mostly still screen's file has a low, fractional frame rate; Rate is its maximum.

features.name: Cursor: Separate or In the picture
features.summary: Separate keeps the pointer out of the movie so Frame Job draws it and you can restyle it; In the picture has macOS draw it in for good.

features.name: Show Clicks
features.summary: Shows each mouse click: with In the picture a ring is drawn into the movie, and with Separate the screen clips land with click ripples on.

features.name: What a Separate recording lands with
features.summary: The clip gets a Cursor section with the pointer drawn; with Show Clicks too, Clicks is Ripple in the same undo step.

features.name: What an In the picture recording lands with
features.summary: The pointer is in the movie, the cursor file says so, and the clip shows no Cursor section, so nothing is drawn twice.

features.name: The Cursor section
features.summary: A recording's clip gets a Cursor section, after Background, to restyle the pointer Frame Job draws, unless the pointer is in the movie.

features.name: Show or hide the pointer (Show cursor)
features.summary: Turns the drawn pointer on or off for the clip.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Cursor ▸ Show cursor

features.name: Pointer size
features.summary: Scales the drawn pointer, 25–800 %.

features.name: Pointer style
features.summary: Offers As recorded and Arrow, but both draw Frame Job's arrow; the only difference you'll see is the section's header.

features.name: Frame Job's arrow
features.summary: A black arrow with a white outline, 14 by 21 points at 100 %, redrawn for each Size so it stays crisp.

features.name: Pointer smoothing
features.summary: Calms a shaky pointer path: Off, Light, Medium or Strong.

features.name: Hide when idle
features.summary: Fades the pointer out after a set time with no movement or click, and brings it back 0.15 s before it next moves.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Cursor ▸ Hide when idle

features.name: Click ripples (Clicks)
features.summary: Draws a ring growing out of every click: None or Ripple.

features.name: Ripple color
features.summary: Sets the ring's colour, with opacity.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Cursor ▸ Ripple color

features.name: Ripple size
features.summary: Sets how big the ring grows, 25–400 %.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Cursor ▸ Ripple size

features.name: Tidy the pointer in one click (Polish)
features.summary: One button sets Smoothing to Medium and Hide when idle to 3 s.

features.name: Reset the pointer's settings
features.summary: Puts every row of the clip's cursor settings back to its default.

features.name: Cursor settings through actions
features.summary: With an action selected, Size and Ripple size animate across it, while Show cursor, Style, Clicks and Ripple color switch at its end.

features.name: Paste Attributes carries the cursor
features.summary: Paste Attributes copies a clip's cursor settings to another clip with the rest of its picture settings.

features.name: Motion blur on the pointer
features.summary: With the clip's Motion Blur above 0, a moving pointer is streaked along its path across the shutter, even when the clip itself stands still.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Motion Blur

features.name: The pointer is part of its clip
features.summary: The pointer is drawn inside its clip's layer, so it follows the clip's zooms, placement, crop and grade, in the preview, frames and exports.

features.name: The cursor loads in the background
features.summary: A cursor file loads without blocking the preview: the frame draws without it until ready, then redraws.

features.name: The pointer on a reversed clip
features.summary: A reversed clip plays its pointer reversed too.

features.name: The cursor file
features.summary: Each screen recording keeps a .fjcursor file beside its movie, holding the pointer's path, every click and scroll, and any shortcuts.

features.name: Cursor files found on import
features.summary: Importing a movie picks up a same-named .fjcursor beside it, if that's a cursor file made for a movie of exactly this size.

features.name: Cursor files after a relink
features.summary: Relinking takes the cursor file beside the new movie, else keeps the existing one if it is still there and the new movie is the same size.
features.where: Media tab ▸ right-click a row ▸ Relink…

features.name: The Media tab's Cursor section
features.summary: Selecting a video in the Media tab names its cursor file, or says it is missing or absent.

features.name: Attach a cursor file (Locate…)
features.summary: Attaches or re-points a .fjcursor file for the selected video.

features.name: Forget a cursor file (Remove)
features.summary: Forgets the selected video's cursor file; the file itself stays on disk.

features.name: Cursor problems never fail a recording or export
features.summary: If a cursor file can't be written or drawn, the recording still lands and the export still finishes, and Frame Job says what's missing.

features.name: Read cursor events with an agent
features.summary: An agent can read a recording's clicks, scrolls, shortcuts, typing stretches and, if asked, the pointer's path, with get_cursor_events.

features.name: Record shortcuts
features.summary: With a display or window source, notes each keyboard shortcut you press and when you type, never what you type, in the cursor files.

features.name: What counts as a shortcut
features.summary: A shortcut is any key pressed with ⌘ or ⌃, or ⌥ with an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc.

features.name: Typed text is never recorded
features.summary: Every other key press, and every key held until it repeats, is stored only as a moment in time, never which key.

features.name: Nothing is recorded during secure input
features.summary: Nothing is recorded while any app holds secure input, such as a password field, not even a typing mark.

features.name: Auto Zoom
features.summary: Zooms a screen recording in where things happen, from its cursor file: in at each click, holding while you work, out when you stop.

features.name: How far Auto Zoom goes in
features.summary: How far in, as a multiple of the clip's own size, from 1.25 to 4×.

features.name: How long a zoom takes (Arrive)
features.summary: How long the zoom takes: it starts this long before the click and is fully in on the click.

features.name: How long a zoom holds (Stay)
features.summary: How long the zoom holds after the last click or typing.

features.name: Follow the cursor while zoomed
features.summary: Pans along when the pointer stays near the edge of the zoomed view.
features.where: Clip ▸ Auto Zoom… ▸ Follow the cursor while zoomed

features.name: Zoom on typing
features.summary: Also zooms on stretches of typing, aimed at the last click before them.
features.where: Clip ▸ Auto Zoom… ▸ Zoom on typing

features.name: Replace existing zooms
features.summary: Removes the clips' existing zooms first; off keeps your own.
features.where: Clip ▸ Auto Zoom… ▸ Replace existing zooms

features.name: Motion blur on zooms
features.summary: Gives each zoomed clip a 50 % motion blur (a 180° shutter), in the same step, so zooms and pans blur along their movement.

features.name: Auto Zoom's live summary
features.summary: A line under the controls says what Zoom would do, or why it can't, and updates as you change them.

features.name: Auto Zoom remembers its settings
features.summary: Zoom, Arrive, Stay, Follow, Replace and Motion blur are kept for next time, if you changed them and chose Zoom.

features.name: How a visit is planned
features.summary: Clicks and typing are grouped into visits: a zoom-in, a pan to each later click outside the middle 60 % of the view, and a 0.8 s zoom back.

features.name: Zooms are ordinary actions
features.summary: Each planned zoom is a normal action on the action lane that you can move, retime, change or delete.

features.name: Auto Zoom across a split
features.summary: The halves of a split clip are planned as one recording, and every zoom out returns to the first half's placement.

features.name: What stops Auto Zoom
features.summary: Auto Zoom won't plan a reversed clip, a clip with no picture, one placed smaller than the canvas, or one whose cursor file is missing.

features.name: Add Shortcut Overlays
features.summary: Shows each shortcut you pressed while recording as animated keycaps at that moment, one graphic clip each, in one undo step.

features.name: Overlays follow the clip's timing
features.summary: An overlay starts on the frame where its press plays, following the clip's speed and any ramp; a trimmed-away shortcut gets none.

features.name: Overlay duration
features.summary: Each overlay lasts 1.5 s, and never less than the keycaps need to press in turn and fade out.

features.name: Repeats are counted
features.summary: Pressing the same shortcut again before its overlay ends keeps it up 1.5 s past the last press, labelled ×2, ×3 and so on.

features.name: Shortcuts pressed close together
features.summary: A new shortcut takes over once the first has had its minimum; one more than half a second late is left out, and a sheet says so.

features.name: The Shortcuts track
features.summary: Overlays go on the front-most track named Shortcuts when it is usable, otherwise on a new Shortcuts track at the front.

features.name: The Keyboard keys template
features.summary: Overlays are drawn by the project's copy of the bundled Keyboard keys template, written the first time something is placed and reused after.

features.name: What the overlay sheet tells you
features.summary: A sheet says when no shortcut was found, some came too close to show, a clip or cursor file can't be used, or the project changed.

features.name: Speed Up Typing
features.summary: Plays the typing in a screen recording faster, reading it from the cursor file, where nobody speaks and no shortcut shows, in one undo step.

features.name: What a typing stretch is
features.summary: A typing stretch is at least 3 typed keys, each less than 1 s after the last.

features.name: How much faster typing plays (Rate)
features.summary: How much faster the typing plays, from ×2 to ×8.

features.name: Shortest stretch
features.summary: Typing shorter than this is left alone, from 1 to 30 s.
features.where: Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing… ▸ Shortest stretch

features.name: Keep pitch on sped-up typing
features.summary: Keeps the sped-up sound at its own pitch; off, it rises like a fast tape.
features.where: Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing… ▸ Keep pitch

features.name: Speed Up Typing's live summary
features.summary: The sheet says what Apply would do before you press it, or why nothing would change.

features.name: Speed Up Typing remembers its settings
features.summary: Rate, Shortest stretch and Keep pitch are kept for next time, if you changed them and chose Apply.

features.name: Speech stays at normal speed
features.summary: Any part of a stretch with speech under it, on any track, stays at normal speed, using on-device speech detection saved with the project.

features.name: Shortcuts stay at normal speed
features.summary: A recorded shortcut and its overlay are never sped up, so add the overlays first.

features.name: Clean edges
features.summary: Each sped stretch keeps 0.3 s at normal speed at both ends.

features.name: Typing across a split recording
features.summary: The halves of a split recording are treated as one when you select both and they touch, so typing across the cut is one stretch.

features.name: Everything stays in step
features.summary: Each stretch is sped with Retime Range on every unlocked track, so camera and microphone stay in sync and everything after moves up.

features.name: Asked before a clip goes silent
features.summary: If speeding would take a clip with sound past ×12, where its sound is left out, an alert asks first; Cancel leaves the sheet open.

features.name: When Speed Up Typing can't run
features.summary: It's all or nothing: if any stretch can't be sped, nothing changes, and the sheet names the stretch and the reason.

features.name: Asked only when you press Record
features.summary: Frame Job asks for macOS permissions only when you press Record in the panel, never during a countdown or from an agent's tool.

features.name: The order of the permission checks
features.summary: Record checks Screen Recording, then Input Monitoring, then Camera, then Microphone, all before the countdown.

features.name: Screen Recording permission
features.summary: The first press of Record shows macOS's prompt; later presses open System Settings at the right pane, with a note saying to relaunch.
features.where: System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording

features.name: Microphone permission
features.summary: Asked only when a microphone is chosen: the countdown starts as soon as you allow it, and a prior denial opens the Microphone pane.

features.name: Camera permission
features.summary: Asked only with Source Camera or Record the camera too, after Screen Recording and before the microphone.

features.name: Input Monitoring permission
features.summary: Record shortcuts needs Input Monitoring, which shows no prompt, so pressing Record opens the pane and tells you to add Frame Job with +.
features.where: System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring

features.name: Starting Frame Job from a terminal
features.summary: A Frame Job started from a terminal or another app runs under that app's permissions, and the note names the process that launched it.

features.name: macOS's recurring alert
features.summary: macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record; if the panel stays on Starting…, look for that alert.

features.name: The panel steps aside
features.summary: While a macOS prompt or System Settings is up, the panel stops floating so it doesn't cover them.

features.name: A camera that stops
features.summary: If the camera stops, a camera recording ends and lands what was captured; beside a screen, the screen keeps recording.

features.name: A microphone that stops
features.summary: A microphone that stops doesn't end the recording: the picture keeps going, the meter goes silent and a note says so.

features.name: A voice-over whose microphone stops
features.summary: If the microphone stops on its own, the voice-over ends there and what was recorded lands with a note.

features.name: A sleeping display or the system
features.summary: If the display sleeps or goes away, or the system stops the recording, what was captured is added, with a note.

features.name: A locked screen
features.summary: If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, a screen recording can't start until one wakes.

features.name: When Resume fails
features.summary: If Resume fails the recording stays paused and the panel's note carries the reason, so you can retry, or stop and land what you have.

features.name: Unreadable stretches are left out
features.summary: A stretch whose movie will not read is left out and named in the note, and the readable stretches land.

features.name: A left-out stretch's voice still lands
features.summary: If a left-out stretch's microphone file reads, it lands without its picture, in the slot the picture would have had.

features.name: A file too short for one frame
features.summary: A file too short for one frame lands in the Media tab with a note, and the rest of the recording lands as usual.

features.name: A failed landing names the files
features.summary: If a recording cannot be added, the note names every saved file so nothing is lost.

features.name: Very long recordings
features.summary: A recording longer than 9:59:59 shows a label wider than the menu-bar item was sized for.

features.name: The export sheet
features.summary: One sheet exports the timeline as a movie, an audio file or an animated image, and shows what the file will be before anything is written.

features.name: Controls a format cannot use
features.summary: A control the chosen format can't use is greyed out rather than hidden, so it never affects the file.

features.name: The readout line
features.summary: A line under the controls states the size, frame rate and duration the file will actually have.

features.name: The footnote
features.summary: A small line under the readout names the file's codec and container, plus any rates, stems or loudness target you chose.

features.name: Estimated export time
features.summary: AV1 and VP9 exports show a second readout line estimating how long the export will take.

features.name: The remembered last choice
features.summary: The sheet reopens on the last choices you exported with, in every document.

features.name: Cancel, Export… and Add to Queue
features.summary: The sheet ends in three buttons: close it, write the file now, or queue it and keep editing.

features.name: The fifteen formats
features.summary: The Format popup offers fifteen encodings, each a container and a codec together.

features.name: Sound in each format
features.summary: Every file with sound is stereo at 48 kHz, in AAC, Opus or LPCM depending on the format.

features.name: Changing the format
features.summary: Changing the format rebuilds the Size list and returns it to that format's default, and leaves your other choices alone.

features.name: Software and hardware encoders
features.summary: AV1 and VP9 are encoded in software and take longer than the HEVC formats, which use the Mac's hardware encoder.

features.name: A Mac with no encoder for a format
features.summary: A Mac with no encoder for a format reports it and leaves no file.

features.name: H.264 (MP4)
features.summary: The default export: H.264 video in an MP4 that every player and upload form takes.

features.name: HEVC (MP4)
features.summary: HEVC video in an MP4: a smaller file at the same picture, though not yet accepted everywhere.

features.name: HEVC 10-bit (MP4)
features.summary: HEVC Main 10 in an MP4, so a 10-bit source keeps its gradients in a delivery file.

features.name: HEVC with Alpha (MOV)
features.summary: A small 8-bit delivery movie that keeps a transparent canvas, for Safari, QuickTime and Apple's apps.
features.where: Export sheet ▸ Format ▸ HEVC with Alpha (MOV)

features.name: Fast start for delivery files
features.summary: MP4 and M4A files are written with their index at the front, so a player can start before the whole file has downloaded.

features.name: ProRes 422 (MOV)
features.summary: A 10-bit editing master for another application, at ProRes's fixed profile rate.

features.name: ProRes 4444 (MOV)
features.summary: A 12-bit master that keeps the alpha channel, for a title or lower third another application will composite.

features.name: AV1 (MP4)
features.summary: AV1 video and AAC sound in an MP4, always 10-bit, aiming for HEVC's picture or better at the same rate.

features.name: AV1 (WebM)
features.summary: The same AV1 picture in a WebM file with Opus sound, for the web.

features.name: VP9 (WebM)
features.summary: VP9 video and Opus sound in a WebM file, for a web page, encoded by the VP9 encoder built into Frame Job.

features.name: VP9 with Alpha (WebM)
features.summary: VP9 (WebM) that keeps a transparent canvas, for a title or lower third a web page plays over its own background in Chrome or Firefox.
features.where: Export sheet ▸ Format ▸ VP9 with Alpha (WebM)

features.name: The rate as a soft cap
features.summary: On AV1 and VP9 the rate is a soft cap: a constant quality chosen to match HEVC at that rate, so the file usually stays under it.

features.name: AV1 on M1 and M2 Macs
features.summary: On M1 and M2 Macs neither Frame Job nor QuickTime can play an AV1 file, and Frame Job can't import one, though it can still export it.

features.name: Animated GIF
features.summary: A short, silent, looping GIF sized to be sendable.

features.name: Animated PNG
features.summary: A lossless, silent, looping true-colour animation with real transparency.

features.name: The 600-frame limit
features.summary: An animated GIF or APNG holds at most 600 frames, and a longer range shows a sentence in the readout and greys out Export… and Add to Queue.

features.name: Fitting inside the size
features.summary: GIF and APNG list their own cap first and fit the picture inside the chosen size, keeping its shape and never enlarging it.

features.name: Audio only (M4A)
features.summary: Writes the timeline's sound with no picture as a compressed AAC file, the smallest to send.

features.name: Audio only (WAV)
features.summary: Writes the mix as uncompressed sound, for a mastering engineer or a DAW.

features.name: Audio only (AIFF)
features.summary: Writes the same samples as WAV in an AIFF file.

features.name: The 48 kHz stereo master
features.summary: Every export with sound works on the mix as 48 kHz stereo 32-bit float and rounds it once at the very end.

features.name: Controls for audio-only exports
features.summary: Audio-only formats grey out Size, Frame rate, Speed and Burn in timecode, because there's no picture.

features.name: The Size popup
features.summary: Export at the document's size, or at a standard size named by its short edge.

features.name: Custom size
features.summary: Type a width and height for the export, from 16 to 8192 pixels each.

features.name: Repeated rows hidden
features.summary: A row with the same numbers as an earlier row is hidden, so one size shows once under the name that says more.

features.name: Larger than the document
features.summary: Sizes larger than the document are offered, so a 720p recording can be exported at 4K.

features.name: Even-dimension rounding
features.summary: Formats that need even dimensions write an odd width or height one pixel smaller, and report the real size.

features.name: Letterboxing to a different shape
features.summary: A custom size of a different shape from the canvas is letterboxed with black, except in the formats that keep transparency.

features.name: The Frame rate popup
features.summary: Export at the project's rate, or at a fixed rate from 23.976 to 60 fps.

features.name: The Speed row
features.summary: Choose how long the AV1 encoder works on each frame, trading time against file size.

features.name: Format default
features.summary: The default row works the video rate out from the frame's size and rate, and uses 192 kbps sound.

features.name: Low, Medium, High and Maximum
features.summary: Four tiers set a video rate from the frame's size, so a tier means the same picture quality at every size.

features.name: How the rate scales
features.summary: The video rate scales with the frame's area, rises for high frame rates, and is lower for the more efficient codecs.

features.name: Audio bitrate by tier
features.summary: A Quality tier also sets the AAC or Opus sound rate, from 128 to 320 kbps.

features.name: When Quality greys out
features.summary: Quality is greyed out for ProRes, WAV, AIFF, GIF and APNG, where the format fixes the rate.

features.name: The Bit depth row
features.summary: Write Audio only (WAV) or (AIFF) at 16 or 24 bits.

features.name: The Range popup
features.summary: Write the whole timeline, or only the in/out range.

features.name: Exports write the top-level timeline
features.summary: An export always writes the top-level timeline, even when you're working inside a nest, so it can't use a nest's own range.

features.name: Sound ends with the range
features.summary: A file's sound is exactly as long as the range it exports, including when a clip in it plays faster or slower.

features.name: The Stems row
features.summary: An audio export can also write each track's sound as its own file beside the mix, for mixing or mastering in another editor.

features.name: Which tracks get a stem
features.summary: Only tracks you can hear get a stem, one per track or one per track name.

features.name: Stem file names
features.summary: A stem is named after the mix and its track, beside the mix.

features.name: Overwriting and clean-up
features.summary: A stem replaces a file of its name without asking, but never the project's media, and a cancelled or failed export removes what it wrote.

features.name: Stems are pre-master
features.summary: Each stem holds its tracks' sound as the mix plays it, but with no loudness target and no master limiter.

features.name: The Loudness popup
features.summary: Normalise the whole mix to an integrated loudness target, measured to ITU-R BS.1770-4.

features.name: Measuring, then one gain
features.summary: The export measures the real mix first, then applies one gain to everything, so levels inside the timeline keep their relationship.

features.name: The master limiter
features.summary: Every export with sound goes through a true-peak limiter at −1 dBTP, so a mix that would pass it is limited instead of clipped.

features.name: Track compressors in the export
features.summary: A track's own compressor and limiter run before the master, on that track's sound alone, exactly as set.

features.name: What the loudness line means
features.summary: Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured, whether or not you normalised it.

features.name: Burn in timecode
features.summary: Writes the project's timecode into the exported picture, for a review copy; it appears only in the file, never in the preview.

features.name: What a preset stores
features.summary: A preset stores the choices on the sheet, not the numbers they resolve to, so it means the same on a document of another size.

features.name: Apply a preset
features.summary: Pick a preset from the Preset popup and every control is set exactly as if you had clicked it.

features.name: Save a preset
features.summary: Save the sheet's choices under a name, from the gear beside Preset.

features.name: Delete a preset
features.summary: Choose a preset in the popup, then choose Delete from the gear.

features.name: Change a preset
features.summary: Apply a preset, adjust the controls, and save again under the same name.

features.name: Back to Custom
features.summary: Changing a control by hand puts the Preset popup back on Custom.

features.name: The presets file
features.summary: Presets are kept for your macOS user account, so every project and window shares them.

features.name: The save panel
features.summary: A save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension and says what is being written.
features.where: Export sheet ▸ Export… or Add to Queue

features.name: The Exporting sheet
features.summary: A progress bar, a percentage and a status line show the file being written.

features.name: Cancel a running export
features.summary: Cancel stops the export and removes the half-written file.

features.name: The finish report
features.summary: When an export finishes, the line names the file and says what the sound measured, with Show in Finder and Close.

features.name: Graphic and cursor warnings
features.summary: A warning does not stop an export: the finish line adds a count and its tooltip lists each one.

features.name: When an export cannot run
features.summary: An export that can't run says why in a sentence, on the sheet or on its queue row.

features.name: Quitting during a progress sheet
features.summary: Frame Job won't quit while an Export… progress sheet is writing, and brings a minimised window or a hidden Frame Job back.

features.name: Add to Queue
features.summary: Writes the same file without the wait: the export runs behind the editor while you keep working.

features.name: The Export Queue window
features.summary: A window lists every queued, running and finished export, run one at a time while you keep editing.

features.name: A queued job's snapshot
features.summary: A job holds the timeline as it was when you confirmed it, including its media files, reversed clips and graphics.

features.name: Queue rows and their buttons
features.summary: Each row shows the file's name and state, with buttons to cancel the job, remove a finished row or reveal the file.

features.name: Clear Finished and Cancel All
features.summary: Clear Finished removes every finished, cancelled and failed row, and Cancel All stops the running job and every waiting one.

features.name: Quitting with jobs in the queue
features.summary: Quitting while a queued job runs or waits asks first.

features.name: The AV1 and VP9 memory wait
features.summary: A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits if starting it would take the AV1 and VP9 exports running past a quarter of the Mac's memory.

features.name: Save Frame
features.summary: Saves the frame under the playhead as a still.

features.name: PNG, JPEG or HEIC
features.summary: The save panel's Format popup offers PNG, JPEG and HEIC, and a line under it says what each does with transparency.

features.name: Drawn the way an export draws it
features.summary: The frame is drawn the way an export draws it, at the canvas's full size.

features.name: Save Frame inside a nest
features.summary: Inside a nest the saved frame is the nest's own picture at the nest's time, the one the canvas shows.

features.name: Deep and HDR frames
features.summary: A frame showing a deep still or 10-bit VP9 clip, and any PNG or HEIC from an HDR project, saves as 16-bit PNG or 10-bit HEIC.

features.name: Waiting for masks
features.summary: A clip with Remove Background waits up to 30 seconds for that frame's masks, and past that the frame is saved with the clip whole.

features.name: Stills from an agent
features.summary: An agent's render_frame writes the same file as Save Frame for the same frame and format.

features.name: Which formats keep transparency
features.summary: A transparent canvas keeps its transparency only in ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha, VP9 with Alpha (WebM) and Animated PNG.

features.name: Which transparent movie to send
features.summary: VP9 with Alpha is for the web, HEVC with Alpha for Apple's players, and ProRes 4444 for another editor.

features.name: Straight alpha
features.summary: The colour in all three transparent movies is straight, so a re-imported ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha file composites correctly.

features.name: The same-shape rule
features.summary: ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha won't write a different shape from the canvas, because padding would lose the alpha.

features.name: The Transparency note
features.summary: While the canvas isn't fully opaque, the Document tab says how many export formats will keep its transparency.

features.name: Chapters in exports
features.summary: Chapter markers on the timeline become chapters in MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, in time order.

features.name: Chapters in a range export
features.summary: A range export keeps the chapters inside the range, with their times counted from the start of the file.

features.name: The same picture as the preview
features.summary: An export draws the picture the way the preview does, and view-only settings never reach the file.

features.name: What an export waits for
features.summary: An export waits for masks, rendered sound, loudness measurements and cursor tracks, and never writes that sound silent or that clip uncut.

features.name: Missing media still exports
features.summary: A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound.

features.name: Graphics as they were when you exported
features.summary: An export draws graphics as they were when you asked for it, even if a graphic's code is saved again while it runs.

features.name: Burned-in captions
features.summary: Captions are ordinary text clips, so they are always burned into the picture, never a switchable subtitle track.

features.name: Colour labels
features.summary: An exported file carries colour labels for players to read: SDR files BT.709, HDR files BT.2020 with HLG or PQ.

features.name: Your own Anthropic key
features.summary: The Assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key, so Anthropic bills its usage to your account and there is no Frame Job account or relay.

features.name: The Assistant section of Settings
features.summary: Settings has an Assistant section holding the key, the model and the chat settings.

features.name: Save your Anthropic API key
features.summary: Paste your key into the Anthropic API key field and click Save or press Return. It is never shown again.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant ▸ Anthropic API key:

features.name: Remove the saved key
features.summary: Click Remove to delete the saved key. The button is only enabled while a key is saved.

features.name: The key's status line
features.summary: A line above Save and Remove tells you the key's state and what your last press did.

features.name: Test your key
features.summary: Sending a message from the Assistant tab is the test: a key Anthropic won't accept shows as an error in the transcript.

features.name: Choose the Assistant's model
features.summary: Type a Claude model id, or leave the field blank for the default, claude-opus-5-5.

features.name: Compact when context reaches
features.summary: Sets when a long conversation is replaced by a summary: on at 300,000 tokens, from 20,000 to 900,000.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant ▸ Compact when context reaches … tokens

features.name: Clear old tool results
features.summary: Off by default. Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees past 150,000 tokens.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant ▸ Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens

features.name: A key or model change ends the conversation
features.summary: Saving or removing the key, or changing to a different model, ends the conversation in every open window.

features.name: Chat settings apply at once
features.summary: Changing the compaction or clearing settings applies to every open conversation and keeps each one going.

features.name: The Assistant ⓘ
features.summary: The ⓘ beside the Assistant heading sums up what is sent and to whom, what it costs, where the key is kept, and what the chat settings do.

features.name: Where the key is kept
features.summary: A saved key lives in a file named anthropic-key that only your user account can read.

features.name: Settings agents can't touch
features.summary: No tool reads or writes the key, the model or the chat settings, so neither an MCP agent nor the Assistant can see or change them.

features.name: A key from the environment
features.summary: With no saved key, Frame Job uses the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable.
features.where: Launch Frame Job from a shell that sets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

features.name: What the tab shows without a key
features.summary: Without a key, the Assistant tab replaces the message field with a prompt and an Open Settings… button.

features.name: If the helper is missing
features.summary: The Assistant runs in a helper inside the app. A copy of Frame Job without it says so in the transcript when you send a message.

features.name: The Assistant tab
features.summary: A conversation with Claude in the inspector of every editor window, which reads and edits that window's project.

features.name: Open the Assistant
features.summary: Shows the inspector if it was hidden, switches to the Assistant tab and puts the cursor in the message field.

features.name: The tab's layout
features.summary: From the top: Context with Clear, Spend, the transcript, a row for any waiting question, and the message field with Send.

features.name: The tab stays put
features.summary: The Assistant's own edits change the selection without moving you off its tab, so you can read along.

features.name: Send a message
features.summary: Type a request in the field and press Return or click Send; the field empties once the message is taken.

features.name: Send with Return
features.summary: Return or keypad Enter sends the message and gives the keys back to the editor, so Space plays while the Assistant works.

features.name: New line in the message field
features.summary: Return with ⇧, ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ starts a new line.

features.name: Tab leaves the message field
features.summary: Tab and ⇧Tab give the keys back to the editor and never type a tab.

features.name: Undo in the message field
features.summary: ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z in the field undo and redo your typing, which never lands on the project's undo stack.

features.name: If a message can't be sent
features.summary: If the conversation cannot start, the reason appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the field.

features.name: What each message carries
features.summary: A short block describing your window goes with each message, so "this clip" and "the selected titles" mean what you'd expect.

features.name: One conversation per window
features.summary: Each editor window has its own conversation about its own project, and closing the window ends it.

features.name: Clear the conversation
features.summary: Clear ends the conversation, empties the transcript and resets Spend and Context. Your next message starts a fresh one.

features.name: Streaming replies
features.summary: A reply streams in as it's written, under your message, and the transcript scrolls to the newest line.

features.name: Working notes
features.summary: The Assistant's notes between tool calls appear small and faint. They're its thinking updates.

features.name: Tool call lines
features.summary: Each tool call shows as one small monospace line with the tool's name and its arguments.

features.name: When a tool call doesn't work
features.summary: A tool call that didn't work is followed by a failed: line giving the reason.

features.name: Permission lines
features.summary: Each answered question is recorded in the transcript as Allowed: or Declined:, with the question's sentence.

features.name: Notes in the transcript
features.summary: Small monospace notes record each turn's cost, compaction and clearing, a key or model change, and a spend ledger problem.

features.name: Errors in the transcript
features.summary: An error is a red line that says what went wrong.

features.name: Automatic retries
features.summary: Rate limits, outages and connection failures are retried up to three times before an error appears.

features.name: Copy from the transcript
features.summary: The transcript is one block of text, so a selection can cross entries and ⌘C copies it as plain text.

features.name: If the helper stops
features.summary: If the helper stops, the transcript says so, a waiting question is declined, and your next message starts a new conversation.

features.name: The same tools as MCP
features.summary: The Assistant uses the same tools an agent uses over MCP, less a few held back, and searches for the one it needs.

features.name: Ask it to open, save and move around
features.summary: It can open, create and save projects, move the playhead, set the in and out range, change the selection, and enter or leave a nest.

features.name: Ask it to change tracks, markers and the canvas
features.summary: It can add, remove, reorder, rename, hide, mute, solo and lock tracks, edit markers, and change the canvas's size and frame rate.

features.name: Ask it to manage media
features.summary: It can import, relink and remove media, copy it into the project (it asks first), and set a file's camera log.

features.name: Ask it to place clips
features.summary: It can place media, text, shapes, backgrounds, adjustment clips and graphics, and insert, overwrite, paste and duplicate.

features.name: Ask it to edit clips
features.summary: It can move, trim, split, slip, roll, rate-stretch, lift, ripple-delete, insert time, close gaps, detach audio and make J- and L-cuts.

features.name: Ask it to nest clips
features.summary: It can nest clips or take a nest apart.

features.name: Ask it to change speed
features.summary: It can set speed, reverse a clip, freeze a frame, add speed ramps, retime a range and speed up typing in a screen recording.

features.name: Ask it to change look and sound
features.summary: It can change a clip's look and sound, add transitions, actions and zooms, rename it, turn its picture or sound off, and paste attributes.

features.name: Ask it for captions and words
features.summary: It can import captions, transcribe on this Mac, read a clip's timed words, and export captions.

features.name: Ask it to clean up audio
features.summary: It can find and cut silences and filler words, normalise loudness, enhance a voice, match a clip's sound and synchronise audio.

features.name: Ask it to export
features.summary: It can export, check how an export is going, or cancel it. Exporting asks first.

features.name: It looks at rendered frames
features.summary: The Assistant renders a frame of the finished timeline, drawn the way an export draws it, to look before and after a visual edit.

features.name: Each edit is an undo step
features.summary: Each edit the Assistant makes is its own undo step, named in Edit ▸ Undo. Changes to graphics files make no undo step.

features.name: Short replies
features.summary: Its replies are a sentence or two and don't repeat what the tool lines already show.

features.name: Captions only on request
features.summary: The Assistant writes or restyles a caption only when you ask.

features.name: Medium effort, thinking on
features.summary: The model always runs at medium effort with thinking on, and Settings has no control for either.

features.name: Only its own window's project
features.summary: The Assistant acts only on the project in its own window. A tool call that names another project doesn't run.

features.name: It can't record
features.summary: The Assistant can't record the screen or a camera, because recording needs a person at the Record button.

features.name: It can't close the project
features.summary: The Assistant can't close its own project, because that would close the window the conversation lives in.

features.name: It can't use cloud transcription
features.summary: The Assistant can't transcribe with AssemblyAI: audio leaves your Mac only when you choose it, with the price in front of you.

features.name: It can't upload audio to find fillers
features.summary: The Assistant can't start the cloud transcription that finds filler words, because that uploads audio. Press Transcribe yourself.

features.name: What it asks about first
features.summary: Before it exports, saves the project, copies media or exports a graphic, the Assistant waits for you to choose Allow or Deny.
features.where: Assistant tab ▸ ask-first row ▸ Allow or Deny

features.name: What each question reads
features.summary: The question names the tool and the file it would write, and says when it would replace one.

features.name: File writes that do not ask
features.summary: Temporary renders and files in the project's graphics folder are written without a question.

features.name: The dot on the Assistant tab
features.summary: While a question waits, a small accent dot shows on the Assistant tab title, whichever inspector tab you are on.

features.name: Declining
features.summary: Deny tells the Assistant you declined, and it won't try that call again in the same turn unless you ask.

features.name: A waiting question holds only its window
features.summary: Other windows' Assistants and agents over MCP keep working while one window waits for an answer, and you can go on editing.

features.name: MCP agents aren't bound by these rules
features.summary: An agent over MCP drives the same tools directly, so it's never asked first and none of these tools is held back from it.

features.name: Stop a turn
features.summary: Click Stop, the Send button while a turn runs or a question waits, to end the request to Anthropic and halt what has not started.

features.name: What stopping leaves in place
features.summary: Stop undoes nothing and ends only the turn: edits that landed stay, and your next message carries on the same conversation.

features.name: Stop leaves queued exports alone
features.summary: An export goes to the Export Queue as soon as it starts, so Stop doesn't reach it. Cancel it there, or ask the Assistant to.

features.name: The 30-round limit
features.summary: One turn stops after 30 requests to Anthropic, with no error. Send another message to carry on.

features.name: Tool calls wait for your drag
features.summary: A tool call that arrives during a drag waits until you release the mouse, then runs as its own undo step after yours.
features.where: Timeline, canvas or inspector slider drags

features.name: Tool calls take turns
features.summary: The assistant's tool calls and MCP agents' calls take turns, one at a time, and each window's calls run in order.

features.name: The context meter
features.summary: The Context meter shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response.

features.name: Compaction
features.summary: With Compact when context reaches on, a summary replaces the conversation at the end of the first turn to reach the threshold.

features.name: With compaction off
features.summary: With compaction off, a conversation grows until it fills the model's window, and requests then fail until you click Clear.

features.name: Clearing old tool results
features.summary: Past 150,000 tokens Anthropic may drop older tool results, keeping the five most recent. The conversation itself stays.

features.name: All figures are estimates
features.summary: Every cost figure is Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM's published prices. The Anthropic Console shows what you were billed.

features.name: The cost of a turn
features.summary: Each turn ends with a transcript line giving its estimated cost and the price table used.

features.name: Unpriced responses
features.summary: A response that could not be priced shows as unknown with its reason, never as $0.

features.name: Responses cut short
features.summary: A response cut short by Stop or an error is priced from what had arrived.

features.name: The Spend row
features.summary: The tab's Spend row adds up the conversation's turns since the last Clear, or since a key or model change ended the conversation.

features.name: This month's spend
features.summary: A line in Settings, under Save and Remove, totals what the Assistant has cost in the current calendar month, in UTC.

features.name: Prices refreshed daily
features.summary: Costs use LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices: a table built into the app, and a copy refreshed at most once a day.

features.name: The spend ledger
features.summary: Each response is written to spend.jsonl on your Mac with its model, tokens and estimated dollars, never your key or the conversation.

features.name: What goes to Anthropic
features.summary: Your messages, what the tools send back and the frames it renders go to Anthropic under your key, and nowhere else.

features.name: What stays on your Mac
features.summary: The key file, the spend ledger and the cached price table stay in your Application Support folder.

features.name: The conversation lives in memory
features.summary: A conversation is kept in memory only, so it goes when you clear it or close the window, and nothing is saved in the project.

features.name: The whole editor as tools
features.summary: Frame Job serves its whole editor as MCP tools, so an agent such as Claude Code can open projects, cut, style, check frames and export.

features.name: The framejob-mcp helper
features.summary: A small stdio MCP server inside the app bundle is how MCP clients connect to Frame Job.

features.name: The tool list with Frame Job closed
features.summary: A client can start a session and see every tool with nothing on screen.

features.name: Opening on the first tool call
features.summary: If a tool call finds Frame Job not running, the helper launches its own copy in the background and waits for it.

features.name: Who can connect
features.summary: Only programs running under your own account can connect, and any of them can while Frame Job is running; there is no network port.

features.name: Assistant rules do not bind an MCP client
features.summary: The Assistant's limits and questions are its own: a client connected over MCP calls every tool directly and nothing asks you first.

features.name: Settings can't be changed by an agent
features.summary: No MCP tool reads or writes anything in Settings, so keys, the model, the region and Background render are set only by a person.

features.name: The MCP section in Settings
features.summary: Settings opens with an MCP section explaining how a client reaches Frame Job.

features.name: The helper path in Settings
features.summary: The MCP section shows the full, selectable path of this copy's framejob-mcp.

features.name: Copy MCP Command
features.summary: One button puts the Claude Code registration command for this copy of Frame Job on the clipboard.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP ▸ Copy MCP Command

features.name: The missing helper warning
features.summary: If the helper is missing from this copy or can't be run, Copy MCP Command is dimmed and the status line says so.

features.name: Connect Claude Code
features.summary: Paste the copied command into Terminal to register Frame Job with Claude Code.

features.name: Claude Desktop and other stdio clients
features.summary: Any MCP client that starts a stdio server can use the same helper by its path.

features.name: Testing a second copy
features.summary: Setting RC_AGENT_SOCKET for both Frame Job and framejob-mcp keeps a test copy on its own socket, apart from your everyday one.

features.name: The local agent socket
features.summary: Frame Job opens a local Unix socket every time it launches, with no switch to turn it on or off and no network port.

features.name: Streamable HTTP over the socket
features.summary: The socket serves MCP as streamable HTTP, so a client that speaks HTTP over a Unix socket can connect directly.

features.name: The socket's folder and permissions
features.summary: The socket sits in a private 0700 folder and is itself 0600; a folder with the wrong permissions means no socket at all.

features.name: One copy holds the socket
features.summary: With several copies of Frame Job open, the first owns the socket and later ones leave it alone.

features.name: Stale socket cleanup
features.summary: A socket file left by a crashed copy is removed and replaced automatically.

features.name: The socket released at quit
features.summary: Quitting removes the socket file if it is still this copy's, and a call in flight cannot hold up the quit.

features.name: Socket status in the log
features.summary: A launch that cannot open the socket logs why and carries on, with no dialog.

features.name: The helper stays in the bundle
features.summary: The helper launches only the Frame Job it belongs to, so register it at its path inside the app bundle.

features.name: One launch between several clients
features.summary: Two clients that both find no Frame Job launch one copy between them, not two.

features.name: The launch wait
features.summary: The helper waits up to 60 seconds for a launched Frame Job, and RC_MCP_LAUNCH_WAIT changes that.

features.name: Failed launches
features.summary: If a launched Frame Job never starts listening, the call says so and that client session stops launching more.

features.name: Long calls are never timed out
features.summary: A forwarded tool call can take as long as it needs, so the helper never cuts off a long recording or analysis.

features.name: Errors from the helper
features.summary: A call the helper could not deliver comes back as a tool result with isError true and a plain sentence.

features.name: Protocol versions
features.summary: Frame Job speaks three MCP protocol revisions and uses the one a client asks for, or the newest if it asks for any other.

features.name: Tool list changes
features.summary: If the list a client got from the stored copy differs from the running app's, the helper tells the client the list changed.

features.name: A custom socket path
features.summary: RC_AGENT_SOCKET moves the socket to an absolute path of at most 103 bytes, in a folder held to the same permission rules.

features.name: One call at a time
features.summary: Frame Job runs one tool call at a time, across every connected client and the Assistant.

features.name: Calls wait for your drag
features.summary: A call made while you drag a clip, canvas handle or inspector slider waits until you let go, then runs as its own undo step.

features.name: A tool call never asks
features.summary: A tool call never puts up an alert or asks for a permission; it comes back with a message instead.

features.name: The ffmpeg offer is declined
features.summary: An agent's import never shows the ffmpeg question: unless you've chosen to convert automatically, the file is turned down with the reason.

features.name: close_project stops rather than asks
features.summary: close_project won't close a project with unsaved changes unless passed discard: true, or a window with a sheet open.

features.name: Which project a call acts on
features.summary: Every tool takes an optional project path; without it the call goes to the frontmost open project.

features.name: One call, one undo step
features.summary: Every tool that edits makes exactly one undo step, however many clips it touched.

features.name: Edits show live
features.summary: Every edit an agent makes shows in the window at once, marks the document edited and can be undone with ⌘Z.

features.name: Analysis tools wait 60 seconds, then resume
features.summary: A call that needs analysis waits at most 60 seconds; what was analysed is kept, so calling again carries on from there.

features.name: Calls and Background render
features.summary: An MCP call stops Background render when it edits a project or moves a playhead; a call that only reads does not.

features.name: Times in ticks
features.summary: Time arguments are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid.

features.name: One id space
features.summary: Clip, track, marker and media ids share one number space, so an id names one thing on its own.

features.name: Track order
features.summary: tracks[0] is the back of the layer stack and the bottom lane of the timeline; a higher index draws in front.

features.name: Colour formats
features.summary: Clip and canvas colours are [r, g, b, a] from 0 to 1, and a few other colours are spelled their own way.

features.name: Boolean spellings
features.summary: A tool's boolean argument may also be sent as "true", "1", "false" or "0".

features.name: Keys that must be sent even when null
features.summary: set_transition's kind and add_zoom_action's region must be sent even when null, because null means something.

features.name: No empty lists
features.summary: An empty clips, ranges or groups list stops the call and names it; only set_selection takes an empty list, to select nothing.

features.name: Speed rates are clamped
features.summary: set_speed and add_speed_ramp bring a rate outside ×0.1–×1000 into that range; a rate of zero or less stops the call.

features.name: How a patch merges
features.summary: Property tools take a patch object that merges into what the clip already has, at every depth.

features.name: A bad patch names its path
features.summary: An unknown key or wrong value in a patch stops the call, naming its dotted path and the value sent.

features.name: Unknown arguments are named
features.summary: An argument a tool doesn't take stops the call before anything runs, and the message lists what it does take.

features.name: Text and shape shorthands
features.summary: add_text_clip's text may be a plain string (the words), and add_shape_clip's shape a plain string (the kind).

features.name: Errors come back as tool results
features.summary: Every outcome comes back as the tool's result, errors included, so a model can read it and correct itself.

features.name: A landed edit
features.summary: An edit that landed returns ok: true, the ids it created and a short project summary.

features.name: A call that changed nothing
features.summary: A message that the project is already in that state means nothing was wrong and no undo step was made, so it's safe to retry.

features.name: An edit a rule declined
features.summary: A message reading "was refused at" means a rule declined the edit. It says what to act on, and no undo step was made.

features.name: Keyed tools with no key
features.summary: A tool that sends to AssemblyAI needs your key only at the moment it would send; without one it stops and says where to set it.

features.name: Tools that never reach the network
features.summary: Reads of words and analysis never make a network request and need no key.

features.name: The scope argument
features.summary: Every edit tool takes scope, a nest id, so one call edits inside that nest from wherever the window is looking.

features.name: Opening and closing a nest with set_scope
features.summary: set_scope opens a nest by its id or the clip that shows it, like double-clicking the clip; with no arguments it comes back out.

features.name: Tools that follow the open nest
features.summary: Tools that aren't plain edits take no scope and work in whatever nest set_scope has open.

features.name: protected_nests in detect_silence
features.summary: detect_silence names the nest clips a quiet run crossed and left uncut, so you can open one and look for dead air inside it.

features.name: Edit tools that won't take a scope
features.summary: Eleven edit tools have no meaning inside a nest and stop with an error if given a scope.

features.name: Document edits while a nest is open
features.summary: With a nest only open, nine of those tools apply to the whole project, and the result lists what went there under document_ops.

features.name: Markers while a nest is open
features.summary: add_marker, and set_marker with a time, return an error while a nest is open, because a marker sits at project time.

features.name: Document-wide limits inside a nest
features.summary: An edit valid inside a nest can still fail, because the clip, track and nesting limits count the whole project.

features.name: A typical session
features.summary: The usual order is open, read the project, import, place, edit, render a frame, save, export and poll.

features.name: get_project
features.summary: Returns the whole project as JSON, the same document every edit changes; every other tool names things by the ids it reports.

features.name: The graphics summary
features.summary: get_project reports each graphic module's name, revision, whether it compiles and the clips drawn by it.

features.name: Reading a file's Camera Log
features.summary: get_project's media[].color reports a file's colour setting and shows detected: true for one set at import.

features.name: The report while a nest is open
features.summary: While a nest is open get_project reports it as if it were the project, and render_frame draws it at its own size.

features.name: render_frame
features.summary: Draws one frame of the finished timeline the way an export draws it, so an agent can see what the file will hold.

features.name: render_frame: t
features.summary: Chooses the moment to render, in ticks; the playhead by default.

features.name: render_frame: path
features.summary: Chooses where to write the file; a temporary file by default.

features.name: render_frame: format
features.summary: Writes png, jpeg or heic, and wins over the path's extension.

features.name: render_frame: max_width
features.summary: Caps the width at 16 to 8192 pixels; the picture keeps its shape and is never made larger than the canvas.

features.name: render_frame: burn_in_timecode
features.summary: Draws the project timecode over the picture.

features.name: render_frame: ungraded
features.summary: Draws every clip as if it weren't graded, the picture View ▸ Show Ungraded gives.

features.name: render_frame: selection
features.summary: Given an adjustment clip's id, draws what its qualifier selects, the picture View ▸ Show Selection gives.

features.name: render_frame: sdr_version
features.summary: In an HDR project, draws its SDR version, the picture View ▸ Show SDR Version gives.

features.name: render_frame: waveform, parade and histogram
features.summary: Each also measures that scope: the text gives the clipping share and a JSON file beside the image holds the counts.

features.name: render_frame: vectorscope and vectorscope_zoom
features.summary: Measures the vectorscope, with its neutral share in the text and an optional zoom of 1, 2 or 4.

features.name: Graphic problems in a rendered frame
features.summary: When a graphic in the frame failed or warned, the text names it, and a failed graphic draws its error card in the picture.

features.name: Waiting for cutout masks
features.summary: A Remove Background clip waits up to 30 seconds for the masks the frame needs; past that it's drawn whole and the text says so.

features.name: Frames from an HDR project
features.summary: In an HLG project a PNG is 16-bit and a HEIC 10-bit, both labelled BT.2100 HLG; a JPEG or sdr_version frame is the SDR version.

features.name: export
features.summary: Puts the job on the Export Queue and returns at once with export_id, path and status.

features.name: export_status
features.summary: Reports how an export is going, as its Export Queue row does, and never waits.

features.name: cancel_export
features.summary: Stops an export, as the queue row's Cancel does.

features.name: export_id and its lifetime
features.summary: An export_id is known until Frame Job quits, even after its row is removed from the Export Queue.

features.name: When an export can't start or fails
features.summary: A problem Frame Job can see from the request comes back from export; one while writing comes back from export_status as failed.

features.name: Export presets
features.summary: Fifteen export presets cover video, audio and animated images.

features.name: Export frame rate
features.summary: There is no frame-rate argument: an export runs at the project's rate, or 12.5 fps for gif and 25 fps for apng.

features.name: Export paths
features.summary: An existing file at the path is replaced, and the file always ends in the preset's extension.

features.name: export: size
features.summary: Chooses the output size: the document, a named short edge, the preset, or a [width, height].

features.name: export: range
features.summary: Writes the whole timeline, or only the in and out range.

features.name: export: exact bitrates
features.summary: An agent sets video and audio rates in bits per second directly.

features.name: export: the loudness report
features.summary: loudness_lufs normalises the whole mix, and a finished export reports its full loudness measurements.

features.name: peak_dbtp
features.summary: Sets the ceiling of the limiter every export with sound goes through.

features.name: audio_bits
features.summary: Chooses 16 or 24 bits for audio_wav and audio_aiff.

features.name: export: stems
features.summary: Also writes one file per heard track, or per track name, beside an audio mix.

features.name: dynamic_range
features.summary: Chooses HLG, HDR10 or the SDR version when exporting an HLG project.

features.name: encoder_speed
features.summary: Chooses faster, balanced or smaller for av1 and av1_webm.

features.name: Transparent export presets
features.summary: Four presets keep a transparent canvas transparent: prores_4444, hevc_alpha, vp9_alpha_webm and apng.

features.name: record_screen
features.summary: Records for 1 to 600 seconds and lands the recording in the project as the panel does, with no countdown.

features.name: record_screen: seconds
features.summary: How long to record, 1–600 s; required.

features.name: record_screen: source
features.summary: screen, voice_over or camera; screen by default.

features.name: record_screen: display
features.summary: Records a chosen shareable display, 0 being the main one.

features.name: record_screen: window
features.summary: Records one window at its own size.

features.name: include_framejob_windows
features.summary: Puts Frame Job's own windows in a display recording.
features.where: Recorder panel ▸ Include Frame Job windows

features.name: record_screen: microphone
features.summary: Also records the default microphone to a second file that lands on a Microphone track.

features.name: system_audio
features.summary: Records what the system plays, except Frame Job, into the movie.

features.name: show_clicks
features.summary: Shows each mouse click: drawn into the movie with in_picture, as click ripples with separate.

features.name: record_screen: cursor
features.summary: separate keeps the pointer out of the movie for Frame Job to draw; in_picture burns it in.

features.name: record_screen: keys
features.summary: shortcuts writes each shortcut, spelled, and a time-only typing mark for every other key into the cursor files.

features.name: record_screen: rate
features.summary: Sets the most frames a second the file may hold, 30 or 60, and a new project's canvas rate.

features.name: record_screen: size
features.summary: Records at a display's point or pixel size.

features.name: record_screen: path
features.summary: Records into a folder of your choice; the file name is always the dated one.

features.name: record_screen: project
features.summary: The open project to land in; the front project by default.

features.name: record_screen: place
features.summary: Puts clips on the timeline, or with false adds the recording to the media list only.

features.name: Voice-overs
features.summary: source: "voice_over" records the default microphone alone, and an argument it can't use stops the call by name.

features.name: A camera alone
features.summary: source: "camera" records a camera on its own, with camera to choose one and camera_format its format.

features.name: camera and camera_format
features.summary: Names the camera by unique id or name in any case, and its format as 1920x1080@30, WIDTHxHEIGHT or best.

features.name: A camera beside the screen
features.summary: With source: "screen" and camera, each stretch gets a camera movie on one new front Camera track in the same undo step.

features.name: camera_layout
features.summary: Lays each camera clip out from its first frame with its screen clip, as the panel's Layout does.

features.name: camera_cutout
features.summary: Runs Remove Background on the camera clips as its own undo step right after the landing.
features.where: Recorder panel ▸ Remove the camera's background when it lands

features.name: record_screen: enhance
features.summary: Runs enhance_voice on the microphone's clips at −16 LUFS as its own undo step once their sound is analysed.
features.where: Recorder panel ▸ Enhance the microphone when it lands

features.name: After-landing steps
features.summary: auto_zoom, shortcut_overlays and speed_up_typing run those tools on the screen clips after the landing, each its own undo step.

features.name: record_screen never asks for a permission
features.summary: A missing permission stops the call with a message naming the System Settings pane; it never shows a prompt, the picker or Settings.

features.name: What record_screen checks first
features.summary: A call is checked in a fixed order, the caller's own mistakes first, so an agent hears of a mistake even with no permission given.

features.name: A person can pause or stop a recording
features.summary: The same menu-bar item appears while an agent records, so a person can pause, resume or stop it; the recording still lands.

features.name: What record_screen returns
features.summary: The result reports the files, duration, stretches, pauses, how it stopped, where it landed, and media and clip ids.

features.name: Undoing a recording
features.summary: Undo removes the recording's media and clips in one step and leaves the files on disk.

features.name: The tool catalog
features.summary: Frame Job gives an agent 125 tools: 69 edit tools, each one undo step, and 56 app tools for files, reads, the view and whole commands.

features.name: How arguments are published
features.summary: Each tool publishes its arguments as JSON Schema: names, kinds, closed lists of values, bounds and which are required.

features.name: set_video: position, scale, rotation, opacity and blend
features.summary: Places, scales, turns and fades a clip, and chooses how it combines with what is under it.

features.name: set_video: crop and corners
features.summary: Crops a clip's edges in place and rounds its corners.

features.name: set_video: shadow, chroma key, filters, reflection, spotlight and obscure
features.summary: Adds a clip's picture effects, each an object that merges or a list that replaces.

features.name: set_video: cutout
features.summary: Remove Background: the clip drawn as its subject alone, from masks made on this Mac.

features.name: set_video: cursor
features.summary: Styles how the pointer recorded beside a screen recording is drawn on a clip, through eight keys.

features.name: set_video: motion
features.summary: Gives a clip an entrance, an exit and a motion all the way through.

features.name: set_video: motion_blur
features.summary: Blurs a clip and its moving cursor along their motion, as a shutter fraction of a frame.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Motion Blur

features.name: set_video: hide_silent
features.summary: Fades the clip out while a media's speech is silent, and back in ahead of the next words.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Hide While Silent

features.name: set_video: behind_subject
features.summary: Cuts the clip by the person of every cut-out clip behind it, so the person stands in front.

features.name: set_video: color
features.summary: Sets all thirteen Light and Color values through one patch.

features.name: set_video: wheels
features.summary: Pushes lift, gamma and gain towards a hue and sets each one's brightness.

features.name: set_video: curves
features.summary: Writes the master, red, green, blue, Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves, one list of points per channel.

features.name: set_video: look
features.summary: Applies one of eight built-in looks at an amount, or an imported .cube LUT.

features.name: set_video: qualifier
features.summary: Narrows which pixels an adjustment clip grades, by hue, saturation and luma.

features.name: set_text: word timings and word style
features.summary: set_text edits a caption page's words, their timing and how the active word is drawn.

features.name: set_action_end: graphic props
features.summary: set_action_end animates a graphic clip's props, through a graphic group in its patch.

features.name: set_action_end: speed
features.summary: set_action_end's speed ramps a media clip's rate along the action's curve and holds it after.

features.name: set_action_end: switching off at an end
features.summary: set_action_end's off turns an optional property off at an action's end.

features.name: set_track: compressor and limiter
features.summary: set_track's compressor and limiter each take a whole object, or null to clear, and work on timeline tracks only.

features.name: set_track: mattes
features.summary: set_track's matte makes a track cut the track directly behind it.

features.name: set_track
