features.summary: Sets name, Hide Video, Mute Audio, Lock Track, Solo and Matte, and the mix panel's volume, pan, compressor and limiter.
features.where: Track ▸ Hide Video / Mute Audio / Lock Track / Solo

features.name: set_audio: volume and mute
features.summary: Sets a clip's gain, from 0 to 32, and mutes it.

features.name: set_audio: fades and fade shapes
features.summary: Fades a clip's sound in and out, and chooses each fade's curve.

features.name: set_audio: ducking
features.summary: Lowers other sound while this clip plays, or only while its speech plays.

features.name: set_audio: mono, keep pitch, pan and channels
features.summary: Plays a clip in mono, keeps its pitch at a new speed, pans it, and picks or swaps its channels.

features.name: set_audio: compressor and limiter
features.summary: Compresses a clip's sound and adds a true-peak limiter last in its chain.

features.name: set_audio: noise reduction and voice isolation
features.summary: Reduces noise, or isolates a voice with Apple's on-device model.
features.where: Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Noise Reduction, Voice Isolation

features.name: set_audio: EQ
features.summary: Shapes a clip's tone with seven slots.

features.name: set_audio: hum removal
features.summary: Notches out mains hum and its harmonics.

features.name: set_audio: gate
features.summary: Turns the pauses down with a downward expander.

features.name: set_audio: leveller
features.summary: Evens out a speaker who moves on and off the mic, from a gain curve made ahead of time.

features.name: set_audio: de-esser
features.summary: Turns the band above a frequency down on sibilance.

features.name: set_audio: voice effects
features.summary: Replaces a clip's sound with a rendered voice effect.

features.name: Cutting what detect_silence and detect_fillers found
features.summary: Pass the ranges of detect_silence or detect_fillers to ripple_delete_ranges to make the cut.

features.name: transcribe engines
features.summary: transcribe runs on this Mac by default, or with AssemblyAI using your key.

features.name: transcribe: speakers and vocabulary
features.summary: With AssemblyAI, speakers starts a new cue at a change of speaker and vocabulary says which words to expect.

features.name: Checking a transcript before placing it
features.summary: place: false returns the cues without changing the project.

features.name: transcribe: caption styles and paging
features.summary: style chooses subtitles or one of five word styles, and word styles fill each page to the width it measures on this canvas.

features.name: transcribe: caption looks
features.summary: slide, fill and dim add looks to a word style's pages, each false unless given.

features.name: transcribe: restyling captions
features.summary: replace removes earlier caption tracks when restyling.

features.name: Where get_transcript's words come from
features.summary: Words come from the file's saved AssemblyAI transcript, else this Mac's own recogniser, and reading never uploads anything.

features.name: Fillers in a transcript
features.summary: Each word says whether it is a filler, and fillers_reported says whether the transcript was made with filler words at all.

features.name: get_transcript: the from and to window
features.summary: A from/to window in timeline time returns only the words that overlap it, and a word crossing an edge comes back whole.

features.name: Heard words and editable words
features.summary: Words come from every clip playing speech, nests included; each says if cutting it is safe and keeps its id across edits.

features.name: Read once per file
features.summary: A file with no saved AssemblyAI transcript is read whole by this Mac's recogniser once, and the words are saved in the project.

features.name: Duplicate speech
features.summary: When two clips of different files carry the same speech at the same time, notes names the pair and both sets of words stay.

features.name: get_timeline_transcript: paging
features.summary: Long timelines come in pages of at most 2,000 words, with a place to continue from.

features.name: Cutting words and pauses
features.summary: Each word and pause carries the range the Transcript tab would cut it by, and one ripple_delete_ranges does the cut.

features.name: get_timeline_transcript
features.summary: Reads every word heard on the timeline or in the open nest, in timeline order, nested clips included.

features.name: get_transcript
features.summary: Reads one clip's spoken words with their times on the timeline.

features.name: get_media_analysis kind: shots
features.summary: Finds the hard cuts, with clip and timeline times when you name a clip.

features.name: get_media_analysis kind: masks
features.summary: Says where a person is, as runs of frames, never the masks themselves.

features.name: get_media_analysis kind: faces
features.summary: Finds every face ten times a second, with its box, its tilt and how wide and open the mouth is.

features.name: get_media_analysis kind: subjects
features.summary: Finds boxes for people and the regions the eye is drawn to, ten times a second.

features.name: get_media_analysis kind: sound_events
features.summary: Says how sure Apple's sound classifier is of laughter, applause, cheering, a crowd, music and speech, every 0.75 s.

features.name: reframe_clip follow: subject, face, person and salient
features.summary: Follows a face, a person or a salient region found on this Mac, analysing the clip first.

features.name: reframe_clip follow: cursor
features.summary: Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer from its media's cursor file, with no analysis and no wait.

features.name: reframe_clip follow: layout
features.summary: Re-lays a camera clip's camera layouts and its screen's on the current canvas.

features.name: reframe_clip follow: speaker
features.summary: Frames a wide shot of two to four people on whoever is talking, from the microphone clips in mics.
features.where: File ▸ Make Vertical Version… ▸ Follow ▸ Speaker

features.name: reframe_clip follow: center
features.summary: Holds the frame on the middle of the picture for the whole clip, at zoom.

features.name: reframe_clip follow: fit
features.summary: Shows the whole picture for the whole clip.

features.name: reframe_clip follow: keep
features.summary: Rescales the clip from the canvas it was made for.

features.name: reframe_clip: zoom, where_empty, backdrop and replace
features.summary: Sets how tight the frame is, what shows where nothing is found, a blurred copy behind, and whether the clip's own moves are kept.

features.name: reframe_clip's analysis wait
features.summary: The tool analyses the part of the file the clip plays and waits up to a minute; past that it changes nothing and says how much is done.

features.name: Clips reframe_clip won't frame
features.summary: A clip that can't be framed stops the call with one sentence saying why, and the checks run in a fixed order.

features.name: make_vertical_version: subject following
features.summary: Each movie clip that fills the old frame on one side is framed on its subject, or shown whole where nothing is found.

features.name: make_vertical_version: screen recordings follow the cursor
features.summary: A screen recording with a cursor file follows its cursor, its own zooms and pans replaced, or is shown whole when the file cannot be read.

features.name: make_vertical_version follow: speaker
features.summary: With follow: speaker and mics, a wide shot of two to four people cuts to whoever is talking.

features.name: make_vertical_version: camera layouts re-laid
features.summary: A camera and its screen in camera layouts are re-laid for the new canvas.

features.name: make_vertical_version: stills, graphics, titles and plates
features.summary: Stills and nests are centred; other items are resized, kept or re-filled by kind.

features.name: make_vertical_version: a copy or in place
features.summary: By default it opens a new project holding the change as one undo step "Make Vertical"; copy: false applies it to the project you name.

features.name: make_vertical_version: captions re-paged
features.summary: Word caption tracks are re-paged for the new canvas as relay_captions does.

features.name: make_vertical_version: bundled templates updated
features.summary: In a copy, older copies of bundled templates are rewritten with the current text; in place they are only listed.

features.name: switch_by_speaker options
features.summary: Every argument is optional, and each tunes how the Program track is cut.

features.name: switch_by_speaker: previewing with apply: false
features.summary: apply: false returns the planned shots without editing the project.

features.name: switch_by_speaker: faces mode
features.summary: When one microphone is shared by two or more cameras, their faces decide who talks.

features.name: When switch_by_speaker won't cut
features.summary: Nothing changes, and problems that are checked together are all named in one sentence.

features.name: render_graphic: the contact sheet
features.summary: The png format returns up to 16 frames on a grid, each frame number under its cell.

features.name: render_graphic: one frame as SVG
features.summary: The svg format returns one frame's SVG text, its diagnostics and the ctx it was drawn with.

features.name: render_graphic options
features.summary: render_graphic can draw with chosen properties, size, width limit, background and output path.

features.name: Editing the graphics folder with your own file tools
features.summary: An agent may edit the graphics folder with its own file tools, and the app sees the change within a moment.

features.name: Write, place, change and check a graphic
features.summary: An agent writes a module, places a clip with explicit options, changes it, animates it and checks a timeline frame.

features.name: What can and cannot be undone in graphics
features.summary: File writes can't be undone, but placing and changing clips can; Frame Job keeps the last 10 versions of each module.

features.name: Fonts and pictures for graphics
features.summary: An agent adds a font or a picture to the project's graphics by path.

features.name: How to read the menu tables
features.summary: What the key symbols, the (key) mark, Always and "the current track" mean in the menu tables.

features.name: Frame Job menu
features.summary: About, Check for Updates…, Settings…, the Hide items and Quit, and what can stop a quit.

features.name: File menu: projects and recording
features.summary: The File menu's first groups make, open, close and save projects, and start or stop a recording.

features.name: File menu: media, captions and graphics
features.summary: The File menu's middle group brings in media, captions, fonts and pictures, and looks after the project's graphics.

features.name: File menu: export
features.summary: The File menu ends with Export… for a movie and Save Frame… for a still.

features.name: Edit menu
features.summary: Undo and redo, the clipboard, Delete and Ripple Delete, Insert and Overwrite at Playhead, and the selection commands.

features.name: Insert menu
features.summary: Adds an adjustment clip, a graphic, or a title behind the person.

features.name: Track menu
features.summary: Adds and removes tracks, and sets the current track's picture, sound, lock, solo, mix and matte.

features.name: Mark menu
features.summary: Adds and steps through markers, and sets or clears the in/out range.

features.name: View menu: zoom, snapping and panes
features.summary: Canvas zoom, Fit Timeline, Snapping, Safe Areas, the inspector, its Transcript and Assistant tabs, and track height.

features.name: View menu: preview, grade and meters
features.summary: Preview Quality, the Preview Window, and the view items that change what you see but never an export.

features.name: Window menu
features.summary: Minimize, Zoom, the Export Queue, Bring All to Front and the list of open windows.

features.name: Help menu
features.summary: Opens the bundled graphics scripting reference. Frame Job ships no help book, so this site is the help.

features.name: The Clip menu in order
features.summary: Every Clip menu item from top to bottom, with its shortcut.

features.name: Clip menu: cutting and trimming
features.summary: Split, Split at Shot Changes, the two Trim to Playhead items, Freeze Frame and Close Gap.

features.name: Clip menu: sound
features.summary: Detach and Attach Audio, Normalize, Enhance Voice, Match Audio…, Synchronize Audio and Switch by Speaker….

features.name: Clip menu: actions, automatic moves and speed
features.summary: Add Action, the commands that write moves for you, and the speed commands.

features.name: Clip menu: Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words
features.summary: Remove Silences… cuts dead air with no key. Remove Filler Words… cuts "um"s and "uh"s, usually with your AssemblyAI key.

features.name: Clip ▸ Transition ▸
features.summary: Sets the transition into the clip.

features.name: Clip ▸ Motion ▸
features.summary: Sets how the clip enters, leaves and moves, and previews it.

features.name: Clip ▸ Look ▸
features.summary: Puts a look or a LUT on the clip.

features.name: Clip ▸ Remove Background
features.summary: Keeps the person and removes the rest of the picture, or turns that off.

features.name: Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸
features.summary: Lays out the camera and the screen behind it at the playhead, eased over half a second and held until the next switch.

features.name: Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸
features.summary: Changes which camera track the selected shot comes from, keeping its span, switches and dissolves, as one undo step.

features.name: Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ and Add Blurred Background
features.summary: Puts a white rectangle, a picture or a blurred copy of a clip on a new track behind everything.

features.name: Clip ▸ Rename… and Label ▸
features.summary: Renames the selected clip in place on the timeline and gives clips a colour label.

features.name: Clip menu: nests
features.summary: Nest, Un-nest, Open Nest and Close Nest.

features.name: How the keys are shared
features.summary: Keys with no modifier belong to the editor window and stop while you type or a sheet is open. The rest are menu shortcuts.

features.name: Every shortcut on a menu item
features.summary: Every shortcut that belongs to a menu item, grouped by job.

features.name: Playback and moving the playhead
features.summary: Space, J, K, L, the arrows, Home and End play and move the playhead. None has a menu item.

features.name: Editing keys
features.summary: Keys with no modifier that nudge, trim, mark, add text, and turn on crop and region modes.

features.name: Keys in text on the canvas
features.summary: What Return and Escape do while text is edited in place on the preview.

features.name: Keys in a rename field
features.summary: Return or Tab saves a clip, track or marker name on the timeline, and ⎋ keeps the old one.

features.name: Keys in the Transcript
features.summary: With the Transcript tab's text focused, the arrows move by word and line and Delete cuts words.

features.name: Keys in the Assistant's message field
features.summary: Return sends, and Return with a modifier starts a new line.

features.name: The toolbar's timecode field
features.summary: Click the timecode, type a time and press Return to jump there.

features.name: Keys in inspector fields
features.summary: Return and Tab apply a value; Escape throws it away.

features.name: Modes that ⎋ leaves
features.summary: Escape backs out of a canvas drag, crop mode, region mode, the eyedroppers and a selected curve point.

features.name: Timeline gestures: selecting
features.summary: Click, ⇧-click and marquee selection on the timeline.

features.name: Timeline gestures: moving clips
features.summary: Drag moves clips in time and to other tracks; ⌥-drag duplicates.

features.name: Timeline gestures: trim, rate stretch, slip and roll
features.summary: Dragging a clip's edge trims it; modifiers make it a rate stretch, a roll or, on the body, a slip.

features.name: Timeline gestures: fades and the volume line
features.summary: Dragging a fade handle sets an audio fade; dragging the volume line sets the level.

features.name: Timeline gestures: action bands
features.summary: Click a band to select an action; drag it or its edges to move and resize it.

features.name: Timeline gestures: double-clicks and the nest breadcrumb
features.summary: A double-click renames a clip, opens a nest or closes a gap; the breadcrumb comes back out of a nest.

features.name: Timeline gestures: the ruler and markers
features.summary: Click or drag the ruler to scrub. Drag a marker to move it, or double-click it to rename it.

features.name: Timeline gestures: track headers
features.summary: Drag to restack, double-click to rename, and five buttons on each header.

features.name: Timeline gestures: snapping
features.summary: With snapping on, drags snap within 8 points. Hold ⌘ to turn it off for that drag.

features.name: Timeline gestures: zoom and scroll
features.summary: Pinch or ⌥ / ⌘ scroll zooms around the pointer; a plain scroll scrolls.

features.name: Dragging media in
features.summary: Drag a Media row to a track or the canvas, or files from the Finder onto the window.

features.name: Preview canvas gestures: selecting and moving
features.summary: Click selects the front-most visible clip, ⇧-click adds to the selection, and a drag moves the selected clips.

features.name: Preview canvas gestures: scale, rotate and crop
features.summary: The handles scale and rotate a clip; crop mode trims its edges.

features.name: Preview canvas gestures: endpoints, obscure regions and text
features.summary: Drag a line's ends and an obscure region's grips, and double-click text to edit it.

features.name: Preview canvas gestures: zoom and pan
features.summary: Pinch or ⌥ / ⌘ scroll steps the zoom; a scroll or Space-drag pans a canvas larger than the preview.

features.name: Color tab controls
features.summary: Hold ⌥ for fine moves on wheels, strips and curve points. Double-click a wheel or strip to reset it.

features.name: Buttons with no menu item
features.summary: Loop, the timeline zoom controls, Add Text and Add Shape have no menu item, and a few buttons match View menu items.

features.name: Add Shape
features.summary: The timeline bar's Add Shape button adds a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow. No menu bar item lets you choose one.

features.name: Where a right-click opens a menu
features.summary: Right-click or ⌃-click opens a menu on a track header or empty lane, a Media row, an inspector row and a curves channel.

features.name: Track header or empty lane
features.summary: The menu for the track you clicked, showing that track's own state.
features.where: Right-click or ⌃-click a track's header or the empty part of its lane

features.name: Media row
features.summary: The menu for one file in the Media tab; it acts on the clicked row whatever the list's selection is.
features.where: Right-click a row in the Media tab

features.name: Inspector row
features.summary: Right-click a row's label, slider, checkbox or the space beside them; the menu shows only what applies to that row.
features.where: Right-click a row in the inspector

features.name: Curves channel strip
features.summary: Right-click a channel in the Color tab's curves strip to reset that curve.
features.where: Right-click a cell of the curve editor's channel strip

features.name: Recording status item
features.summary: While a recording runs, its time shows in the macOS menu bar, and a click offers its controls.

features.name: The Settings window
features.summary: One window holds what belongs to you and not to a project, in four sections: MCP, Assistant, Transcription and Playback.

features.name: The ⓘ buttons
features.summary: The Assistant, Transcription and Playback headings each carry an ⓘ that explains the section.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ ⓘ beside a heading

features.name: Settings: MCP
features.summary: Tells an MCP client such as Claude Code how to reach Frame Job, shows the helper's path and copies the command that registers it.

features.name: Settings: Assistant
features.summary: Your Anthropic API key, the model, and two settings for long conversations.

features.name: Settings: Transcription
features.summary: Your AssemblyAI key and region, used by File ▸ Generate Captions… with AssemblyAI chosen and by Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words….

features.name: How the two key fields behave
features.summary: A saved key is never shown again; a line under the controls reports what happened to it.

features.name: Settings: Playback
features.summary: Whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time while you are idle, and how long it waits first.
features.where: Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Playback ▸ Background render

features.name: What agents can't reach in Settings
features.summary: No MCP tool reads or writes anything in Settings: keys, the model, the region and Background render are set only by a person.

features.name: View choices Frame Job remembers
features.summary: Snapping, Safe Areas, the inspector, track height and Preview Quality: the next window opens with your last choice.

features.name: Pane sizes
features.summary: Dragging a divider sizes the inspector or the timeline, and new windows open at that size.
features.where: Drag the divider above the timeline, or left of the inspector

features.name: The Preview Window's frame
features.summary: The Preview Window opens where the last one was left, on a second display for example.

features.name: What is not remembered
features.summary: Scopes, the meter and other view items start off in each window. Timeline zoom, Loop, the playhead and the in/out range reset.

features.name: Sheets that reopen on your last choice
features.summary: Some sheets reopen on what you chose last time; these are your choices, not the project's, and no agent tool reads them.

features.name: The recorder panel
features.summary: The recorder panel reopens on your last choices, apart from Record Into:.

features.name: Inspector sections
features.summary: Whether each inspector section is collapsed or expanded is remembered, per section, in every window.

features.name: Permission questions already asked
features.summary: Frame Job remembers that it has already asked macOS, because macOS will not show its prompt twice.

features.name: Convert on import
features.summary: Choosing Do this automatically from now on in the Convert / Repackage alert remembers your answer.
features.where: Import alert ▸ Do this automatically from now on

features.name: Automatic update checks
features.summary: The downloaded copy remembers your answer to whether it should check for updates automatically, and when it last checked.

features.name: Where these are kept
features.summary: All of these live in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, the com.kgalligan.FrameJob domain; keys are never stored there.

features.name: The Application Support folder
features.summary: Frame Job's own folder is ~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/.

features.name: Key files
features.summary: Your keys are the files assemblyai-key and anthropic-key in Frame Job's Application Support folder.

features.name: How keys are stored
features.summary: Each key is a plain file readable and writable only by your user account.

features.name: Keys from the environment
features.summary: If no key is stored, Frame Job falls back to an environment variable, useful when you launch it from a terminal.

features.name: The spend ledger and price table
features.summary: spend.jsonl records one line per assistant response; anthropic-prices.json is the cached price table.

features.name: Export presets
features.summary: Your named export presets are kept in ExportPresets.json.

features.name: Rewrapped copies
features.summary: Movies Frame Job converted or repackaged from files macOS could not open live in the Rewrapped folder.

features.name: The agent socket
features.summary: The local socket MCP clients connect to is created at every launch.

features.name: Recordings
features.summary: Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs go to ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/, named by date and time.

features.name: Projects
features.summary: Projects are .framejob packages wherever you save them, and hold their own caches.

features.name: Movies
features.summary: MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays, with H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG or MPEG-4 video, and VP9 and AV1 with limits.

features.name: WebM and Matroska
features.summary: .webm and .mkv with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound, copied unchanged into a QuickTime movie.

features.name: Sound
features.summary: M4A (AAC, ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF everywhere; other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, import when dropped on the Media tab.

features.name: Any sample rate
features.summary: A source that is not 48 kHz stays aligned on the timeline through a hidden 48 kHz copy.

features.name: MP3 gapless start
features.summary: An MP3's encoder delay is skipped, at any sample rate, so its sound starts on time.

features.name: Pictures
features.summary: PNG, JPEG and HEIC everywhere; TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF, WebP and AVIF import when dropped on the Media tab.

features.name: Deep and HDR stills
features.summary: A still deeper than 8 bits a component is drawn at 16-bit float, and one labelled HLG or PQ is read as HDR.

features.name: Movies with alpha
features.summary: Transparency in a movie is detected on import.

features.name: Portrait and rotated movies
features.summary: A portrait phone clip imports at its display size, not sideways.

features.name: Variable and unusual frame rates
features.summary: A rate within 0.01 fps of a standard one becomes exactly that rate, and any other keeps three decimals.

features.name: LUTs
features.summary: .cube 3D LUTs, applied as a clip's look or as a file's Camera Log.

features.name: Caption files are not media
features.summary: An .srt or a .vtt comes in through File ▸ Import Captions…, not as media.

features.name: Which way in takes which file
features.summary: The Add Media… and Open panels list fewer types than a drop on the Media tab takes.

features.name: What a package is
features.summary: A project is one .framejob package: a folder the Finder shows as one file, holding the edit, its caches and, on request, copies of the footage.

features.name: project.json
features.summary: The edit itself: canvas, media list, tracks, clips, markers, and the only thing a package needs in order to open.

features.name: cache/
features.summary: Things Frame Job can rebuild, so a package with a missing or damaged cache/ still opens and redraws.

features.name: Transcripts are worth keeping
features.summary: A transcript from AssemblyAI costs money to make again, so treat cache/transcripts/ as worth keeping.

features.name: media/
features.summary: Copies of the footage, present only after Consolidate Media….

features.name: graphics/
features.summary: Graphic modules, their fonts, images and kept versions, present only once you add a graphic, font or image.

features.name: How a package travels
features.summary: Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps its caches.

features.name: Project size
features.summary: A project holds at most 4,096 clips, 64 tracks, 1,024 markers and 1,024 media files, with nests up to 8 deep.

features.name: Canvas, layers and text
features.summary: Canvas sides are even numbers from 16 to 16,384 px, and a clip takes up to 4 filters and 4 obscure regions.

features.name: Timeline and editing
features.summary: The overlap rule, the one-frame minimum and the timeline's ranges.

features.name: Speed
features.summary: A rate is always between ×0.1 and ×1000, and a clip keeps its sound up to ×12.

features.name: Audio
features.summary: Clip volume reaches 3200 % and track volume +12 dB, and the gate, leveller and de-esser need a measured clip.

features.name: Captions and transcription
features.summary: AssemblyAI takes files up to 10 hours long and 1,000 Vocabulary terms, and caption import reads SubRip and WebVTT.

features.name: Colour
features.summary: A curve holds 2 to 16 points, and only 3D .cube LUTs of size 2 to 65 are read.

features.name: Export
features.summary: Custom sizes of 16 to 8,192 px, 600 frames for an animated GIF or PNG, and the limits on loudness, 24-bit sound and transparency.

features.name: Graphics
features.summary: A graphic draws at most 8,192 pixels on a side.

features.name: Recording
features.summary: Camera frame rates, the panel's five layouts and the menu-bar item's length. No global shortcut stops a recording.

features.name: The Assistant and agents
features.summary: The compaction threshold is 20,000 to 900,000 tokens, and a launch or get_media_analysis waits up to 60 seconds.

features.name: Settings and tools
features.summary: Background render's wait, the inspector and timeline pane sizes, and where Frame Job looks for ffmpeg.

features.name: A command is greyed out
features.summary: Every menu item has a rule for when it is on: check the selection, a nest, an open sheet and any key it needs.

features.name: A key does nothing
features.summary: Single-letter keys and the arrow keys stop working while you type in a field or a sheet is open.

features.name: The app beeps and an edit doesn't happen
features.summary: When the project's rules won't allow an edit, the app beeps, nothing changes and the rule appears at the foot of the inspector.

features.name: A project won't open
features.summary: A project that can't be read fails with a message naming the problem, and Frame Job doesn't rewrite the package.

features.name: A file won't import
features.summary: Frame Job tells you which file it couldn't add and why.

features.name: Clips show a slate
features.summary: A project always opens; clips whose file is gone keep their place, show a slate, and their media rows wear the missing badge.
features.where: Right-click a row in the Media tab ▸ Relink…

features.name: A clip is silent
features.summary: Check the clip's own sound, the track's Mute and Solo, the clip's rate and whether its sound is still rendering.

features.name: An export won't start or stops
features.summary: An export that fails says why and leaves no finished file.

features.name: A feature asks for a key
features.summary: Anything that sends your words or audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key.

features.name: Recording won't start
features.summary: A recording needs macOS's permissions, asked only when you press Record.

features.name: An agent can't reach Frame Job
features.summary: Only programs running as you can connect, through the framejob-mcp helper.

features.name: Glossary: projects and the timeline
features.summary: Words for the things you edit.

features.name: Glossary: picture and sound
features.summary: Words for what is drawn and heard.

features.name: Glossary: graphics and agents
features.summary: Words for code-drawn clips and for driving Frame Job from an agent.

features.name: Frame Job's licence
features.summary: Frame Job is released under the Apache License, Version 2.0.

features.name: Third-party notices
features.summary: Every copy of the app carries Acknowledgements.txt, listing every third-party notice it owes, each with its licence text.

features.name: What carries its own licence
features.summary: The bundled fonts, the voice-activity model, the encoders and the patched tiny-skia keep their own licences.
